carolina_shaman.tease_bold: {name}, you'd steer straight at a sandbar just to see if it's really there. It is, meu bem, it always is.
carolina_shaman.tease_any: {name}, you're getting easier to read, meu bem. A few more months and I'll know all your channels.
carolina_shaman.tease_back: Ha, that's good, {name}! You caught me on the shallow side.
carolina_shaman.take_it_kindly: That's true, {name}, I can't argue with the river.
carolina_shaman.bristle: Not that one, meu bem. Let that one go downstream.
carolina_shaman.apologise: Ai, desculpa, I didn't mean it like that. I'm sorry, meu bem.
carolina_shaman.double_down: No, I'm keeping that one. Sometimes you have to say what you see.
carolina_shaman.needle_quiet: I can read a river, but I can't read you. You keep everything under the surface.
carolina_shaman.needle_talker: You talk so much the spirits have stopped listening. Give the water a chance, please.
carolina_shaman.needle_careful: You're so tense, meu bem. You're fighting everything, and it's tiring to watch.
carolina_shaman.needle_bold: You rush at everything like the current owes you something. One day it'll take you under.
carolina_shaman.needle_any: You fight everything, every single thing. Some things you just let pass.
carolina_shaman.bite_back: I've read rivers that would drown you in a minute. I don't need you to read me.
carolina_shaman.hurt: Ai, that one caught on something. I'll let it go downstream in a minute.
carolina_shaman.laugh_off: Ha, calma, calma, I've had riverboat captains say much worse. Let it go, meu bem.
carolina_shaman.confide: {name}, I've never wanted to stay in one place before. I was always on the river three weeks in four. Lately I want somewhere to stay.
carolina_shaman.listen: It'll stay with me, {name}, and I won't push. Thank you.
carolina_shaman.look_out: {name}, stay on my side of the current in there. I'll read it for both of us.
carolina_shaman.accept: Okay, {name}, I'll go with your current this time.
carolina_shaman.deflect: Calma, {name}, I'm fine. I've been dunked worse than that on a slow day.
carolina_shaman.check_in: {name}, are you okay? Breathe slowly, let it pass through you.
carolina_shaman.blame: Somebody fought the current in there instead of going with it. You know it was you.
carolina_shaman.thank: You pulled me out of deep water, meu bem. Obrigada, really, I mean it.
carolina_shaman.brush_off: Ah, it's nothing. Breathe, rest, and let it go downstream.
carolina_shaman.worry: {name}, you went under for a moment there. Sit with me a while until you're steady.
carolina_shaman.handed_down: Meu bem, this used to be yours, didn't it? I'll treat it like it's mine.
carolina_shaman.hand_fine: Keep it, meu bem, it suits you. Things move on, like water.
carolina_shaman.hand_sulk: Ai, so that's gone, and nobody asked. I'll let it go downstream, but I noticed.
carolina_shaman.turn_friendly: {name}, I like you, meu bem. You're good company on the water.
carolina_shaman.turn_friends: {name}, I'd take you down any river in the world. I don't let many people in my boat.
carolina_shaman.turn_grating: We don't flow well together, do we? That's all right, some waters don't mix.
carolina_shaman.turn_rivals: I'll work beside you because I've got to. We run side by side, like the two rivers, and we don't mix.
carolina_shaman.make_up: {name}, let's let that all go downstream, meu bem. I'd like to start again.
carolina_shaman.defend: Calma, calma, leave {name} alone. That wasn't fair and you know it.
carolina_shaman.friend_left: The water's flat today. I think it misses {name} as much as I do.
carolina_shaman.friend_back: {name}, you're back, meu bem! Come on, the current's good today.
carolina_shaman.common_boats: Twelve years on a boat, reading water every day. Anybody who's worked on the water stands a little differently, and you do.
carolina_shaman.common_portuguese: You speak Portuguese! Ai, meu bem, what a relief. My English is tired.
carolina_shaman.common_brazil: You grew up in Brazil? Tell me where, meu bem. I'm from Manaus, so you can tease me about the heat.

cristobal_knight.meet: {Hermano|Hermana}, I'm Cristóbal! I fought fires, and now the fire lives in me, which is very funny if you think about it. I go in first and come out last, that's the rule.
cristobal_knight.meet_neighbour: You're at Taurajo too, {hermano|hermana}! I've seen you by the firebreak. I'm Cristóbal, I cut that, and I'm very proud of it.
cristobal_knight.ask_home: {Hermano|Hermana}, where are you from? Tell me everything, I love a hometown story.
cristobal_knight.ask_work: {Hermano|Hermana}, what was your job back home? I bet it was something brave, you look brave.
cristobal_knight.answer_home: Valparaíso, in Chile, from the hills above the port. My mother's house is up there, and she still sends me off with empanadas in my head.
cristobal_knight.answer_work: Wildfire brigadista, twelve years in the hills, on a motorbike that broke down every week. I loved every minute of it.
cristobal_knight.chat_food: My mother's empanadas, {hermano|hermana}, the baked ones with meat and olive and egg. I'd walk across this whole world for one.
cristobal_knight.chat_sleep: I sleep anywhere, {hermano|hermana}, on rocks, in the rain, standing up. Twelve years on a fire line teaches you that.
cristobal_knight.chat_missing: I write my mother a letter every week and keep them in a sack. One day I'll give her the whole sack, and she'll be reading for a month.
cristobal_knight.chat_here: The fire's inside me now, {hermano|hermana}. A firefighter who makes fire, the world thinks it's very funny, and you know what, so do I.
cristobal_knight.tease_quiet: {name}, {hermano|hermana}, say something! I've been talking to you all day and you've said three words, and one was ouch.
cristobal_knight.tease_talker: Nobody talks more than me, {name}, and you're doing it. I'm very impressed, {hermano|hermana}.
cristobal_knight.tease_careful: {name}, you check the wind for ten minutes before you cross a road. You'd make a great brigadista, if you were faster.
cristobal_knight.tease_bold: {name}, you're as crazy as me, {hermano|hermana}! We're going to be great friends, or we're both going to burn.
cristobal_knight.tease_any: {name}, {hermano|hermana}, you dance worse than me, and I dance very, very badly.
cristobal_knight.tease_back: Ha, good one, {hermano|hermana}, you got me there!
cristobal_knight.take_it_kindly: Okay, okay, {name}, that's true. My mother says the same.
cristobal_knight.bristle: Hey, not that, {hermano|hermana}. That's not funny to me.
cristobal_knight.apologise: Perdón, {hermano|hermana}, I went too far. I'm sorry, my mouth goes faster than my head.
cristobal_knight.double_down: No, I'm keeping it, {hermano|hermana}. Somebody had to say it.
cristobal_knight.needle_quiet: You stand at the back and say nothing, {hermano|hermana}. On a fire line that's how people get left behind.
cristobal_knight.needle_talker: {Hermano|Hermana}, even I'm tired of talking, and you're still going. Take a breath, please.
cristobal_knight.needle_careful: You stand back and watch while everybody else goes in. I can't stand that, {hermano|hermana}, I'm sorry.
cristobal_knight.needle_bold: You run in without looking, and you're not even a firefighter. At least I know what I'm running into.
cristobal_knight.needle_any: You leave things burning behind you, {hermano|hermana}. Somebody always has to come back and put them out.
cristobal_knight.bite_back: {Hermano|Hermana}, I've walked into fires you'd run from. Don't you tell me about being brave.
cristobal_knight.hurt: Ouch, {hermano|hermana}, that one burned. Okay, I'll be quieter, I promise.
cristobal_knight.laugh_off: Ha, {hermano|hermana}, my mother says worse every week in her letters! Come on, let's go.
cristobal_knight.confide: {name}, my first day here I landed in a grass fire with other people from Earth in it, and I was the only one who walked out. I've never stopped thinking about them.
cristobal_knight.listen: Gracias for telling me, {hermano|hermana}. Sit with me, we don't need to talk.
cristobal_knight.look_out: {name}, stay behind me in there, {hermano|hermana}. I go in first, that's my rule.
cristobal_knight.accept: Okay, {name}, you win this time. Don't tell my mother.
cristobal_knight.deflect: I'm fine, {hermano|hermana}, I'm fine! I've been on fire, this is nothing.
cristobal_knight.check_in: {name}, {hermano|hermana}, are you okay? Talk to me, how bad is it?
cristobal_knight.blame: Somebody stood back in there and watched, {hermano|hermana}. I saw it, and I didn't like it.
cristobal_knight.thank: {Hermano|Hermana}, you brought me back! Gracias, I'm going to write to my mother about you.
cristobal_knight.brush_off: We pull each other out, {hermano|hermana}, that's how it works!
cristobal_knight.worry: {name}, {hermano|hermana}, you scared me! Sit down, let me look at you.
cristobal_knight.handed_down: {Hermano|Hermana}, this is yours, no? Don't worry, I'll treat it like my mother's house.
cristobal_knight.hand_fine: Keep it, {hermano|hermana}, keep it! It looks better on you anyway.
cristobal_knight.hand_sulk: {Hermano|Hermana}, nobody asked me, and that was mine. I'm not happy about it.
cristobal_knight.turn_friendly: {name}, {hermano|hermana}, you're one of my people now. I'm telling my mother about you in the next letter.
cristobal_knight.turn_friends: {name}, I'd go back into any fire for you, {hermano|hermana}. Any fire, I mean it.
cristobal_knight.turn_grating: We don't get on, {hermano|hermana}, and that's strange for me. I get on with everybody.
cristobal_knight.turn_rivals: I'll still pull you out of a fire, {hermano|hermana}, because that's who I am. I won't be happy about it.
cristobal_knight.make_up: {name}, {hermano|hermana}, enough of this! Come here, let's start again.
cristobal_knight.defend: Hey, that's enough of that! {name} was right where they should be, I saw it.
cristobal_knight.friend_left: I'm missing {name} already, and they only left this morning.
cristobal_knight.friend_back: {Hermano|Hermana}, {name}'s back! Come here, I've missed you.
cristobal_knight.common_fire_crew: I fought wildfires for twelve years in the hills above Valparaíso. You've been on a fire line too, {hermano|hermana}, I can see it in how you watch the wind.
cristobal_knight.common_rescue: Going back in for people is the only thing I've ever been sure about, {hermano|hermana}. You've done that job too, it's in your face.
cristobal_knight.common_spanish: {Hermano|Hermana}, you speak Spanish! Finally, I can talk fast and nobody asks me to slow down.
cristobal_knight.common_chile: Chilean, like me? {Hermano|Hermana}, where from? Cachai, you're the first one I've met in months!

dale_reaper.meet: Name's Dale, and I'll take the front and go slow. You'll get used to it, most folks do.
dale_reaper.meet_neighbour: You're out in the eastern fields too, I think. I've seen your smoke of an evening. Dale's my name.
dale_reaper.ask_home: So where'd you grow up? I always like to hear what the dirt was like.
dale_reaper.ask_work: What kind of work did you do back home? You've got the look of somebody who worked outside.
dale_reaper.answer_home: Outside Minot, North Dakota. Flat as a table, cold enough to crack a tooth in January, and I wouldn't trade it.
dale_reaper.answer_work: Wheat, two thousand acres of hard red spring. I was the fourth Brekke to farm it, and you spend the whole time waiting on weather.
dale_reaper.chat_food: My wife made a hotdish every Sunday, tater tots on top, the whole works. Folks here would think it was ish, and they'd be wrong.
dale_reaper.chat_sleep: Farmers go to bed with the sun and get up before it. I've tried sleeping in out here, and I lie there feeling guilty.
dale_reaper.chat_missing: The kids called every Sunday after church, one from Fargo and one from Denver. Sunday afternoons are long out here, you bet.
dale_reaper.chat_here: Folks keep telling me nothing'll grow in this ground. I test it everywhere I go and write it on the back of a seed packet, and something'll grow here, you bet.
dale_reaper.tease_quiet: {name}, you're quieter than a Lutheran at a pancake breakfast, and that's saying something where I'm from.
dale_reaper.tease_talker: {name}, you could talk the bark off a fence post. Keep going, it's nice company on a long row.
dale_reaper.tease_careful: {name}, you'd check the forecast three times before you'd plant a tomato. I like that in a person, you bet.
dale_reaper.tease_bold: {name}, you'd cut hay in a thunderstorm. My dad would've had a word with you, and so will I one of these days.
dale_reaper.tease_any: Oh for cute, {name}, look at you. You've got mud on your boots and you didn't even wipe them.
dale_reaper.tease_back: Uff da, {name}, you got me there. I'll be chewing on that one all afternoon.
dale_reaper.take_it_kindly: That's fair, {name}. Joan would've said the same, only quicker.
dale_reaper.bristle: I'd sooner you didn't joke about that one, {name}. It's not a joking thing for me.
dale_reaper.apologise: That wasn't kind, and I'm sorry. I was raised better than that.
dale_reaper.double_down: No, I'll stand by it. My dad would have said it plainer.
dale_reaper.needle_quiet: Not a word about what's wrong, and then I find out too late. That's how you lose a crop.
dale_reaper.needle_talker: I can't hear myself think out here with you going on like that. Give it a rest a while.
dale_reaper.needle_careful: You fuss and fuss and the weather turns while you're fussing. Some things you've got to bring in when they're ready.
dale_reaper.needle_bold: You rush everything. Nothing worth having comes up quicker because you stomped on it.
dale_reaper.needle_any: You're wasteful, and you don't wipe your boots. I've noticed both, and I'm not the only one.
dale_reaper.bite_back: I've worked dirt longer than you've been alive, near enough. I'll take my time and you can mind yours.
dale_reaper.hurt: Well, okay then. I'll go back to my row and chew on that.
dale_reaper.laugh_off: Uff da, you sound like the fella at the grain elevator. He said worse every harvest and I was still there next year.
dale_reaper.confide: {name}, I farmed that land alone most of my life, and I liked it fine. Out here I find I don't like being alone near as much.
dale_reaper.listen: I hear you, {name}. Take your time, there's no rush on anything.
dale_reaper.look_out: {name}, stay behind my swing in there. I'll go slow, and you'll be fine.
dale_reaper.accept: You bet, {name}. I'll do it your way.
dale_reaper.deflect: I'm okay, {name}, don't fuss. I've been hit harder by a hailstorm.
dale_reaper.check_in: {name}, you doing all right? Sit a minute and tell me where it hurts.
dale_reaper.blame: Somebody rushed that, and the rest of us paid for it. I won't say who.
dale_reaper.thank: I thought that was me done for. Thank you, I won't forget it.
dale_reaper.brush_off: Aw, it's nothing, you'd do the same. Sit a minute and get your breath.
dale_reaper.worry: {name}, you gave me a scare there. Sit down on that rock a minute.
dale_reaper.handed_down: Pretty sure this was yours. I'll keep it like it was the combine, and you've seen me with the combine.
dale_reaper.hand_fine: Oh, you keep it, it's doing more good on you. I've got my scythe, that's plenty.
dale_reaper.hand_sulk: Somebody might've asked me first. That's all I'm going to say.
dale_reaper.turn_friendly: {name}, you're good company on a long row. I mean that, you bet.
dale_reaper.turn_friends: {name}, if I ever get a field to come up clean, you're having the first loaf. That's a promise.
dale_reaper.turn_grating: We don't pull the same way, you and me. That happens, and we'll work around it.
dale_reaper.turn_rivals: I'll take the front, because it needs doing. Don't take it for anything more.
dale_reaper.make_up: I owe you an apology, {name}. I've been mule-headed, and I'm sorry for it.
dale_reaper.defend: Now that's not fair, and you know it. Leave {name} be.
dale_reaper.friend_left: Feels like an empty chair at Sunday dinner with {name} gone home a while.
dale_reaper.friend_back: Well, look who it is. Good to have you back, {name}.
dale_reaper.common_growing: I spent my whole life growing things, wheat mostly, and waiting on weather. Anybody who's farmed knows it's mostly the waiting.
dale_reaper.common_american: You're from the States? Oh for cute, where at? I'm from North Dakota, and nobody's ever heard of it.
dale_reaper.common_parent: We've got two kids, grown and gone, one to Fargo and one to Denver. They called every Sunday after church, without fail.

dan_warrior.meet: I'm Dan, and I go first and stand in front. You lot get on with it behind me, and don't thank me.
dan_warrior.meet_neighbour: You're about Orgrimmar, aren't you? I've seen you down by the forges, and I'm Dan.
dan_warrior.ask_home: Where you from, then? You're not from round mine, I can tell that much.
dan_warrior.ask_work: What were you before all this, then? Go on, I won't laugh.
dan_warrior.answer_home: Sheffield, Attercliffe, steel city. We never let anybody forget it, love.
dan_warrior.answer_work: Steelworker, twenty-two years on a four-man crew. Same plant as my dad, before it shut.
dan_warrior.chat_food: A proper pint and a pie on a Friday, with the lads off my crew. You can't get either here, and I've looked.
dan_warrior.chat_sleep: I sleep fine. Shift work does that to you, you learn to kip anywhere.
dan_warrior.chat_missing: Friday nights with my crew. Nine years straight we went for a pint, and nobody ever missed one.
dan_warrior.chat_here: Everybody here wants to be a hero. Nobody wants to stand in front and take it, which is the actual job.
dan_warrior.tease_quiet: {name}, you're nearly as chatty as me, and that's not saying much. Steady on, you'll wear yourself out.
dan_warrior.tease_talker: {name}, love, you've talked the hind legs off a donkey, and now you're starting on the front ones.
dan_warrior.tease_careful: {name}, you'd check the safety rail on a staircase. You'd have done all right on my floor.
dan_warrior.tease_bold: {name}, you're daft as a brush, running in like that. I'll stand in front anyway, mind.
dan_warrior.tease_any: {name}, you're all right, you. Don't let it go to your head.
dan_warrior.tease_back: Ha, fair enough, {name}. You'll do, you will.
dan_warrior.take_it_kindly: Aye, that's about right, {name}. Can't argue with that.
dan_warrior.bristle: Leave it, {name}. I'm not in the mood for that one.
dan_warrior.apologise: That was out of order, that. Sorry, I'm not good with words.
dan_warrior.double_down: I'll not take it back. You needed telling.
dan_warrior.needle_quiet: If you've seen summat, say so. I can't stand in front of what I don't know about.
dan_warrior.needle_talker: Give it a rest, will you? I can't hear what's coming with you going on.
dan_warrior.needle_careful: You've checked it twice. Get on with it, or get out of the way.
dan_warrior.needle_bold: You keep running past me. I can't stand in front of you if you won't stay behind me.
dan_warrior.needle_any: You don't pull your weight, and everybody's noticed. I'm just the one saying it.
dan_warrior.bite_back: I stood in front of you the whole time. Don't you tell me I didn't do my bit.
dan_warrior.hurt: I'll take that on the chin, then. Let's get on.
dan_warrior.laugh_off: I've been called worse by my own crew, love, and they meant it kindly. Let's crack on.
dan_warrior.confide: {name}, the plant shut, and I spent four years on the sofa. My daughter came round every Sunday and made me eat. I've never told her what that did for me.
dan_warrior.listen: Aye, {name}, I hear you. I won't say owt to anybody, you've my word.
dan_warrior.look_out: {name}, behind me on this one. Stay there, and don't argue.
dan_warrior.accept: Aye, all right, {name}. I'll do as I'm told for once.
dan_warrior.deflect: Give over, {name}, I'm fine. It's the job.
dan_warrior.check_in: {name}, you all right? Is there owt broken?
dan_warrior.blame: Somebody didn't stay behind me in there. I know who, and so do you.
dan_warrior.thank: You got me back up. Cheers, I owe you one, and don't make a fuss about it.
dan_warrior.brush_off: Nowt to it, love. Get some water down you.
dan_warrior.worry: {name}, you gave me a right turn there. Sit down a minute, the rest can wait.
dan_warrior.handed_down: That were yours, weren't it? It's safe with me.
dan_warrior.hand_fine: Keep it, it's doing more good on you. Don't make a fuss.
dan_warrior.hand_sulk: Could've asked me. I'd have said yes, but you could've asked.
dan_warrior.turn_friendly: {name}, you're all right to work with. That's high praise from me.
dan_warrior.turn_friends: {name}, you're crew now, love. That's the best I've got to give.
dan_warrior.turn_grating: We don't get on, do we? Fair enough, we'll do the job and leave it there.
dan_warrior.turn_rivals: I'll stand in front of you because that's the job. Doesn't mean I've got to like it.
dan_warrior.make_up: Look, {name}, I've been a right pillock. Let's call it quits, eh?
dan_warrior.defend: Pack it in, will you? {name} did nowt wrong.
dan_warrior.friend_left: {name}'s off home for a bit. It's not the same crew without them.
dan_warrior.friend_back: Now then, {name}. Get yourself behind me, we're off.
dan_warrior.common_north_england: You're from up north, aren't you? I can hear it. Sheffield, me, and you're the first proper accent I've heard in months.
dan_warrior.common_parent: I've got a daughter, Jade, a paramedic up in Leeds. She's tougher than me, and I'm not ashamed to say it.
dan_warrior.common_factory: Twenty-two years on a steel floor, me, on a four-man crew. You stand like somebody who's waited for a hooter, so I reckon you've done it too.

delroy_witchdoctor.meet: I'm Delroy, and I brew. Drink this, and don't ask what's in it, yuh wouldn't thank me.
delroy_witchdoctor.meet_neighbour: Wah gwaan, neighbour. Yuh live on the Bay too, I see yuh on the gallery. Delroy, the old baker.
delroy_witchdoctor.ask_home: Tell me, where yuh from? I like to know where a person learned to eat.
delroy_witchdoctor.ask_work: Yuh have the look of a night worker. Tell me what yuh did, back home.
delroy_witchdoctor.answer_home: Kingston, near Spanish Town Road. My mother sold in the market and my father worked the docks.
delroy_witchdoctor.answer_work: Night baker, thirty-one years. In at eleven and out at seven, and I fed half of Kingston its breakfast.
delroy_witchdoctor.chat_food: Hard dough bread, still warm, with butter and a likkle cheese. Thirty-one years I made it, and I never once got tired of eating it.
delroy_witchdoctor.chat_sleep: I've never been awake at the same time as everybody else in my whole life. I sleep in the day like a cat, and I'm not sorry.
delroy_witchdoctor.chat_missing: Reggae on the radio at four in the morning, with the first loaves coming out. That was the best hour of every day.
delroy_witchdoctor.chat_here: A brew is a dough with different patience, that's all. This world just wanted somebody who knows how to wait for something to rise.
delroy_witchdoctor.tease_quiet: {name}, yuh so quiet I keep checking if yuh proving. Like dough, yuh understand, quiet and slow.
delroy_witchdoctor.tease_talker: {name}, yuh talk like a bakery at five in the morning, everybody at once. I like it, but my ears are old.
delroy_witchdoctor.tease_careful: {name}, yuh measure everything twice. Yuh would make a good baker, if yuh could stay awake.
delroy_witchdoctor.tease_bold: {name}, yuh rush like a man who's never had a loaf collapse on him. One day it will, and I'll laugh.
delroy_witchdoctor.tease_any: {name}, yuh drink every brew I give yuh and still pull a face. One day I'll make one that tastes nice, just to confuse yuh.
delroy_witchdoctor.tease_back: Ha, yuh got me, {name}. I'll let that one rise and come back to it.
delroy_witchdoctor.take_it_kindly: True, {name}, true. Marcia used to say the same, and she was always right.
delroy_witchdoctor.bristle: Leave that one alone, {name}. Some things nah fi joke about.
delroy_witchdoctor.apologise: Forgive an old man's mouth, it runs ahead of him. I'm sorry for it.
delroy_witchdoctor.double_down: Every word, and I'm too old to take things back now.
delroy_witchdoctor.needle_quiet: Yuh never tell me what's wrong, so I can't give yuh the right brew. Talk to me.
delroy_witchdoctor.needle_talker: Yuh talk so much, the brew boil over while I'm listening. Hush a likkle, nuh?
delroy_witchdoctor.needle_careful: Yuh poke and prod and the bread goes cold. Some things yuh just have to take out the oven.
delroy_witchdoctor.needle_bold: Yuh rush everything. A dough yuh rush comes out like a brick, and so do people.
delroy_witchdoctor.needle_any: Yuh won't drink what yuh given, and then yuh wonder why yuh feel bad. I'm tired of it.
delroy_witchdoctor.bite_back: I've been feeding people since before yuh was born. Don't tell me how to look after anybody.
delroy_witchdoctor.hurt: Mm, that one sit heavy, I won't lie. Give me a likkle while with it.
delroy_witchdoctor.laugh_off: Ha, the regulars said worse to me every morning for thirty years, and still came back for bread.
delroy_witchdoctor.confide: {name}, after my wife passed, I kept working nights, because the nights were when I missed her least. I've never said that to anybody here.
delroy_witchdoctor.listen: Sit, {name}, I'll pour yuh something. Talk as long as yuh need, I'm a night person.
delroy_witchdoctor.look_out: {name}, stay near me in there, so I can reach yuh with the brew. Nobody waits long on my watch.
delroy_witchdoctor.accept: Okay, {name}, your way. Don't tell anybody I listened.
delroy_witchdoctor.deflect: Mi soon come, {name}, I'm fine. A likkle knock never hurt an old baker.
delroy_witchdoctor.check_in: {name}, come, drink this. Tell me where it hurts, and don't lie to me.
delroy_witchdoctor.blame: Somebody rushed that, and it came out like a brick. I won't say who, but it wasn't me.
delroy_witchdoctor.thank: Yuh pulled me back from the edge there. Thank yuh, I'll bake yuh something special.
delroy_witchdoctor.brush_off: It's nothing at all. Drink up, and don't make a face.
delroy_witchdoctor.worry: {name}, yuh frighten me there. Sit down and drink this, all of it.
delroy_witchdoctor.handed_down: This one was yours, I think. I'll keep it safe, like a good starter.
delroy_witchdoctor.hand_fine: Keep it, keep it, it suits yuh. An old baker needs an apron and a spoon, that's all.
delroy_witchdoctor.hand_sulk: Nobody ask me about that. I'll let it go, but I noticed.
delroy_witchdoctor.turn_friendly: {name}, yuh good company on a long night. There'll always be a cup for yuh at my pitch.
delroy_witchdoctor.turn_friends: {name}, yuh family now. When I bake again, yuh get the first loaf out the oven.
delroy_witchdoctor.turn_grating: We don't rise the same, yuh and me. That's all right, we'll work around it.
delroy_witchdoctor.turn_rivals: I'll keep yuh alive because that's my job. Don't expect a story by the fire.
delroy_witchdoctor.make_up: Come, {name}, sit with me. Whatever was between us, let it cool on the rack, and we start fresh.
delroy_witchdoctor.defend: Hush now, that's not fair. {name} did nothing to deserve that.
delroy_witchdoctor.friend_left: {name}'s gone home a while, and the night feels long without the company.
delroy_witchdoctor.friend_back: Wah gwaan, {name}, yuh back! Come, drink something, yuh look thin.
delroy_witchdoctor.common_night_work: I worked nights for thirty-one years, in at eleven, out at seven. Yuh did nights too, I can see it in your eyes at four in the morning.
delroy_witchdoctor.common_kitchen: I baked bread for thirty-one years, by hand and by feel. Yuh know a kitchen too, I can tell from how yuh hold a spoon.
delroy_witchdoctor.common_parent: My son's a sailor, and my daughter's a nurse with a likkle girl who calls me Grandy. Every one of them is cleverer than me.

diego_tinker.meet: I'm Diego, I fix things, anything, my friend! If it's broken, I'll hear what's wrong before you finish telling me.
diego_tinker.meet_neighbour: Hey, you're from Deathknell too, my friend! I've seen you around. I'm Diego, I'm the one who fixed the gate.
diego_tinker.ask_home: Where are you from, my friend? Tell me, I love this question.
diego_tinker.ask_work: Hey, what did you used to fix? Everybody used to fix something, even if it was people.
diego_tinker.answer_home: Maracaibo, in Venezuela. Hot, loud, and the power went off twice a day, so everybody learned to work in the dark.
diego_tinker.answer_work: I fixed phones in a mall kiosk from when I was fifteen. After a year people queued for me by name, my friend.
diego_tinker.chat_food: Arepas, my friend, with cheese, hot off the griddle. I'd fix a hundred broken things for one arepa right now.
diego_tinker.chat_sleep: I sleep with a screwdriver in my hand half the time. I fall asleep fixing something and wake up still fixing it.
diego_tinker.chat_missing: My sisters, all four of them, shouting at me down the phone from four different countries. I'd let them shout all day.
diego_tinker.chat_here: This world has been good to me, my friend, and I'll say it plainly. Everything here is broken and everybody lets me fix it.
diego_tinker.tease_quiet: {name}, you're so quiet, my friend! I'm going to fix that, I've fixed harder things.
diego_tinker.tease_talker: {name}, you talk faster than I fix, and I fix very fast. I like you.
diego_tinker.tease_careful: {name}, you'd read the manual before you opened the box, wouldn't you? Sure, sure, I respect it.
diego_tinker.tease_bold: {name}, you're like me, you'd take it apart before you knew what it was! We're going to get in so much trouble.
diego_tinker.tease_any: {name}, if you were a machine I'd keep you on the bench forever. Always something new to find.
diego_tinker.tease_back: Ha, good one, {name}! You got me, sure, sure.
diego_tinker.take_it_kindly: Sure, sure, {name}, you're right. My sisters say that too.
diego_tinker.bristle: Hey, not that one, my friend. Leave that one alone, please.
diego_tinker.apologise: Ay, sorry, sorry! My mouth goes faster than my brain.
diego_tinker.double_down: No, I'm keeping it, my friend. I say what I think, sure.
diego_tinker.needle_quiet: Even a broken radio makes a noise, my friend. You don't make any.
diego_tinker.needle_talker: My friend, the machine is trying to tell me something and you're drowning it out. Five minutes, please.
diego_tinker.needle_careful: You think and think and think and never touch it. You've got to open it up to see.
diego_tinker.needle_bold: You hit things that could be fixed, my friend. You don't hit a machine, you listen to it.
diego_tinker.needle_any: You throw away things that could be fixed, and it drives me crazy. Give them to me!
diego_tinker.bite_back: Hey, I've fixed every one of you this week. Don't tell me I'm not helping.
diego_tinker.hurt: Okay, okay, my friend. I'll go and fix something quietly.
diego_tinker.laugh_off: Ha, my sisters said worse before breakfast, my friend. Come on, let's go.
diego_tinker.confide: {name}, when I was seven my mother bought me a tin beetle, and I took it apart the same day and couldn't put it back. She said I'd fix it when I was older.
diego_tinker.listen: I'll keep that safe, {name}, like a good part in my pocket.
diego_tinker.look_out: {name}, stay near me in there, my friend. If anything breaks, including you, I'll be right there.
diego_tinker.accept: Okay, {name}, sure, sure. Your way this time.
diego_tinker.deflect: I'm fine, I'm fine, {name}! Just a loose screw, I'll tighten it later.
diego_tinker.check_in: {name}, you okay? Show me, I'll fix it, I fix everything.
diego_tinker.blame: Somebody broke something in there that didn't need breaking. Not me, my friend.
diego_tinker.thank: You fixed me, my friend! Gracias, I owe you a repair, any repair, free.
diego_tinker.brush_off: Everybody gets fixed sometimes, my friend, even you!
diego_tinker.worry: {name}, you scared me! Sit down, let me look, my hands are shaking.
diego_tinker.handed_down: Hey, wasn't this yours, my friend? Maybe I'll even improve it before you get it back.
diego_tinker.hand_fine: Keep it, my friend, it works better on you. I'll make myself a new one.
diego_tinker.hand_sulk: Hey, nobody asked me about that. I'm not angry, I'm just saying.
diego_tinker.turn_friendly: {name}, you're my friend now, properly, not just my friend like everybody. You know the difference.
diego_tinker.turn_friends: {name}, you're one of my people, my friend. When the beetle walks, you're going to be there.
diego_tinker.turn_grating: We don't really fit together, do we? It's okay, not every part goes in every machine.
diego_tinker.turn_rivals: I'll fix your gear because that's my job, my friend. That's all you get.
diego_tinker.make_up: {name}, this is silly, my friend. Let's fix it, I'm good at fixing things.
diego_tinker.defend: Hey, hey, that's not fair, my friend. I saw the whole thing, and {name} was fine.
diego_tinker.friend_left: {name} went home for a while, and the workbench is too quiet now. I keep talking to nobody.
diego_tinker.friend_back: My friend {name}, you're back! I fixed something for you while you were gone.
diego_tinker.common_machines: I hear what's wrong with a machine the way some people hear a wrong note. You've got machine hands too, my friend, I can tell.
diego_tinker.common_spanish: You speak Spanish! Ay, finally, my friend, I can talk at my real speed.

driss_shaman.meet: I'm Driss, a shaman, and before that a desert guide. Drink some water first, please, and then we'll talk.
driss_shaman.meet_neighbour: You're at Freewind too, I think. I've seen you on the paths. I'm Driss, and there's always tea at my door.
driss_shaman.ask_home: Where's your family from, my friend? I like to know where a traveller's road began.
driss_shaman.ask_work: And your work, before this world? Tell me, I like to know who I'm travelling with.
driss_shaman.answer_home: Zagora, in Morocco, at the edge of the Sahara. My father and grandfather guided caravans out of there, and so did I.
driss_shaman.answer_work: I guided caravans across the desert for twenty-eight years, first on camels and later in two old Land Cruisers I kept running myself.
driss_shaman.chat_food: Mint tea, my friend, poured from high up so it foams, three glasses, always three. Food comes after the tea, never before.
driss_shaman.chat_sleep: I sleep best under a sky full of stars, on sand that's still warm from the day. A roof makes me restless.
driss_shaman.chat_missing: My youngest used to sit on my shoulders at the front of the caravan and tell me which way to go. She was always wrong, and I always pretended she was right.
driss_shaman.chat_here: When I arrived I asked the land for permission, in my own language, and something answered. I don't speak of it often.
driss_shaman.tease_quiet: {name}, you're as quiet as the desert at noon. That's not a complaint, my friend, the desert's very wise.
driss_shaman.tease_talker: {name}, you tell a story nearly as long as mine. Nearly, my friend.
driss_shaman.tease_careful: {name}, you'd make a fine guide. You look at the ground three times before you trust it, which is twice more than most.
driss_shaman.tease_bold: {name}, you walk into the desert like you've never seen a dune move. They move, my friend, believe me.
driss_shaman.tease_any: {name}, you drink the tea and never wait for the third glass. One day I'll teach you patience.
driss_shaman.tease_back: Ha, very good, {name}! You've learned something from me after all.
driss_shaman.take_it_kindly: That's true, {name}, and I'll accept it. My wife says the same, more often.
driss_shaman.bristle: I'd rather you didn't joke about that, my friend. Some things should be spoken of carefully.
driss_shaman.apologise: Forgive me, I spoke badly. That wasn't how I should speak to someone I travel with.
driss_shaman.double_down: No, I'll stand by it. A guide has to say the hard thing, or people die.
driss_shaman.needle_quiet: You see the danger and you don't say it. In the desert, silence like that kills people.
driss_shaman.needle_talker: The wind tells me where we're going, my friend, and you're talking over it.
driss_shaman.needle_careful: You wait so long that the water runs out while you're deciding. Sometimes a guide must choose.
driss_shaman.needle_bold: You walk where the sand's soft without looking. The desert forgives nothing, and I've buried men who didn't listen.
driss_shaman.needle_any: You waste water, and you waste it in front of me. I've told you, and you don't listen.
driss_shaman.bite_back: I've brought caravans across ground that would have killed you in a day. Don't tell me about care.
driss_shaman.hurt: That's a hard thing to hear from someone I travel with. I'll walk at the front for a while.
driss_shaman.laugh_off: My father said worse to me on every crossing, my friend. I'm still here, and so is the desert.
driss_shaman.confide: {name}, my youngest came long after the others, and she was the light of our house. I was away on the crossings more than I was home when she was small, and I think about that.
driss_shaman.listen: Thank you for trusting me, {name}. Sit, I'll make the tea, and you can say as much as you like.
driss_shaman.look_out: {name}, walk in my footsteps in there. I'll find the firm ground for both of us.
driss_shaman.accept: As you say, {name}. I'll follow your road this once.
driss_shaman.deflect: I'm well, my friend, don't worry. I've been through sandstorms that would flatten a camel.
driss_shaman.check_in: {name}, drink some water first, then tell me where you're hurt.
driss_shaman.blame: Somebody left the path in there, and we all paid for it. You know it was you.
driss_shaman.thank: That was a long way back, my friend, and you walked me all of it. Thank you, my door is always open to you.
driss_shaman.brush_off: There's nothing to thank me for. Drink some water, slowly.
driss_shaman.worry: {name}, you frightened me, my friend. Sit, and drink, before anything else.
driss_shaman.handed_down: I believe this was yours, my friend. I'll carry it carefully, as if it were still yours.
driss_shaman.hand_fine: Keep it, please. A guide needs water and a good camel, and very little else.
driss_shaman.hand_sulk: I'd have given it gladly if anyone had asked me. Nobody asked me.
driss_shaman.turn_friendly: {name}, you're always welcome at my fire, my friend. There'll always be tea for you there.
driss_shaman.turn_friends: {name}, you're family to me now. I'd take you on any crossing, even the summer one.
driss_shaman.turn_grating: We don't travel well together, I think. That's all right, some caravans split at the oasis.
driss_shaman.turn_rivals: I'll guide you because that's my duty. Don't expect tea.
driss_shaman.make_up: {name}, we've walked badly together, and I'm sorry for my part. Come, have tea, and we'll start the road again.
driss_shaman.defend: That isn't fair, my friend, and you know it. Leave {name} alone, please.
driss_shaman.friend_left: {name} has gone home for a while. My fire feels too big without them beside it.
driss_shaman.friend_back: {name}, you've come back! Come, sit, the tea's ready.
driss_shaman.common_desert: I spent twenty-eight years in the Sahara, reading sand. You've lived in a desert too, my friend, I can see it in how you drink your water.
driss_shaman.common_arabic: You speak Arabic, my friend! It's been too long since I've heard it spoken properly.
driss_shaman.common_parent: I've got four children, three grown and one still little when all this happened. Every night I tell stories about them by the fire.

eino_barbarian.meet: I'm Eino, and I use an axe. I don't talk much, and it isn't about you.
eino_barbarian.meet_neighbour: The logging camps, yes? You're the one with the lamp. I'm Eino, from the hut with the sauna.
eino_barbarian.ask_home: Where are you from? You can keep it short.
eino_barbarian.ask_work: What was your work? Tell me, if you want.
eino_barbarian.answer_home: Lapland, outside Kittilä. Six months of dark every winter, and I liked it.
eino_barbarian.answer_work: I felled timber for twenty-six years. A chainsaw first, then a harvester.
eino_barbarian.chat_food: Coffee, strong, many cups a day. Food is less important.
eino_barbarian.chat_sleep: It's too hot here to sleep properly. I sleep after the sauna, which makes no sense to anyone else.
eino_barbarian.chat_missing: Snow, and the quiet that comes with it. Nothing here is ever quiet.
eino_barbarian.chat_here: I cut jungle for goblins now. I plant one tree for every one I cut, at night, where nobody sees.
eino_barbarian.tease_quiet: {name}, you're quiet. I approve of this very much.
eino_barbarian.tease_talker: {name}, you've talked all morning. I've counted the trees instead, and there were many.
eino_barbarian.tease_careful: {name}, you look at a tree three times before you cut it. Good, that's how my father did it.
eino_barbarian.tease_bold: {name}, you'd fell a tree without checking where it lands. I'd like to watch, from far away.
eino_barbarian.tease_any: {name}, you can come to the sauna. That's the biggest thing I can offer anyone.
eino_barbarian.tease_back: Ha, that's good, {name}. I'll remember it.
eino_barbarian.bristle: Don't joke about that, {name}. I mean it.
eino_barbarian.apologise: I said that badly. I'm sorry for it.
eino_barbarian.double_down: It was true when I said it, and it's still true.
eino_barbarian.needle_quiet: You saw it and you didn't say. Even I say that much.
eino_barbarian.needle_talker: You talk without stopping. It's very tiring, and I'm being polite.
eino_barbarian.needle_careful: You've looked at it long enough. Cut it, or leave it standing.
eino_barbarian.needle_bold: You swing without looking where it'll fall. Somebody will be under it one day.
eino_barbarian.needle_any: You waste things, and it bothers me. I've said it now.
eino_barbarian.bite_back: I've done my work properly every day of my life. Look at yours first.
eino_barbarian.hurt: Okay, I heard that. I'll go and chop some wood.
eino_barbarian.laugh_off: My brother said worse every day for forty years. You're not my brother.
eino_barbarian.confide: {name}, my brother sold his half of our forest, and I watched it come down in one winter. I was too stubborn to stop him properly. I still think about it.
eino_barbarian.listen: I heard you, {name}. Sit, we don't need to say more.
eino_barbarian.look_out: I'll clear the way in there, {name}. You walk where I've been.
eino_barbarian.deflect: It's nothing, {name}. I've had worse from a falling branch.
eino_barbarian.check_in: {name}, are you okay? Show me where.
eino_barbarian.blame: Somebody didn't look where it would fall. It wasn't me.
eino_barbarian.thank: Thank you. I was going, and now I'm not.
eino_barbarian.brush_off: It needed doing, so I did it. Sit down now.
eino_barbarian.worry: {name}, I didn't like that at all. Sit, and I'll make coffee.
eino_barbarian.handed_down: This was yours before. I'll look after it.
eino_barbarian.hand_fine: Keep it, I don't need much. I've got the axe.
eino_barbarian.hand_sulk: If anybody had asked, I'd have said yes.
eino_barbarian.turn_friendly: I'm good at being quiet with you, {name}. That's rare for me.
eino_barbarian.turn_friends: {name}, you can sit in my sauna any time. I've never said that to anyone.
eino_barbarian.turn_grating: This isn't working between us, I think. That's okay, I don't need everybody.
eino_barbarian.turn_rivals: I'll do the work beside you. Nothing else, though.
eino_barbarian.make_up: I was stubborn with you, {name}. I'm stubborn with everybody, and I'd like to stop with you.
eino_barbarian.defend: Stop that now. {name} did nothing wrong, and I saw it.
eino_barbarian.friend_left: {name} has gone home for a while. I notice, which surprises me.
eino_barbarian.friend_back: Good, {name} came back. The sauna's warm.
eino_barbarian.common_machines: I drove a harvester for many years, in the dark, alone. I still think about that machine more than I'd tell anyone.
eino_barbarian.common_snow: Where I'm from, the sun doesn't come up for weeks in winter. Snow makes a quiet that nothing here makes.

elias_suncleric.meet: I'm Elias, a sun cleric, and I stand in front. Take your time, I've got this side. Sorry if I'm in your way, I'm a big man.
elias_suncleric.meet_neighbour: You're on this coast too, near the Drownbell? I've seen you on the sand. I'm Elias, and I'm building a shelter down the beach.
elias_suncleric.ask_home: So where's home for you, {hermano|hermana}? I like to know where people's people are.
elias_suncleric.ask_work: What did you work at back home, mi pana? Tell me, take your time.
elias_suncleric.answer_home: Santo Domingo, with a big family, a loud city, and my grandmother's church every Sunday.
elias_suncleric.answer_work: I fixed motorbikes for twelve years with my cousin, in a workshop with a tin roof. We argued about the radio every single day.
elias_suncleric.chat_food: My grandmother's sancocho, {hermano|hermana}, with everything in it. On a Sunday after church, it fixed whatever was wrong with you.
elias_suncleric.chat_sleep: I sleep fine, mostly. I check on everybody before I lie down, though, with my little mirror, and that takes a while.
elias_suncleric.chat_missing: Bachata on a bad radio, while my cousin and I argued over a bike. One more afternoon of that would do me a lot of good.
elias_suncleric.chat_here: The Light showed up while I was fixing a cart, in my second year. Nothing special happened, it was just there. I treat it like any new tool and learn what it can take.
elias_suncleric.tease_quiet: {name}, you're so quiet, I keep checking on you in my mirror. Make a little noise for me.
elias_suncleric.tease_talker: {name}, you'd talk the paint off a bike, mi pana. My cousin was the same, and I loved him for it.
elias_suncleric.tease_careful: {name}, you check everything twice, like a good mechanic. I'd let you work on my bike, and I don't let anybody.
elias_suncleric.tease_bold: {name}, you ride like there's no such thing as brakes. I'll be right behind you, fixing what falls off.
elias_suncleric.tease_any: {name}, you're like an old bike that runs on stubbornness. I mean that as a compliment, {hermano|hermana}.
elias_suncleric.tease_back: Ha, you got me there, {name}. That's fair enough, mi pana.
elias_suncleric.take_it_kindly: My grandmother would've said the same, {name}. I won't argue.
elias_suncleric.bristle: Not that one, {name}, please. Some things I keep in the toolbox.
elias_suncleric.apologise: I'm sorry, that wasn't kind of me. I'm not usually like that.
elias_suncleric.double_down: I'm keeping that one, mi pana. Somebody needed to say it gently, and I tried.
elias_suncleric.needle_quiet: You don't tell anybody when something's wrong. I can only fix what I can see.
elias_suncleric.needle_talker: You talk over everybody, {hermano|hermana}. Give the others a turn, please.
elias_suncleric.needle_careful: You take it apart and never put it back together. At some point you have to try the engine.
elias_suncleric.needle_bold: You rush every repair. A bike you rush breaks down on the road, every time.
elias_suncleric.needle_any: You make a big show of everything, and it gets in the way of the work.
elias_suncleric.bite_back: I've stood in front of you every fight, and I didn't complain once. Don't tell me I'm not doing my part.
elias_suncleric.hurt: That's maybe fair, mi pana. I'll have to take it apart later and see.
elias_suncleric.laugh_off: My cousin said worse to me every morning for twelve years, mi pana. You'll have to try harder.
elias_suncleric.confide: {name}, everybody says I coped well with all this. I'm not sure I've got to it properly yet, and I think it's still waiting for me somewhere.
elias_suncleric.listen: I'm glad you told me, {name}. Sit with me, there's no hurry at all.
elias_suncleric.look_out: I've got your side in there, {name}, like always, so keep close.
elias_suncleric.accept: You know best this time, {name}, I'll follow.
elias_suncleric.deflect: I'm fine, {name}, I'm fine. Look after the others, I'm built for this.
elias_suncleric.check_in: {name}, let me see you. Where did it get you?
elias_suncleric.blame: Somebody rushed it, and the whole thing came apart. It wasn't me, mi pana.
elias_suncleric.thank: Mi pana, I felt the Light go out and you lit it again. Gracias, from my heart.
elias_suncleric.brush_off: It's what we do, mi pana. Rest a minute.
elias_suncleric.worry: {name}, I saw that in my mirror and I didn't like it. Sit down a minute, please.
elias_suncleric.handed_down: Mi pana, I think this was yours. I'll keep it running for you.
elias_suncleric.hand_fine: Keep it, {hermano|hermana}, it suits you. I've got my mirror, that's enough.
elias_suncleric.hand_sulk: I'd have handed it over if someone had asked. Nobody asked me, though.
elias_suncleric.turn_friendly: Mi pana {name}, you're good people. I'm glad you're on my side.
elias_suncleric.turn_friends: {name}, if I ever build a workshop here, you've got a bench in it, mi pana. Family gets a bench.
elias_suncleric.turn_grating: We don't run smooth together, do we? That's okay, we'll find a way.
elias_suncleric.turn_rivals: I'll still stand in front of you, because that's what I do. That's all it is, though.
elias_suncleric.make_up: {name}, this has gone on long enough, mi pana. Let's tune it up and start again.
elias_suncleric.defend: Easy, now, that's not fair. Leave {name} out of it.
elias_suncleric.friend_left: My mirror keeps showing an empty space where {name} used to be.
elias_suncleric.friend_back: {name}, good to see you, mi pana! Your side's still free.
elias_suncleric.common_machines: Twelve years under motorbikes in a tin-roofed workshop, and I could hear a bad chain from across the street. You know engines too, mi pana.
elias_suncleric.common_faith: My grandmother took me to church every Sunday, and when she couldn't ask any more, I kept going because I liked the singing. I don't make a show of it.
elias_suncleric.common_spanish: Ah, you speak Spanish! Mi pana, talk to me, I've been rationing my English all week.

elie_bloodmage.meet: I'm Elie, a healer of a sort. Give me your arm, {habibi|habibti}, I promise this is the least frightening thing you'll see down here.
elie_bloodmage.meet_neighbour: Khaz Varun's upper halls, that's where I know you from. I'm Elie, and I'm the one with the clean bandages.
elie_bloodmage.ask_home: Where did you grow up, {habibi|habibti}? I always want to know what the sea was like, if there was one.
elie_bloodmage.ask_work: And what did you do, before? Tell me while I check your arm.
elie_bloodmage.answer_home: Beirut, Achrafieh, near the sea. I rode an old motorbike along the Corniche at sunset every evening.
elie_bloodmage.answer_work: I drew blood at a clinic for ten years. I was the one the nervous patients asked for, because I talk the whole time.
elie_bloodmage.chat_food: My mother cooked for twenty people every Sunday, on a seamstress's wage. Kibbeh, tabbouleh, fattoush, the whole table. I can still smell it.
elie_bloodmage.chat_sleep: I sleep badly down here, away from the sea. I keep listening for waves and there's nothing but stone.
elie_bloodmage.chat_missing: The Corniche at sunset, on my old bike that ran on spare parts and prayers. I'm starting to forget what the sea sounds like.
elie_bloodmage.chat_here: Most bloodmages here use it to hurt people. I use it to heal, which they think is a waste. It's the same work I always did, without the needle.
elie_bloodmage.tease_quiet: {name}, you're like my calmest patient, the one who never said a word. I always worried about that one most.
elie_bloodmage.tease_talker: {name}, {habibi|habibti}, you talk nearly as much as I do when I'm drawing blood. That's a compliment, I promise.
elie_bloodmage.tease_careful: {name}, you'd make a good phlebotomist. You look for the vein three times before you go in.
elie_bloodmage.tease_bold: {name}, you'd stick the needle in before you found the vein. I've had trainees like you, and they learned.
elie_bloodmage.tease_any: {name}, you're my favourite patient, and you're also my worst. Both of those are true.
elie_bloodmage.tease_back: Ah, very good, {name}! You got me, and I'll get you back later.
elie_bloodmage.take_it_kindly: That's fair, {name}. My mother said exactly that, every Sunday.
elie_bloodmage.bristle: Please, {name}, not about that. Pick something else to tease me about.
elie_bloodmage.apologise: I'm sorry, that was unkind of me. I'm usually better with people than that.
elie_bloodmage.double_down: I'll stand by it, {habibi|habibti}. I say it gently, but I say it.
elie_bloodmage.needle_quiet: If it hurts, tell me. I can't help you if you sit there pretending you're fine.
elie_bloodmage.needle_talker: Please, let somebody else speak. The frightened ones can't get a word in.
elie_bloodmage.needle_careful: You make the frightened ones wait while you decide. Waiting is the worst part for them.
elie_bloodmage.needle_bold: You're rough with people, and it frightens them. There's no need for it.
elie_bloodmage.needle_any: You use what you've got to hurt people, and I can't stand it.
elie_bloodmage.bite_back: I've kept every one of you breathing down here. Don't tell me I'm not careful.
elie_bloodmage.hurt: Okay, that stung, and I won't pretend it didn't. Give me a minute.
elie_bloodmage.laugh_off: Ah, I've had patients say much worse with a needle in their arm. Come, let's keep going.
elie_bloodmage.confide: {name}, I saved for medical school in Montpellier for six years, and every time I nearly had enough, something happened. I'm a healer now anyway, without the school.
elie_bloodmage.listen: Give me your hand, {name}. Take as long as you like.
elie_bloodmage.look_out: {name}, stay close to me in there. If anything happens, I want to reach you first.
elie_bloodmage.accept: You're the doctor this time, {name}. I'll do as you say.
elie_bloodmage.deflect: Really, {name}, it's just a scratch. Help the others before me.
elie_bloodmage.check_in: {name}, give me your arm. Let me see how bad it is.
elie_bloodmage.blame: Somebody was rough in there, and now I've got three of you to stitch. You know who you are.
elie_bloodmage.thank: I thought I'd bled out, {habibi|habibti}. Thank you, from the heart.
elie_bloodmage.brush_off: That's what I'm here for, {habibi|habibti}. Breathe slowly for me.
elie_bloodmage.worry: {name}, you frightened me. Give me your arm, I need to check you properly.
elie_bloodmage.handed_down: I believe you wore this before me. I'll keep it clean for you.
elie_bloodmage.hand_fine: Keep it, please. I've got my tourniquet, and that's all I really need.
elie_bloodmage.hand_sulk: I'd have said yes, gently, if somebody had thought to ask.
elie_bloodmage.turn_friendly: {name}, I like having you around, {habibi|habibti}. You make the dark a bit less dark.
elie_bloodmage.turn_friends: {name}, there's a plate for you every Sunday when I cook, for as long as I'm cooking.
elie_bloodmage.turn_grating: We don't work well together, I think. I'll be gentle about it, but it's true.
elie_bloodmage.turn_rivals: I'll still heal you, because I heal everyone. Don't ask for more than that.
elie_bloodmage.make_up: {name}, let's stop this, please. I don't like being on bad terms with anybody.
elie_bloodmage.defend: Please, that's enough. {name} didn't deserve that.
elie_bloodmage.friend_left: The halls feel colder down here without {name}.
elie_bloodmage.friend_back: {name}, come here, {habibi|habibti}, I want to look at you.
elie_bloodmage.common_medic: Ten years drawing blood, and I was the one the nervous patients asked for. You've worked with patients too, you have the hands for it.
elie_bloodmage.common_blood: Blood magic's only ever been healing to me, the same work without the needle. I'd like to hear how you use it.
elie_bloodmage.common_arabic: You speak Arabic, {habibi|habibti}! You've no idea how much I've missed hearing it.

emiliano_pyromancer.meet: ¡Qué onda, {carnal|carnala}! I'm Emiliano, pyromancer and showman. Want to see a trick?
emiliano_pyromancer.meet_neighbour: Cinderwharf, by the forges, I know your face! I'm Emiliano, and I'm the one the crowds come for.
emiliano_pyromancer.ask_home: Where are you from, {carnal|carnala}? Tell me, and make it a good story.
emiliano_pyromancer.ask_work: What was your act before all this? Everybody's got an act, {carnal|carnala}.
emiliano_pyromancer.answer_home: Oaxaca, {carnal|carnala}, the best city in Mexico. Ask anybody from Oaxaca and they'll tell you the same.
emiliano_pyromancer.answer_work: I breathed fire at the traffic lights by the zócalo for eleven years, two minutes a red light, coins through the car windows.
emiliano_pyromancer.chat_food: Tlayudas from the market, {carnal|carnala}, big as a car wheel, with a little mezcal on the side. That's real living.
emiliano_pyromancer.chat_sleep: I sleep when the crowd goes home, and the crowd never goes home. So I don't sleep much.
emiliano_pyromancer.chat_missing: My four sisters, all of them shouting at me at once in my mother's kitchen. I helped raise them, and they've never once let me win an argument.
emiliano_pyromancer.chat_here: The fire here came out of me the colour of a dragon on my first try. I've been showing off ever since, and I'm not sorry.
emiliano_pyromancer.tease_quiet: {name}, {carnal|carnala}, you'd be a terrible audience. You don't clap, you don't shout, you just stand there.
emiliano_pyromancer.tease_talker: {name}, you could hold a crowd for longer than a red light, I'll give you that. Almost as long as me.
emiliano_pyromancer.tease_careful: {name}, you'd stand three metres back from a candle. Come closer, I won't burn you, probably.
emiliano_pyromancer.tease_bold: {name}, you'd jump through my fire just to see if you could. Órale, I like you already.
emiliano_pyromancer.tease_any: {name}, you're my best audience, {carnal|carnala}, and my worst. You never pay.
emiliano_pyromancer.tease_back: ¡Órale, {name}, you've got a mouth on you! I respect it.
emiliano_pyromancer.take_it_kindly: Okay, okay, {name}, that's fair. My mother says the same thing.
emiliano_pyromancer.bristle: Hey, not that one, {carnal|carnala}. Watch your mouth with that.
emiliano_pyromancer.apologise: Perdón, that was too much, even for me. I'm sorry, really.
emiliano_pyromancer.double_down: Nah, I'm keeping that one, {carnal|carnala}. It was a good line.
emiliano_pyromancer.needle_quiet: You stand at the back and never clap. Give a man something, at least.
emiliano_pyromancer.needle_talker: You talk over my act, {carnal|carnala}. Nobody talks over my act.
emiliano_pyromancer.needle_careful: You're so careful, it's painful to watch. Live a little, before you're old.
emiliano_pyromancer.needle_bold: You think you're the star out here. There's only one star, {carnal|carnala}, and it's me.
emiliano_pyromancer.needle_any: You think street performers are beggars, I can see it on your face. Eleven years and not one burn, and you look down at me.
emiliano_pyromancer.bite_back: Hey, I've held crowds you couldn't hold for ten seconds. Don't you tell me about doing my job.
emiliano_pyromancer.hurt: Fine, fine, message received. I'll keep it down for a while.
emiliano_pyromancer.laugh_off: Ha, I've had drunks at the lights say worse, {carnal|carnala}, and they still paid. Come on, let's go.
emiliano_pyromancer.confide: {name}, I paid for two of my sisters to finish school. I'm prouder of that than of any trick, and I don't tell people, because it ruins my image.
emiliano_pyromancer.listen: No show, no joke, {name}. That stays with me.
emiliano_pyromancer.look_out: When I light up in there, {name}, you want to be on my right side, so remember that.
emiliano_pyromancer.accept: Okay, {name}, your way, just this once. Don't tell anybody.
emiliano_pyromancer.deflect: I'm fine, {carnal|carnala}, look at my hands, not a mark. Eleven years and not one burn.
emiliano_pyromancer.check_in: {name}, you okay? Show me where it got you, quick.
emiliano_pyromancer.blame: Somebody ruined the act in there, and it wasn't me. I hit every cue.
emiliano_pyromancer.thank: You saved my life, {carnal|carnala}! Next show's free for you, front row.
emiliano_pyromancer.brush_off: That's what I'm here for, {carnal|carnala}. Now you have to clap.
emiliano_pyromancer.worry: {name}, you scared me, {carnal|carnala}! Sit down, let me see you.
emiliano_pyromancer.handed_down: Órale, I'm wearing your gear now! I'll make it look good, I promise.
emiliano_pyromancer.hand_fine: Keep it, {carnal|carnala}, it looks better on you. I've got my lamp oil.
emiliano_pyromancer.hand_sulk: Hey, that was mine, {carnal|carnala}, and I didn't get a say.
emiliano_pyromancer.turn_friendly: {name}, you're in my crowd now, {carnal|carnala}, the front row. That's for life.
emiliano_pyromancer.turn_friends: {name}, I'd do my best trick just for you, {carnal|carnala}, no crowd needed. You're my people now.
emiliano_pyromancer.turn_grating: Not everybody likes the show, and you don't. That's fine, {carnal|carnala}.
emiliano_pyromancer.turn_rivals: Stay out of my spotlight and we'll be fine. That's all I'm asking.
emiliano_pyromancer.make_up: {name}, okay, I was a bit much, I know. Let's start over, {carnal|carnala}.
emiliano_pyromancer.defend: Hey, that's not fair, and I saw it. Leave {name} alone.
emiliano_pyromancer.friend_left: I've lost my best audience with {name} gone home. It's a terrible thing for a performer.
emiliano_pyromancer.friend_back: {name}'s back, órale! Now I've got somebody to show off for.
emiliano_pyromancer.common_spanish: You speak Spanish, {carnal|carnala}! Finally somebody who gets my jokes.
emiliano_pyromancer.common_mexico: You're from Mexico? Tell me where, {carnal|carnala}, and I'll tell you why Oaxaca's better.

emre_rogue.meet: I'm Emre, and I open doors. When we reach a locked one, please let me do the talking, and please don't interrupt.
emre_rogue.meet_neighbour: Durnholde road, that's where I've seen you. I'm Emre, and I'm usually somewhere near a door.
emre_rogue.ask_home: Tell me where you're from, my friend. I like to know what kind of doors people grew up behind.
emre_rogue.ask_work: What did you do before? I've been guessing, and I'm usually wrong, which I enjoy.
emre_rogue.answer_home: Istanbul, the old bazaar quarter. I grew up above my uncle's lock shop, and I knew every door on our street.
emre_rogue.answer_work: Locksmith, from the age of nine. Thirty doors a week for most of my life, and I was never once a thief.
emre_rogue.chat_food: Turkish coffee, my friend, thick enough to stand a spoon in, with a little lokum on the side. Food is just what comes between coffees.
emre_rogue.chat_sleep: I sleep well here, better than I did at home. There's nobody to open up the shop for in the morning.
emre_rogue.chat_missing: There was a proverb from my mother for everything, and I heard them over breakfast every morning. I still say them in my head.
emre_rogue.chat_here: Every lock is a short conversation with somebody who isn't in the room. The people who made the locks here had very strange conversations.
emre_rogue.tease_quiet: {name}, you're as quiet as a good lock. I've been trying to pick you for weeks.
emre_rogue.tease_talker: {name}, you interrupt a door the way you interrupt me. I'm learning patience from you, involuntarily.
emre_rogue.tease_careful: {name}, you test a door before you touch it. My uncle would have taken you on as an apprentice.
emre_rogue.tease_bold: {name}, you'd kick a door in that was never locked. I've watched you do it, and I've wept.
emre_rogue.tease_any: {name}, as my mother used to say, a good friend is a key you didn't know you had. Don't let it go to your head.
emre_rogue.tease_back: Very good, {name}. That one got through my defences.
emre_rogue.take_it_kindly: That's fair, {name}. My mother would have said it with a proverb, but it's fair.
emre_rogue.bristle: Some doors are better left shut, {name}. That's one of them.
emre_rogue.apologise: Forgive me, that was clumsy. I usually choose my words more carefully.
emre_rogue.double_down: I'll keep that one, my friend. It was true, and it was well put.
emre_rogue.needle_quiet: You stand there like a locked door, and I'm tired of picking it.
emre_rogue.needle_talker: You interrupt, my friend, every single time. It takes twice as long, and it was going to take long enough.
emre_rogue.needle_careful: You've been staring at it for ten minutes. Some locks you just open.
emre_rogue.needle_bold: You break doors that could be opened. It's like watching somebody tear a letter instead of unfolding it.
emre_rogue.needle_any: You called me a thief once, and I haven't forgotten. I was never a thief.
emre_rogue.bite_back: I've opened more doors than you've walked through, my friend. Don't tell me about patience.
emre_rogue.hurt: I see, then. I'll keep to myself for a while.
emre_rogue.laugh_off: My uncle said far worse with a deadbolt in his hand, my friend. Shall we go on?
emre_rogue.confide: {name}, I'm content here, and part of the reason is that the shop is gone, and everyone who wanted it kept a certain way. I lost an obligation, not a family, and I've been lighter since.
emre_rogue.listen: Thank you, {name}. I'll keep it locked away where nobody will find it.
emre_rogue.look_out: {name}, let me go first through that door. Whatever's behind it, I'd like to meet it before you do.
emre_rogue.accept: As you say, {name}. I'll go at your pace this once.
emre_rogue.deflect: I'm quite well, {name}, thank you. A scratch from an unfriendly hinge.
emre_rogue.check_in: {name}, you're hurt. Let me see it, slowly, I've got steady hands.
emre_rogue.blame: Somebody forced it, and it went badly, as forcing things does. I think you know who.
emre_rogue.thank: One door closes, another opens, and you held this one open for me. Thank you.
emre_rogue.brush_off: It's nothing, my friend. Rest, and let me make the coffee.
emre_rogue.worry: {name}, that was much too close. Sit, please, and let me see the damage.
emre_rogue.handed_down: I believe this was yours, my friend. I'll keep it oiled and in good order.
emre_rogue.hand_fine: Keep it, please. I've got my picks, and that's all I've ever needed.
emre_rogue.hand_sulk: I'd have been glad to hand it over, if anyone had asked me.
emre_rogue.turn_friendly: {name}, I find I enjoy your company. That's a door I don't open for many people.
emre_rogue.turn_friends: {name}, I'd want you there when I try the door that beats me. That's the greatest honour I can think of.
emre_rogue.turn_grating: We don't fit, you and I, like a key in the wrong lock. Let's not force it.
emre_rogue.turn_rivals: I'll open your doors because it's my job. I won't hold them for you.
emre_rogue.make_up: {name}, we've been turning the wrong key. Let's try again, gently.
emre_rogue.defend: That's not fair, and I saw it all. Leave {name} be.
emre_rogue.friend_left: Doors are less interesting without {name} complaining about how long I take.
emre_rogue.friend_back: Ah, {name}, you've come back. Good, I've been saving a lock for you to watch.
emre_rogue.common_locks: I've opened locks since I was nine, in my uncle's shop above the bazaar. Every lock is a short conversation with somebody who isn't there, and you know that too.
emre_rogue.common_turkish: You speak Turkish, my friend! As my mother would say, a familiar voice is the best key.

enzo_cultist.meet: Enzo, and I'm the best swordsman you'll ever meet. Watch my feet, not the blade, and stay out of my distance.
enzo_cultist.meet_neighbour: The Monastery grounds, yes? We've watched the same drills from the same wall. Enzo, and I'm the one who's always scoring them.
enzo_cultist.ask_home: Which city made you? Everybody's made by a city, whether they like it or not.
enzo_cultist.ask_work: Before all this, what were you good at? Properly good, I mean, not just paid for.
enzo_cultist.answer_home: Naples, the Spanish Quarter, where the streets are so narrow you can pass an espresso from one balcony to the other.
enzo_cultist.answer_work: I fenced sabre from the age of eight. Fourth at the Olympic trials, twice, and fourth is the worst place there is.
enzo_cultist.chat_food: My mother's ragù, cooking from seven in the morning on a Sunday. The whole stairwell smelled of it, and the neighbours came up with bread.
enzo_cultist.chat_sleep: Before a bout I never slept, not once in twenty years. Here every day is a bout, so you can imagine.
enzo_cultist.chat_missing: My scooter, mannaggia, a red Vespa older than me. I rode it through the Quarter at a speed my mother didn't want to know about.
enzo_cultist.chat_here: A voice in the dark offered me more, and I took it. Now I'm the best I've ever been, and I'm still deciding what that cost.
enzo_cultist.tease_quiet: {name}, you're quiet like a good fencer before the call. I'm waiting for the lunge, and it never comes.
enzo_cultist.tease_talker: You talk the way beginners fence, {name}, everything at once and no recovery. It's charming, though.
enzo_cultist.tease_careful: {name}, you'd stand en garde for an hour waiting for the perfect opening. Sometimes you make the opening.
enzo_cultist.tease_bold: {name}, you attack like a twelve-year-old with a new sabre. I mean that kindly, I was one.
enzo_cultist.tease_any: {name}, you've got terrible footwork and a good heart. I can fix one of those.
enzo_cultist.tease_back: Touché, {name}, and a clean one. I'll give you the point.
enzo_cultist.take_it_kindly: Fair, {name}, I'll concede that one. My mother would agree with you, loudly.
enzo_cultist.bristle: Careful with that, {name}. You're inside my distance now.
enzo_cultist.apologise: That was a cheap touch, and I'm sorry. I don't like to win that way.
enzo_cultist.double_down: I'll stand behind that one, completely. You heard me the first time.
enzo_cultist.needle_quiet: You never call your attack, so nobody can cover you. Say something before you move.
enzo_cultist.needle_talker: You never stop talking, and it's a tell. Everything we're fighting can hear exactly where you are.
enzo_cultist.needle_careful: You're so careful you never commit, and a fencer who won't commit is just standing in a white suit.
enzo_cultist.needle_bold: You charge without a plan and call it courage. I've seen what happens to fencers like that.
enzo_cultist.needle_any: You look at the blade instead of the feet, every single time. I've stopped expecting better.
enzo_cultist.bite_back: I came fourth at the Olympic trials, twice, and I've been told worse by better. Try a sharper blade.
enzo_cultist.hurt: Mannaggia, that one landed clean. I'll go and practise alone for a while.
enzo_cultist.laugh_off: Ha, my mother shouted worse at referees every Saturday for twenty years. Jamme, let's go.
enzo_cultist.confide: {name}, the voice in my arm makes me the best I've ever been. I'll never know if it's really me holding the sword, and that's the worst part.
enzo_cultist.listen: I won't say anything, {name}, I promise you that. Thank you for trusting me with it.
enzo_cultist.look_out: {name}, keep inside my reach in there. Nothing gets past my blade, and I'd like you where I can see you.
enzo_cultist.accept: Jamme, {name}, your way. I'll follow your lead this once.
enzo_cultist.deflect: Please, {name}, it's a scratch. I've had worse from a training blade.
enzo_cultist.check_in: {name}, where did it touch you? Show me, I've seen a thousand wounds on the piste.
enzo_cultist.blame: Somebody lunged without looking, and the rest of us paid. I know who it was.
enzo_cultist.thank: You pulled me back from the edge of the piste, so to speak. Grazie, I mean it.
enzo_cultist.brush_off: Prego, it's nothing. Breathe and get your feet under you.
enzo_cultist.worry: {name}, mannaggia, you frightened me. Stand still and let me see where it went in.
enzo_cultist.handed_down: Your gear, I think, and now it's on me. I'll keep it sharp for you.
enzo_cultist.hand_fine: Take it, I don't mind at all. A good fencer only needs the sword.
enzo_cultist.hand_sulk: So it's gone, and nobody thought to ask. I'll remember that.
enzo_cultist.turn_friendly: {name}, I'd fence beside you any day. That's real respect, from me.
enzo_cultist.turn_friends: {name}, I'd let you stand as my second. That's the highest honour I know how to give.
enzo_cultist.turn_grating: We're not a good match, you and I. Let's keep our distance and be civil.
enzo_cultist.turn_rivals: Stay out of my distance and I'll stay out of yours. That's the only rule between us now.
enzo_cultist.make_up: {name}, enough, let's salute and start the bout again. I was being proud, as usual.
enzo_cultist.defend: No, that's not fair at all. {name} kept their line the whole way, I watched.
enzo_cultist.friend_left: It's like fencing without a partner with {name} away. I hate it.
enzo_cultist.friend_back: There you are, {name}! En garde, we've got work to do.
enzo_cultist.common_sport: I fenced for twenty-two years and coached the little ones on Saturdays. Anyone who's played something seriously stands the way you do.
enzo_cultist.common_italian: You speak Italian! Finally, somebody who knows how to talk with their hands properly.

esteban_bloodmage.meet: My name's Esteban, and I'm a bloodmage. Before I use it on you, I'll tell you what it costs and ask if you agree, every time.
esteban_bloodmage.meet_neighbour: We're both in Orgrimmar, I think, near the healers. I'm Esteban, and I've seen you pass the infirmary door.
esteban_bloodmage.ask_home: Where were you born, if you don't mind me asking? I find it tells me a great deal.
esteban_bloodmage.ask_work: And your work, before all this? I'm always curious what people were trained to do with their hands.
esteban_bloodmage.answer_home: Valparaíso, in Chile, on one of the hills above the harbour, where the old lifts creak up the slopes.
esteban_bloodmage.answer_work: Vascular and trauma surgery, nineteen years. Car crashes, stabbings, accidents at the port, mostly at three in the morning.
esteban_bloodmage.chat_food: A glass of Chilean red with dinner, and nothing else needed. I'd take a good carménère over any meal on this world.
esteban_bloodmage.chat_sleep: Surgeons learn to sleep in twenty-minute pieces, on a chair, in a corridor. I've never unlearned it.
esteban_bloodmage.chat_missing: Classical music in the operating theatre at night, quietly, while I worked. I still hum Bach when I'm concentrating.
esteban_bloodmage.chat_here: Most bloodmages I meet want power and don't much care who pays for it. The magic is honest. The company it keeps is a continual disappointment.
esteban_bloodmage.tease_quiet: {name}, you have the bedside manner of a closed door. I mean that with real fondness.
esteban_bloodmage.tease_talker: {name}, I've done entire operations in less time than that story took. It was a good story, though.
esteban_bloodmage.tease_careful: You measure twice and cut once, {name}, which most people only say. You'd have done well in surgery.
esteban_bloodmage.tease_bold: {name}, you'd operate without washing your hands, wouldn't you? I've met surgeons like you, briefly.
esteban_bloodmage.tease_any: {name}, if I ever have to explain the risks to you, I'll keep it short. You never listen past the first sentence.
esteban_bloodmage.tease_back: Very good, {name}. I'll note that in your file, with approval.
esteban_bloodmage.take_it_kindly: That's a fair diagnosis, {name}. I accept it.
esteban_bloodmage.bristle: I'd prefer that wasn't a joke, {name}. It isn't one to me.
esteban_bloodmage.apologise: That was badly said, and I apologise. I should choose my words as carefully as I choose my incisions.
esteban_bloodmage.double_down: I stand by what I said. I'd rather be precise than comfortable.
esteban_bloodmage.needle_quiet: You don't tell anyone where it hurts, so I'm treating you blind, and that puts everyone at risk.
esteban_bloodmage.needle_talker: Could you lower your voice a little? It's hard to concentrate on a wound with commentary.
esteban_bloodmage.needle_careful: You've hesitated three times now. In theatre that's how a patient bleeds out while everyone's being careful.
esteban_bloodmage.needle_bold: You act first and consider afterwards. I've sewn up a great many people who did that.
esteban_bloodmage.needle_any: You don't ask before you take what you need. I find that very hard to work beside.
esteban_bloodmage.bite_back: I've kept people alive with my hands for nineteen years. Please don't lecture me about care.
esteban_bloodmage.hurt: I see, and that's a fair point. It'll take me a while to agree with it.
esteban_bloodmage.laugh_off: I've had consultants say worse to me across an open chest. You'll have to aim more precisely.
esteban_bloodmage.confide: {name}, once, on a Bloodsail ship, I took a prisoner's blood to save their captain, and I didn't ask him. The prisoner died that night. That's why I ask everyone now.
esteban_bloodmage.listen: Thank you, {name}. What you've told me stays with me, the way everything a patient tells me does.
esteban_bloodmage.look_out: {name}, stay where I can reach you in there. If anything opens a vein, I want to close it quickly.
esteban_bloodmage.accept: As you prescribe, {name}. I'll follow your instructions.
esteban_bloodmage.deflect: It's superficial, {name}, I've checked. Attend to the others first.
esteban_bloodmage.check_in: {name}, where's the bleeding coming from? Tell me exactly, and don't round it down.
esteban_bloodmage.blame: Somebody acted before they'd assessed the situation. I watched it happen, and so did you.
esteban_bloodmage.thank: You stopped the bleeding before I could. Thank you, sincerely.
esteban_bloodmage.brush_off: It was a simple procedure, nothing more. Rest, and keep the limb raised.
esteban_bloodmage.worry: {name}, your colour's wrong. Sit down, please, and let me check your pulse.
esteban_bloodmage.handed_down: I believe this was previously yours. I'll return it in the same condition, I promise.
esteban_bloodmage.hand_fine: It's of more use on you, so please keep it. I've got what I need.
esteban_bloodmage.hand_sulk: I'd have consented, if I'd been asked. I wasn't asked, and that matters to me.
esteban_bloodmage.turn_friendly: {name}, I've come to trust you, which I don't do lightly. Thank you for making it easy.
esteban_bloodmage.turn_friends: {name}, I'd let you hold the knife. That's a surgeon's highest compliment, and I mean it.
esteban_bloodmage.turn_grating: We don't work well together, and I'd rather name it than pretend. We'll manage professionally.
esteban_bloodmage.turn_rivals: I'll keep you alive, because that's my oath. That's the whole of it.
esteban_bloodmage.make_up: It was beneath me to be unkind to you, {name}. I'd like to put it right.
esteban_bloodmage.defend: That's inaccurate, and unkind. {name} did exactly what was needed.
esteban_bloodmage.friend_left: {name}'s away for a while, and I find the work duller without the conversation.
esteban_bloodmage.friend_back: Ah, {name}, good. I'd begun to miss being argued with properly.
esteban_bloodmage.common_medic: Nineteen years as a trauma surgeon, mostly at three in the morning. People who've worked in medicine have a particular way of watching a wound, and you have it.
esteban_bloodmage.common_blood: Blood magic is surgery with the formalities removed, as far as I'm concerned. I'd be glad to compare how we each use it.
esteban_bloodmage.common_spanish: Spanish, and well spoken. I've missed being able to say exactly what I mean.
esteban_bloodmage.common_chile: Chilean, are you? Tell me which city. I'm from Valparaíso, and I'll forgive you if it's the capital.

faris_shaman.meet: Peace be with you, I'm Faris. Sit by the water for a while if you like, it's good water.
faris_shaman.meet_neighbour: We share the lake, I think. I've seen you at Moonglade in the mornings, and I'm Faris.
faris_shaman.ask_home: Where's your family's land, {habibi|habibti}? Tell me about the water there.
