imelda_primalist.turn_rivals: I'll still heal you, because it's my job, but don't expect me to like it.
imelda_primalist.make_up: Touch gloves, {name}? Let's start the bout again, clean this time.
imelda_primalist.defend: That's a cheap shot, and it isn't true. Back off from {name}.
imelda_primalist.friend_left: My corner's empty with {name} away, and I don't like it.
imelda_primalist.friend_back: Good to see you back, {name}. Let's get to work.
imelda_primalist.common_ring: Nineteen years in the ring, about ten fights a year, and I won more than I lost. Fighters stand a certain way, and you stand like one.
imelda_primalist.common_sport: I trained every evening after the quay for nineteen years. Anybody who's competed knows the work nobody sees is the real fight.

isla_witchhunter.meet: I'm Isla, a witch hunter. I don't miss, and I'd rather not have to prove it today, so stay out of my line.
isla_witchhunter.meet_neighbour: Light's Hope, aye, I've seen you about the chapel. I'm Isla, with the Order, watching the east road.
isla_witchhunter.ask_home: Which hills are yours, then? Everybody's got a place they measure the rest against.
isla_witchhunter.ask_work: What kept you busy before all this? Tell me plainly, I'll not judge.
isla_witchhunter.answer_home: Above Glen Affric, in the Highlands. A cottage, a lot of hill, and not many people.
isla_witchhunter.answer_work: I stalked deer on an estate, and I shot biathlon for Scotland. Both are about a slow heart and a steady breath.
isla_witchhunter.chat_food: A dram of whisky by the fire after a long day on the hill. That's food enough for me, and my dad would agree.
isla_witchhunter.chat_sleep: I sleep light, always have. A stalker's always half listening for something moving on the hill.
isla_witchhunter.chat_missing: A still dawn in the glen, with the mist on the water and a stag lifting its head. Nothing here's that quiet.
isla_witchhunter.chat_here: I stayed well clear of the Crusade when I got here. I'd watched what they did, and I wanted no part of it.
isla_witchhunter.tease_quiet: Grand, {name}, somebody else who knows how to keep still. We'll get on fine.
isla_witchhunter.tease_talker: You'd scare every deer in the glen, {name}. Keep talking, I'll stalk something else.
isla_witchhunter.tease_careful: You line up a shot nearly as slow as me, {name}, though only nearly, mind.
isla_witchhunter.tease_bold: You'd take the shot before you'd seen the stag, {name}. Och, I'd have sent you home.
isla_witchhunter.tease_any: Dinnae fash, {name}, I've seen worse shots than you. Not many, but some.
isla_witchhunter.tease_back: Aye, very good, {name}. That one hit.
isla_witchhunter.take_it_kindly: Fair, {name}, I'll give you that one. My dad would have laughed.
isla_witchhunter.bristle: Leave it, {name}, I'm not laughing at that one.
isla_witchhunter.apologise: That came out harder than I meant it to. I'm sorry, and that's me saying it properly.
isla_witchhunter.double_down: I said it, and I'll stand by it. I don't miss, and I don't take things back either.
isla_witchhunter.needle_quiet: If you've seen something on the hill, say so. A quiet stalker's no good if nobody knows what they saw.
isla_witchhunter.needle_talker: You'd scare off every living thing for a mile. Some of us are trying to hear what's coming.
isla_witchhunter.needle_careful: You've had the shot three times now. Take it, or let somebody else.
isla_witchhunter.needle_bold: You're careless with that weapon, and it's going to hurt somebody who's on your side.
isla_witchhunter.needle_any: You waste everything, shots, time, breath. It's a hard thing to stand next to.
isla_witchhunter.bite_back: I've shot for my country. Don't you tell me how to hold my aim.
isla_witchhunter.hurt: Aye, that stung, I'll not pretend it didn't. I'll go and watch the road for a while.
isla_witchhunter.laugh_off: My dad told me far worse jokes than that every single morning. Let's get on.
isla_witchhunter.confide: {name}, my dad raised me on his own in a cottage above the glen and taught me to wait. Every good shot I've ever taken is really his.
isla_witchhunter.listen: That stays with me, {name}. I'm good at keeping still, and I'm good at keeping quiet.
isla_witchhunter.look_out: I'll cover you in there, {name}, as long as you stay in my line of sight.
isla_witchhunter.accept: Aye, {name}, have it your way this once.
isla_witchhunter.deflect: Dinnae fash yourself, {name}, it's a wee scratch. See to the rest.
isla_witchhunter.check_in: Talk to me, {name}, where's it got you? Go slowly now.
isla_witchhunter.blame: Somebody took a wild shot in there and gave us all away. You'll know who.
isla_witchhunter.thank: I felt that one going, and you held me on the hill. Thank you, truly.
isla_witchhunter.brush_off: Och, it's nothing at all. Breathe slow, and steady.
isla_witchhunter.worry: Steady now, {name}, steady. My heart's going faster than it has in years.
isla_witchhunter.handed_down: That was yours, aye, and now it's on me. I'll keep it clean, the way my dad kept his rifle.
isla_witchhunter.hand_fine: Aye, keep it, it's more use on you. I travel light on the hill.
isla_witchhunter.hand_sulk: A wee bit of asking wouldn't have hurt anybody, would it?
isla_witchhunter.turn_friendly: I'm glad to have you on the hill with me, {name}. You don't spook easy.
isla_witchhunter.turn_friends: I'd take you up the glen at dawn, {name}, to see the stags. That's the best thing I know.
isla_witchhunter.turn_grating: We're not suited, you and me. I'll keep to my line, and you keep to yours.
isla_witchhunter.turn_rivals: I'll cover you because it's the job. Don't read anything more into it.
isla_witchhunter.make_up: That's enough of being stiff with each other, {name}. Let's start again, aye?
isla_witchhunter.defend: That's wrong, and I had the clearest view. Leave {name} be.
isla_witchhunter.friend_left: The hill's quieter without {name}, and that's saying something for me.
isla_witchhunter.friend_back: There you are, {name}. I kept your place on the ridge.
isla_witchhunter.common_scots: Scottish, are you? Och, thank God for a proper voice. Whereabouts are you from?
isla_witchhunter.common_wild: I've spent more of my life on the hill than off it, stalking and waiting. People who've lived outdoors learn to listen before they look.
isla_witchhunter.common_sport: I shot biathlon for Scotland, skiing and shooting. Anybody who's competed seriously knows how much of it's just breathing.

ivan_warrior.meet: I'm Ivan, and I'm a warrior. Stand where I can see you, go when I say go, and we'll be fine.
ivan_warrior.meet_neighbour: Orgrimmar, yes, you live near the Chasm. I'm Ivan, and I'm the one directing the traffic at seven.
ivan_warrior.ask_home: And where do you come from? Somewhere with good timetables, I hope.
ivan_warrior.ask_work: Your job before, what was it? Something punctual, I hope.
ivan_warrior.answer_home: Novosibirsk, in Siberia. In winter it's forty below, and the trams still run on time.
ivan_warrior.answer_work: I drove a tram for eleven years, Route 13, through the dark mornings. Not one accident, not once.
ivan_warrior.chat_food: Strong black tea, very hot, and black bread with salt. The rest is extra, and usually disappointing.
ivan_warrior.chat_sleep: I'm in bed at ten and up at five. That's the timetable, and this world can't change it.
ivan_warrior.chat_missing: My two girls, Sonya and Katya, arguing over the last of the jam at breakfast. Every morning, the same argument.
ivan_warrior.chat_here: This world has very low standards for punctuality. Nobody's ever on time, and nobody's ever sorry.
ivan_warrior.tease_quiet: Good, {name}, somebody who doesn't talk. You can ride my tram any day.
ivan_warrior.tease_talker: If you talked any more, {name}, I'd have to give you a ticket.
ivan_warrior.tease_careful: You look both ways twice, {name}. Good, you'd be a safe passenger.
ivan_warrior.tease_bold: You step off the kerb without looking, {name}, every time. You'd give a tram driver a heart attack.
ivan_warrior.tease_any: Late again, {name}, by four minutes. I counted, and I forgive you, this once.
ivan_warrior.tease_back: Hm, that was funny, {name}. Don't let it happen again.
ivan_warrior.take_it_kindly: Fair enough, {name}. My wife says the same thing.
ivan_warrior.bristle: That isn't funny, {name}, so please stop.
ivan_warrior.apologise: That was rude of me, and I'm sorry for it. I'm grumpy, but I'm not usually unkind.
ivan_warrior.double_down: I meant every word, and I'd say it on time again tomorrow.
ivan_warrior.needle_quiet: You don't say where you're going, and then you're in the way. Signal, at least.
ivan_warrior.needle_talker: You talk like a broken radio on a long route. Please, a little silence.
ivan_warrior.needle_careful: You wait at every stop until the timetable's ruined. Move when the light's green.
ivan_warrior.needle_bold: You run out in front of everything without looking. One day something won't stop in time.
ivan_warrior.needle_any: You're late, every time, and you're never sorry. I've noticed, and I'm tired of it.
ivan_warrior.bite_back: I drove eleven years without one accident. Don't talk to me about being careful.
ivan_warrior.hurt: Fine, that one stung. I'll go and stand at the back for a while.
ivan_warrior.laugh_off: My passengers complained worse every morning for eleven years. I still got them there on time.
ivan_warrior.confide: {name}, every day on my tram I was frightened of a child stepping off the kerb without looking. You can't stop a tram quickly. I never hit one, and I still dream about it.
ivan_warrior.listen: I heard you, {name}, all of it. I'll keep it, and I'll not say a word.
ivan_warrior.look_out: Stay in my eyeline in there, {name}. I don't like surprises, especially with you.
ivan_warrior.accept: Okay, {name}, your route this time. I'll follow it.
ivan_warrior.deflect: It's nothing, {name}, a bruise. Worry about somebody who's actually hurt.
ivan_warrior.check_in: Up, {name}, slowly, and tell me where. Don't make me guess.
ivan_warrior.blame: Somebody went early, and the whole thing came off the rails. I know who.
ivan_warrior.thank: I was finished in there, and you got me back on the rails. Thank you, I mean it.
ivan_warrior.brush_off: It's nothing, it's part of the job. Sit down and drink your tea.
ivan_warrior.worry: Stay down a minute, {name}. I didn't like how that looked, not one bit.
ivan_warrior.handed_down: Your gear, now on me. I'll look after it like my old tram.
ivan_warrior.hand_fine: Take it, it's more use on you. I don't need much, I never have.
ivan_warrior.hand_sulk: In my country we usually ask first, and nobody asked me.
ivan_warrior.turn_friendly: You're always on time, {name}, more or less. That makes you my friend.
ivan_warrior.turn_friends: You'd have a seat on my tram for life, {name}, the one by the driver. That's the best seat.
ivan_warrior.turn_grating: You and me, we're not on the same timetable. I'll keep to mine, and you keep to yours.
ivan_warrior.turn_rivals: I'll stand where I'm needed, that's what I'm paid in bread for. Don't expect a cup of tea.
ivan_warrior.make_up: We've been stubborn, both of us, {name}. Let's start the route again from the first stop.
ivan_warrior.defend: That's wrong, and I saw it happen. Leave {name} be.
ivan_warrior.friend_left: The route feels empty now {name}'s gone home. I don't like empty routes.
ivan_warrior.friend_back: Good, {name}, you're back on the timetable, so let's go.
ivan_warrior.common_road: Eleven years driving the same route through the dark mornings. People who've driven for a living know every pothole like a person.
ivan_warrior.common_snow: In Novosibirsk it's forty below in January, and the trams still run on time. This world doesn't know what cold is.
ivan_warrior.common_parent: I've got two girls, Sonya and Katya. I talk about them all the time, my wife says too much, and she's right.

joaquin_suncleric.meet: I'm Joaquín, and I heal, and I fight with my hands when I've got to. If you've got something heavy to put down, the Order's a good place for it, che.
joaquin_suncleric.meet_neighbour: The Bulwark, near the Order's quarter, I've seen you there. I'm Joaquín, and I'm usually by the chapel.
joaquin_suncleric.ask_home: Which city raised you, che? Tell me about it, I like hearing about places.
joaquin_suncleric.ask_work: And before all this, what were you? I'm a teacher, so I'll ask follow-up questions.
joaquin_suncleric.answer_home: Rosario, in Argentina. My father worked the railways and my mother ran the library.
joaquin_suncleric.answer_work: I taught history to fifteen-year-olds for fourteen years, with a mate gourd on my desk and a novel in the drawer I never finished.
joaquin_suncleric.chat_food: Mate in the morning, passed round, che, the same gourd for everybody. It's not really about the drink.
joaquin_suncleric.chat_sleep: I sleep badly, most nights. I've got reasons, and I don't think I should sleep well yet.
joaquin_suncleric.chat_missing: A classroom of difficult teenagers on a Friday afternoon, all of them arguing with me about the French Revolution.
joaquin_suncleric.chat_here: I adjusted to this world far too well, and that's the whole problem with me. I'd like to be honest about that.
joaquin_suncleric.tease_quiet: You'd have been one of my good students, {name}, quiet at the back, thinking.
joaquin_suncleric.tease_talker: You'd have been one of my difficult ones, {name}, talking through every lesson. I liked them best, mind.
joaquin_suncleric.tease_careful: You think before you speak, {name}, which puts you ahead of most historians.
joaquin_suncleric.tease_bold: You'd have started a revolution in my classroom, {name}, just to see what happened.
joaquin_suncleric.tease_any: Ten out of ten for effort, {name}, and six for everything else. I'm a strict marker.
joaquin_suncleric.tease_back: Ha, good, {name}, that's a fair hit. I'll give you the mark.
joaquin_suncleric.take_it_kindly: That's fair, che, I accept it, {name}. My students said worse.
joaquin_suncleric.bristle: I'd ask you not to joke about that, {name}. I've got reasons.
joaquin_suncleric.apologise: That was unkind of me, and I'm sorry. I'm supposed to be better than that now.
joaquin_suncleric.double_down: I'll stand by it, gently. You needed to hear it from somebody.
joaquin_suncleric.needle_quiet: You keep everything to yourself until it's too late. I know where that leads, better than most.
joaquin_suncleric.needle_talker: Let somebody else speak, che, please. Listening is most of the job.
joaquin_suncleric.needle_careful: You hesitate so long that it's somebody else who pays for it. I've seen that.
joaquin_suncleric.needle_bold: You're so sure of yourself, and certainty without doubt frightens me more than anything here.
joaquin_suncleric.needle_any: You're cruel when it's easy to be, and I can't stand that. I know cruelty when I see it.
joaquin_suncleric.bite_back: I've done worse things than you'll ever know, and I carry them myself. Don't try to put more on me.
joaquin_suncleric.hurt: You're right, I think, and it hurts because you're right. I'll sit with it.
joaquin_suncleric.laugh_off: I've been hit by people I'd wronged, and they had better reasons than you. Let's keep going.
joaquin_suncleric.confide: {name}, in the Crusade they made me an interrogator, because I listened. I told myself I was saving lives, and I was breaking people. Now I find the ones who lived and say sorry to their faces.
joaquin_suncleric.listen: Take your time, {name}. I'm good at listening, and this time it's only for you.
joaquin_suncleric.look_out: Stay close to me in there, {name}. I'd like to be the one between you and whatever's coming.
joaquin_suncleric.accept: Of course, {name}, we'll do it your way.
joaquin_suncleric.deflect: I'm all right, {name}, it's nothing I don't deserve. Help the others first.
joaquin_suncleric.check_in: Sit up slowly, {name}, and tell me where it hurts.
joaquin_suncleric.blame: Somebody was very sure of themselves in there, and we all paid for it.
joaquin_suncleric.thank: I was gone, che, and you brought me back. I'm not sure I deserve it, but thank you.
joaquin_suncleric.brush_off: It's what these hands are for now. Rest a while.
joaquin_suncleric.worry: Easy, {name}, easy. That was close, and I'm not ashamed to say I was frightened.
joaquin_suncleric.handed_down: Your gear, che, now on me. It'll go back to you whenever you ask.
joaquin_suncleric.hand_fine: Keep it, it's of more use to you. I've got my gourd and my hands.
joaquin_suncleric.hand_sulk: It would have been kind to ask me first. That's all I'll say about it.
joaquin_suncleric.turn_friendly: I'm glad of your company, {name}, che. You're easy to be honest with.
joaquin_suncleric.turn_friends: You're one of the very few people I'd let read my novel, {name}. It's terrible, so that's real trust.
joaquin_suncleric.turn_grating: We don't sit well together, and I'd rather be honest about it.
joaquin_suncleric.turn_rivals: I'll still heal you, because I owe the world more than I can pay. That's all it is.
joaquin_suncleric.make_up: I was hard on you, {name}, and I've had a lot of practice at saying sorry. Let me say it to you.
joaquin_suncleric.defend: No, that's not right, and it's not fair. Leave {name} alone.
joaquin_suncleric.friend_left: {name}'s away for a while, and I find I don't have anybody to tell the true things to.
joaquin_suncleric.friend_back: Ah, {name}, che, back again. Sit, I'll pour the mate.
joaquin_suncleric.common_teacher: Fourteen years teaching fifteen-year-olds, and I liked the difficult ones best. You've stood in front of a class too, I can tell by how you wait for an answer.
joaquin_suncleric.common_ex_scarlet: I joined the Crusade that first winter, like a lot of people did, and I did things there I'll be sorry for until I die. You were there too, I think.
joaquin_suncleric.common_spanish: Spanish, che, finally! Let me hear how you talk, I'll guess where you're from.

junseo_reaper.meet: I'm Jun-seo, a reaper. I'm fast, and I don't talk much, and whatever we do, it's easier than the factory.
junseo_reaper.meet_neighbour: The goblin camp in Stranglethorn, that's where you live too. I run the hoist, and I'm Jun-seo.
junseo_reaper.ask_home: Which city's yours? You don't have to say much.
junseo_reaper.ask_work: Before all this, what did your hands do? I'm curious about it.
junseo_reaper.answer_home: Busan, near the shipyards. My father carried fish at the market, and my mother sewed.
junseo_reaper.answer_work: I welded on a shipyard line, nine years, mostly nights. The same two motions, ten thousand times a night.
junseo_reaper.chat_food: Instant noodles at three in the morning, on a break, with the radio on. I know that's not real food, and I don't care.
junseo_reaper.chat_sleep: I still wake up at the end of a night shift, every morning. My body never got the news.
junseo_reaper.chat_missing: Baseball on the radio, and my mother's kimchi. That's all I'd ask for.
junseo_reaper.chat_here: My first year here I worked every hour there was. In my second year somebody made me sit down, and I didn't know what to do with a day.
junseo_reaper.tease_quiet: We could sit together all day and say nothing, {name}. That's my favourite kind of day.
junseo_reaper.tease_talker: You talk like the radio on a night shift, {name}, never off. It's nice, mostly.
junseo_reaper.tease_careful: You go slowly, {name}, like I'm trying to. Teach me some time.
junseo_reaper.tease_bold: You move before you think, {name}, like me. We should both be more careful.
junseo_reaper.tease_any: Your carving's worse than mine, {name}, and mine's very bad. I'm happy about that.
junseo_reaper.tease_back: Ha, that was good, {name}. I didn't expect it.
junseo_reaper.take_it_kindly: That's true, I think, {name}. I won't argue.
junseo_reaper.bristle: Please, {name}, not about that. I don't like it.
junseo_reaper.apologise: That came out badly, and I'm sorry for it. I'm not good with words.
junseo_reaper.double_down: I meant it, and I'll keep meaning it.
junseo_reaper.needle_quiet: You never say when something's wrong. On the line, that's how somebody gets burned.
junseo_reaper.needle_talker: You talk very loudly, all the time. It's like working next to a foreman.
junseo_reaper.needle_careful: You take so long that the line stops. Somebody has to move.
junseo_reaper.needle_bold: You rush everything, and rushing wastes the work. I've seen it a thousand times.
junseo_reaper.needle_any: You shout at people like a boss, and I don't like bosses who shout.
junseo_reaper.bite_back: I've worked nights for nine years without stopping. Don't tell me I'm slow.
junseo_reaper.hurt: Okay, that hurt a bit. I'll go and carve something badly.
junseo_reaper.laugh_off: Foremen shouted worse at me every night for nine years. Gwaenchana, it's okay.
junseo_reaper.confide: {name}, in a fight my body moves before I decide. It keeps us alive, and I didn't choose any of it. That's why I carve, because I choose every cut.
junseo_reaper.listen: I'm listening, {name}. Take as long as you need, I'm trying to learn to be slow.
junseo_reaper.look_out: Stay behind me in there, {name}. I'm fast, and I'll get there first.
junseo_reaper.accept: Okay, {name}, I'll do it your way.
junseo_reaper.deflect: It's nothing, {name}, easier than the factory. Help somebody else.
junseo_reaper.check_in: Show me where, {name}, slowly. I'm not in a hurry.
junseo_reaper.blame: Somebody rushed it in there, and we all got burned. You know who.
junseo_reaper.thank: I felt myself going, and you stopped it. Thank you, really.
junseo_reaper.brush_off: It's nothing, don't thank me. Sit for a minute.
junseo_reaper.worry: Sit down, {name}, please. My hands are shaking, and they never shake.
junseo_reaper.handed_down: They gave me your gear. I'll take care of it, I promise.
junseo_reaper.hand_fine: Keep it, I don't need it. I've got my hands.
junseo_reaper.hand_sulk: I'd like to have been asked about it, that's all.
junseo_reaper.turn_friendly: I like working next to you, {name}. You don't shout.
junseo_reaper.turn_friends: I'm carving something for you, {name}. It's very bad, and it's yours.
junseo_reaper.turn_grating: We don't fit, you and me. That's okay, I'll keep to myself.
junseo_reaper.turn_rivals: I'll do my part beside you, and nothing else.
junseo_reaper.make_up: We should stop this, {name}. I'm tired of it, and I think you are too.
junseo_reaper.defend: Stop that, it isn't fair. {name} did their part, and I saw it.
junseo_reaper.friend_left: It's quiet without {name}, even for me. I notice it.
junseo_reaper.friend_back: {name}, good, you came back. I saved you a seat by the hoist.
junseo_reaper.common_factory: Nine years on a shipyard line, the same two motions all night. Anybody who's worked a line knows your body learns things your head never agreed to.
junseo_reaper.common_night_work: Nine years of night shifts on the welding line. I still feel most awake at three in the morning, with nobody else around.

karim_felsworn.meet: I'm Karim, a felsworn and a tank. Yes, the eyes are green, and yes, it was a choice, so ask or don't, but please stop staring.
karim_felsworn.meet_neighbour: The Undercrust, below the Flats, I've passed you there. I'm Karim, the one with the survey notes and the green eyes.
karim_felsworn.ask_home: Which country did you come from? A short answer is fine.
karim_felsworn.ask_work: Your old profession, what was it? I'd rather ask than guess wrongly.
karim_felsworn.answer_home: Amman, where my father was an engineer and my mother taught school.
karim_felsworn.answer_work: Land surveyor, fifteen years, mostly in the empty desert east of the city. Weeks at a time with nobody around, and I loved it.
karim_felsworn.chat_food: Black coffee with cardamom, in the desert at dawn. I never needed much else, and I still don't.
karim_felsworn.chat_sleep: I sleep well, as I always have. Empty country teaches you to sleep on anything.
karim_felsworn.chat_missing: A true line across empty ground, and the moment a survey closes perfectly. Nothing here closes perfectly.
karim_felsworn.chat_here: I took the fel deliberately, after consideration, as the fastest way to be useful in a fight. I'll defend that choice to anybody who raises it.
karim_felsworn.tease_quiet: We'd survey well together, {name}. Neither of us would say a word for a week.
karim_felsworn.tease_talker: You've filled the whole valley with words, {name}. I'll have to re-survey it.
karim_felsworn.tease_careful: You check your bearings three times, {name}. I approve, with reservations about the time it takes.
karim_felsworn.tease_bold: You walk straight off the edge of the map, {name}. Somebody has to draw the line where you fell.
karim_felsworn.tease_any: You're imprecise, {name}, and I like you anyway. I find that irritating.
karim_felsworn.tease_back: That was accurate, {name}. I'll allow it.
karim_felsworn.bristle: I'd prefer that didn't become a joke, {name}, so leave it alone.
karim_felsworn.apologise: That was badly put, and I'm sorry. I'm blunt, but I'm not usually cruel.
karim_felsworn.double_down: It was true, and I'll repeat it if you need me to.
karim_felsworn.needle_quiet: You've got a question and you won't ask it. Ask it, or stop looking at me like that.
karim_felsworn.needle_talker: Your words have no edges. Say the thing, and stop there.
karim_felsworn.needle_careful: You've measured it enough. More readings won't change the ground.
karim_felsworn.needle_bold: You run without a bearing, and you expect the rest of us to find you.
karim_felsworn.needle_any: You pity people, and you pity me. I'm tired of it, and I don't need it.
karim_felsworn.bite_back: I chose every part of what I am, carefully. Don't lecture me about choices.
karim_felsworn.hurt: That's fair, and I don't like it. I'll walk ahead for a while.
karim_felsworn.laugh_off: I've been called worse by people who knew me better. Let's keep moving.
karim_felsworn.confide: {name}, my brother moved to Toronto years ago. We called every week, then every month, then not at all. I never decided to stop, and I think about that.
karim_felsworn.listen: No pity, {name}, I promise you that. It stays exactly as you said it.
karim_felsworn.look_out: Stay behind me in there, {name}. I'm the one built to take it.
karim_felsworn.deflect: No pity, please, {name}. It's minor, and you know it is.
karim_felsworn.check_in: Where, {name}, and how deep? Precise answers, please.
karim_felsworn.blame: Somebody went off the line we agreed, and the survey failed. I know whose reading it was.
karim_felsworn.thank: I was gone, and now I'm not. Thank you, plainly.
karim_felsworn.brush_off: It needed doing, and I did it. No need for anything else.
karim_felsworn.worry: Sit down, {name}. That was outside any tolerance I'd accept for you.
karim_felsworn.handed_down: This was on you before. I'll keep it true until you want it.
karim_felsworn.hand_fine: Take it, it does more for you than for me. I don't need much.
karim_felsworn.hand_sulk: Somebody could have asked. I'd have answered.
karim_felsworn.turn_friendly: You've stayed, {name}, after I was blunt with you. Most people don't, and I've noticed.
karim_felsworn.turn_friends: I'd take you surveying in empty country, {name}, for weeks. That's the best thing I know how to offer.
karim_felsworn.turn_grating: We don't work, you and I. I'd rather name it than draw around it.
karim_felsworn.turn_rivals: The job needs a tank, so I'll take the hits for you, and nothing else.
karim_felsworn.make_up: My judgement of you was wrong, {name}, and I'll correct the map. Let's start again.
karim_felsworn.defend: That's imprecise and unfair. Leave {name} alone.
karim_felsworn.friend_left: {name}'s away, and the silence is less comfortable than usual. I didn't expect that.
karim_felsworn.friend_back: Good, {name}'s back. The party's properly surveyed again.
karim_felsworn.common_fel: I took the fel deliberately, after a lot of thought. People who've chosen it the same way are the only ones who don't stare.
karim_felsworn.common_numbers: I've spent my life making lines come out true. People who work with numbers don't round things off, and you don't either.
karim_felsworn.common_desert: Fifteen years in the empty desert east of Amman, weeks at a time alone. People who know the desert know it's never empty.
karim_felsworn.common_arabic: You speak Arabic. Good, it's easier to be precise in your own language.

kesten_the_catalogued.meet: My name's Kesten. For a while I only had a number, and I picked this name myself afterwards, so I'd like you to use it.
kesten_the_catalogued.meet_neighbour: We're both at Kael's Bastion, I think. I'm Kesten, in the storeroom off Gallery Three. I've seen you read the notice board.
kesten_the_catalogued.ask_home: Where were you born? I'd like to write it down, if you don't mind.
kesten_the_catalogued.ask_work: Before all this, what was your work? I keep a record, so I'd like it to be accurate.
kesten_the_catalogued.answer_home: Tallinn, in Kalamaja, the old wooden-house district by the harbour.
kesten_the_catalogued.answer_work: I was an archivist at the Tallinn City Archive for twenty-six years. Parish registers and ships' passenger lists, mostly.
kesten_the_catalogued.chat_food: I don't eat much now, for reasons you can probably guess. I do like the smell of bread, and I stop for it.
kesten_the_catalogued.chat_sleep: I don't sleep the way you do. I read instead, usually, until it's light.
kesten_the_catalogued.chat_missing: The third floor of the archive, in winter, with the radiator ticking. It was the quietest room I've ever worked in.
kesten_the_catalogued.chat_here: I read every notice board in every town here. Somebody ought to keep them, so I've started a copy in pencil.
kesten_the_catalogued.tease_quiet: We'd make a good reading room, {name}. Neither of us would ever say a word.
kesten_the_catalogued.tease_talker: That was four hundred and twelve words, {name}. I counted, and I enjoyed most of them.
kesten_the_catalogued.tease_careful: You check things nearly as often as I do, {name}. I'd have hired you at the archive.
kesten_the_catalogued.tease_bold: You'd open a box without checking the label, {name}. I've seen people do it, and I've never forgotten their names.
kesten_the_catalogued.tease_any: You said about thirty, {name}, and it was twenty-six. I'm telling you because I like you.
kesten_the_catalogued.tease_back: That was well done, {name}, and I'll note it down.
kesten_the_catalogued.take_it_kindly: That's correct, {name}, and I accept the correction.
kesten_the_catalogued.bristle: That isn't something I can laugh about, {name}. Please don't make it a joke.
kesten_the_catalogued.apologise: That was unkind of me, and I'm sorry. I'm out of practice with people.
kesten_the_catalogued.double_down: It was accurate, and I'd say it again, carefully.
kesten_the_catalogued.needle_quiet: If you've seen something, please say so. A record nobody writes down is lost.
kesten_the_catalogued.needle_talker: You round every number you say. It makes it very hard to trust any of them.
kesten_the_catalogued.needle_careful: You've checked it enough. The box doesn't change because you open it again.
kesten_the_catalogued.needle_bold: You're careless with names, and with people. I find that very hard to work beside.
kesten_the_catalogued.needle_any: You said whatever, again. Whatever isn't an answer.
kesten_the_catalogued.bite_back: I was a number in somebody's ledger for two years. Don't tell me I'm careless with people.
kesten_the_catalogued.hurt: I see what you mean. I'll write that down, and think about it later.
kesten_the_catalogued.laugh_off: I've been called worse, and filed under worse. Let's carry on.
kesten_the_catalogued.confide: {name}, I keep my wife's name on the first page of my notebook, because there was a time I couldn't trust myself to remember it. I don't usually tell people that.
kesten_the_catalogued.listen: I'll remember it exactly, {name}, the way you said it. I won't write it down.
kesten_the_catalogued.look_out: Stay where I can see you in there, {name}. I'd like to know where you are.
kesten_the_catalogued.accept: All right, {name}, we'll do it as you say.
kesten_the_catalogued.deflect: It's nothing that matters, {name}. I'm harder to damage than I used to be.
kesten_the_catalogued.check_in: {name}, tell me exactly where you're hurt, please, not roughly.
kesten_the_catalogued.blame: We agreed a number in there and went over it. I keep count, and I know whose pull it was.
kesten_the_catalogued.thank: I felt myself going, and you brought me back. Thank you, I'll remember it.
kesten_the_catalogued.brush_off: It was nothing, truly. Rest, and tell me if it changes.
kesten_the_catalogued.worry: That was too close, {name}. Please sit down, and let me write down how you are.
kesten_the_catalogued.handed_down: My records say this was yours. You'll have it back whenever you ask.
kesten_the_catalogued.hand_fine: It's better used by you, so please keep it. My notebooks are enough.
kesten_the_catalogued.hand_sulk: I'd have liked to be asked. It's a small thing, and I noticed it.
kesten_the_catalogued.turn_friendly: I'd like to put your name in my notebook, {name}, if that's all right. Not the work one.
kesten_the_catalogued.turn_friends: When the first volume's copied, {name}, I'd like you to read it before anyone else.
kesten_the_catalogued.turn_grating: We don't work well together. I'd rather write that down honestly than leave it out.
kesten_the_catalogued.turn_rivals: I'll do my part beside you, accurately. That's all I can promise.
kesten_the_catalogued.make_up: I was unfair to you, {name}, and I'd like to correct the record.
kesten_the_catalogued.defend: That isn't what happened, and I was keeping count. Leave {name} alone.
kesten_the_catalogued.friend_left: I've been saving things up to tell {name}, and they've gone home for a while.
kesten_the_catalogued.friend_back: Good, {name}'s back. I've got eleven things to tell you, in order.
kesten_the_catalogued.common_numbers: I spent twenty-six years making sure the numbers in a register were right. People who work with figures say twenty-six when it was twenty-six, and you do.
kesten_the_catalogued.common_names: I kept parish registers for twenty-six years, and I think every name deserves to be written down properly. You've kept names too, I think.

khalid_hunter.meet: I'm Khalid, a hunter. Walk where I walk and nothing exciting will happen, which is the whole idea.
khalid_hunter.meet_neighbour: Saltwheel, yes, I've seen you at the races. I'm Khalid, the one who never bets.
khalid_hunter.ask_home: Which country are you from? I'm asking politely, so answer politely.
khalid_hunter.ask_work: Your old job, was it logistics? I guess that about everybody, and I'm usually wrong.
khalid_hunter.answer_home: Al Ain, in the Emirates, the oasis city inland. Dates, falcons, and a very large family.
khalid_hunter.answer_work: Logistics at the airport, to pay for the falcons. My family's kept falcons longer than anybody wrote down.
khalid_hunter.chat_food: Arabic coffee with cardamom and dates, in the desert at dawn. Everything else is decoration.
khalid_hunter.chat_sleep: A roof makes me sleep worse, always has. Open sky's better, and here there's plenty of it.
khalid_hunter.chat_missing: My family's gatherings, very loud, forty people and three generations shouting. I was the quiet one in the corner, enjoying it.
khalid_hunter.chat_here: Open country, weather, birds, and no airport. I don't say it in company, but this world suits me.
khalid_hunter.tease_quiet: Finally, {name}, somebody who understands that boring is the aim.
khalid_hunter.tease_talker: You talk like a busy terminal, {name}. Announcements every five minutes, and none of them about my flight.
khalid_hunter.tease_careful: You walk like a falconer, {name}, slowly and looking at everything. My grandfather would approve.
khalid_hunter.tease_bold: You'd fly a falcon in a sandstorm, {name}, to see what happened. I know what happens.
khalid_hunter.tease_any: You're the most interesting thing that's happened to me this week, {name}. That's not a compliment, I like boring weeks.
khalid_hunter.tease_back: Hm, that was funny, {name}. Please don't tell anyone I laughed.
khalid_hunter.take_it_kindly: Correct, {name}, and I'll not argue. My mother would agree with you.
khalid_hunter.bristle: Please leave that alone, {name}. Some things I keep to myself.
khalid_hunter.apologise: That was badly said, and I apologise. I'm better in a small group than a large one.
khalid_hunter.double_down: Once, quietly, and I'll say it a second time just as quietly.
khalid_hunter.needle_quiet: You saw something and didn't say. A falconer who keeps quiet about a hawk loses the bird.
khalid_hunter.needle_talker: You're very loud, and everything in this valley now knows exactly where we are.
khalid_hunter.needle_careful: You wait so long the bird gets bored and flies off. Sometimes you have to cast.
khalid_hunter.needle_bold: You make every day exciting. I've asked you, politely, to make it boring.
khalid_hunter.needle_any: You treat animals like tools. I've noticed, and I find it hard to forgive.
khalid_hunter.bite_back: My family's flown falcons longer than anybody wrote down. Patience is something we invented.
khalid_hunter.hurt: I see what you mean. I'll go and talk to the birds for a while.
khalid_hunter.laugh_off: My mother says worse about my marriage prospects every week. You'll need to try harder.
khalid_hunter.confide: {name}, here's something I don't say in company. I'm happier here than I've been in ten years, and I feel guilty about it, with my family out there somewhere.
khalid_hunter.listen: Quietly kept, {name}, the way I keep everything that matters.
khalid_hunter.look_out: Walk where I walk in there, {name}. With any luck, it'll be very boring.
khalid_hunter.accept: As you like, {name}, and I'll follow.
khalid_hunter.deflect: It's nothing interesting, {name}. Look after the others.
khalid_hunter.check_in: Show me where it caught you, {name}. Slowly, I'm patient.
khalid_hunter.blame: Somebody made it exciting in there, and I'd asked so nicely for boring.
khalid_hunter.thank: I nearly didn't come back from that one. Thank you, {habibi|habibti}, sincerely.
khalid_hunter.brush_off: It's nothing, wallah. Rest a moment, and drink.
khalid_hunter.worry: Please don't do that again, {name}. That was far too exciting for me.
khalid_hunter.handed_down: I'm carrying your gear now, I see. I'll oil the leather, as I used to oil a hood.
khalid_hunter.hand_fine: Take it, it's yours now. I've got my glove.
khalid_hunter.hand_sulk: It would have been polite to ask me first, that's all.
khalid_hunter.turn_friendly: I'll tell you the jokes now, {name}. I only tell them to people I like.
khalid_hunter.turn_friends: If I ever fly a bird again, {name}, I'd want you there, on the glove side.
khalid_hunter.turn_grating: We're not well matched, I think. That's all right, I'll stay quiet.
khalid_hunter.turn_rivals: I'll guide you through because I'm the one who knows the ground. Don't expect jokes.
khalid_hunter.make_up: That was a long, silly silence, {name}, and some of it was mine. Let's start again.
khalid_hunter.defend: That isn't fair, and I saw it all. Leave {name} be.
khalid_hunter.friend_left: {name}'s away for a while, and nobody laughs at my jokes. I'll have to stop telling them.
khalid_hunter.friend_back: Ah, {name}, back again. Good, things were getting interesting without you.
khalid_hunter.common_birds: My family's kept falcons longer than anybody wrote down. People who've flown a bird know the best moment is when it chooses to come back.
khalid_hunter.common_desert: I grew up between the oasis and the desert, and I still think dawn in the dunes is the best hour there is.
khalid_hunter.common_arabic: You speak Arabic, {habibi|habibti}! Now I can tell my jokes properly.

kiet_rogue.meet: I'm Kiet, a rogue, and a courier. Keep your voice down near people, please, you'd be amazed what they say when they think nobody's listening.
kiet_rogue.meet_neighbour: The Abyssal Sands, yes, I've seen you on the caravan road. I'm Kiet, I carry things.
kiet_rogue.ask_home: Which city's yours? Tell me quietly, I like a secret.
kiet_rogue.ask_work: Your old job, I've probably heard about it already, but tell me anyway.
kiet_rogue.answer_home: Bangkok, Khlong Toei, by the port. Loud, hot, and the best street food in the world.
kiet_rogue.answer_work: Motorcycle courier, eleven years. The fastest in my company, and the one nobody remembered.
kiet_rogue.chat_food: Street food in Khlong Toei at midnight, khrap, grilled pork on a stick and sticky rice. Nothing here comes close.
kiet_rogue.chat_sleep: I can't sleep when it's quiet. Eleven years of engine noise, and now I can hear people breathing two rooms away.
kiet_rogue.chat_missing: My grandmother's stories at night, every night, the same ones. She called me her legs.
kiet_rogue.chat_here: Nobody here looks at a courier twice, same as home. You'd be amazed what I've overheard.
kiet_rogue.tease_quiet: You're nearly as invisible as me, {name}. Nearly, I can still see you.
kiet_rogue.tease_talker: You'd make a terrible courier, {name}. Everybody would know where you'd been.
kiet_rogue.tease_careful: You take the long way round every time, {name}. Safe, sure, but slow.
kiet_rogue.tease_bold: You take every gap in the traffic, {name}, like a Bangkok rider. I like you.
kiet_rogue.tease_any: I know three secrets about you, {name}, and I'm keeping all of them, so don't worry.
kiet_rogue.tease_back: Ha, nice one, {name}. I didn't hear that one coming.
kiet_rogue.take_it_kindly: That's fair, khrap, {name}. My grandmother would say the same.
kiet_rogue.bristle: Not that, {name}, please. Leave it alone.
kiet_rogue.apologise: Sorry, that came out wrong. I'm better at listening than talking.
kiet_rogue.needle_quiet: You never say what you've seen, and I'm the one who has to find out. You should tell me.
kiet_rogue.needle_talker: You talk about people like they're not there. They're always there.
kiet_rogue.needle_careful: You take the slow route every time, and we all arrive late.
kiet_rogue.needle_bold: You're so loud going in, everybody knows we're coming. That's the opposite of the job.
kiet_rogue.needle_any: You talk about people behind their backs, and I hear all of it. You should know that.
kiet_rogue.bite_back: I've carried more secrets than you've ever heard. Don't tell me I don't pay attention.
kiet_rogue.hurt: Okay, I heard that. I'll go and be invisible for a while.
kiet_rogue.laugh_off: Mai pen rai, I've had taxi drivers shout worse at me in four languages. Come on, let's go.
kiet_rogue.confide: {name}, I've got a key cut for nothing. I meant to get it cut for a new door downstairs, so my grandmother wouldn't need the stairs. I never got round to it.
kiet_rogue.listen: I won't tell anyone, {name}. I'm very good at that, it's the one thing I'm best at.
kiet_rogue.look_out: Stay in my shadow in there, {name}. Nobody looks at me, so nobody'll look at you.
kiet_rogue.accept: Your route, {name}, okay, and I'll follow it.
kiet_rogue.deflect: Mai pen rai, {name}, it's nothing. Help somebody who needs it.
kiet_rogue.check_in: Quietly now, {name}, tell me where it hurts.
kiet_rogue.blame: Somebody made a lot of noise in there, and everything heard us. You know who.
kiet_rogue.thank: Nobody ever notices me enough to come and get me, and you did. Khob khun khrap, thank you.
kiet_rogue.brush_off: It's nothing, don't make a fuss. Sit still a minute.
kiet_rogue.worry: That was too close, {name}, and I don't like it. Sit down quietly with me.
kiet_rogue.handed_down: I'm wearing what was yours now. I'll deliver it back whenever you want.
kiet_rogue.hand_fine: Couriers don't carry what they don't need, so you keep it.
kiet_rogue.hand_sulk: Nobody asked me, of course. Nobody ever notices me.
kiet_rogue.turn_friendly: I'll tell you the good gossip now, {name}. I only tell it to friends.
kiet_rogue.turn_friends: You'd have a seat on the back of my bike, {name}, any time. I've never offered that to anyone.
kiet_rogue.turn_grating: You and me, we rub each other wrong. That's fine, I'll keep out of your way.
kiet_rogue.turn_rivals: I'll do my part, quietly. Don't expect the gossip.
kiet_rogue.make_up: This is silly, {name}, both of us sulking. Let's stop, khrap.
kiet_rogue.defend: That's not true, and I heard everything. Leave {name} alone.
kiet_rogue.friend_left: It's too quiet since {name} went home, and you know I hate quiet.
kiet_rogue.friend_back: {name}, you're back, khrap! I've saved up so much gossip.
kiet_rogue.common_road: Eleven years on a motorbike in Bangkok traffic. Anybody who's worked the roads knows every route has a shortcut, and every shortcut has a cost.

kourosh_mage.meet: I'm Kourosh, an arcane mage, and I'll stand at the back and be extremely precise. Before every fight I'll give you the odds, cheerfully.
kourosh_mage.meet_neighbour: The Crystalline Underdark, yes, we're nearly neighbours. I'm Kourosh, in the dry corner with the notebooks.
kourosh_mage.ask_home: Which city do you come from? I'm compiling the figures, out of habit.
kourosh_mage.ask_work: And your occupation, before all this? I'd like to adjust my estimates of you.
kourosh_mage.answer_home: Tehran, where my father taught mathematics and my mother worked at a bank and had ambitions for me.
kourosh_mage.answer_work: I was an actuary for twelve years, pricing how likely people were to die. This world is relaxing by comparison.
kourosh_mage.chat_food: My mother's cooking, every Friday, and strong tea with cardamom. The probability of finding either here is low, and I've checked.
kourosh_mage.chat_sleep: I sleep six hours and forty minutes, on average. I'd like more, but the numbers are against it.
kourosh_mage.chat_missing: Persian poetry read aloud, badly, by my father, on a Friday evening. I've got most of it by heart now.
kourosh_mage.chat_here: The first thing I did here was finish the sum I was in the middle of. People call that brave, and it was momentum.
kourosh_mage.tease_quiet: Your silence is statistically remarkable, {name}. I've been recording it.
kourosh_mage.tease_talker: I've estimated your words per hour, {name}, and I won't tell you the figure. It's for your own good.
kourosh_mage.tease_careful: You've checked that twice, {name}. Very sensible, and I'd have checked it a third time.
kourosh_mage.tease_bold: Your odds of surviving the next year are wonderful, {name}, considering how you fight. I've been generous.
kourosh_mage.tease_any: I've calculated our odds of being friends, {name}. They were low at first, and I'm delighted to be wrong.
kourosh_mage.tease_back: Ah, well done, {name}. I'll revise my estimate of your wit upwards.
kourosh_mage.take_it_kindly: That's correct, {name}, within a reasonable margin. I accept it.
kourosh_mage.bristle: The odds of me finding that funny are nil, {name}. Please leave it.
kourosh_mage.apologise: That was poorly judged, and I apologise. I'll recalculate how I speak to you.
kourosh_mage.double_down: The numbers support me, and I'll stand by them.
kourosh_mage.needle_quiet: You've seen something and haven't reported it. Unreported data is the most dangerous kind.
kourosh_mage.needle_talker: You've said a great deal and estimated nothing. Give me something I can use.
kourosh_mage.needle_careful: You're waiting for certainty, and it won't come. At some point you act on the odds.
kourosh_mage.needle_bold: You keep asking me to be brave. I won't, and I'd like you to stop asking.
kourosh_mage.needle_any: You said it'll probably be fine. It won't, probably, and I've done the sum.
kourosh_mage.bite_back: I priced mortality for twelve years. Please don't lecture me on risk.
kourosh_mage.hurt: Noted, with some regret. I'll go and sit with my notebooks for a while.
kourosh_mage.laugh_off: My mother said I was wasting myself every Friday for twelve years. You'll have to do better than that.
kourosh_mage.confide: {name}, in my second year here I priced my mother's odds of having survived, properly. Then I stopped looking, and I've never told anyone else the figure.
kourosh_mage.listen: I've recorded that, {name}, in the one place nobody reads, which is my head.
kourosh_mage.look_out: Stay inside my line of fire in there, {name}. Your odds improve considerably.
kourosh_mage.accept: Very well, {name}. I'll defer to your estimate.
kourosh_mage.deflect: The damage is minor, {name}, within acceptable margins. Attend to the others.
kourosh_mage.check_in: Give me the figures, {name}. Where, how bad, and how long ago?
kourosh_mage.blame: Somebody ignored the odds I gave, and the outcome was entirely predictable.
kourosh_mage.thank: My odds were very poor there, and you improved them. Thank you, sincerely.
kourosh_mage.brush_off: It was a simple matter. Rest, and your odds will continue to improve.
kourosh_mage.worry: That was improbable, {name}, and I don't like improbable. Sit down, please.
kourosh_mage.handed_down: I'm in your gear now, by the look of it. I'll keep it in excellent condition, with records.
kourosh_mage.hand_fine: The expected value's higher on you, so it's yours. My pencil is all I need.
kourosh_mage.hand_sulk: I'd have consented, had I been consulted. I wasn't consulted.
kourosh_mage.turn_friendly: I've stopped calculating your odds, {name}. With me, that's what friendship looks like.
kourosh_mage.turn_friends: I'd let you read my notes, {name}, the private ones. Nobody's read those.
kourosh_mage.turn_grating: We're poorly matched, I think, and the numbers agree. We'll manage professionally.
kourosh_mage.turn_rivals: I'll keep you alive because the odds of the job require it. That's the whole calculation.
kourosh_mage.make_up: My estimate of you was wrong, {name}, and I've revised it. I'd like to start again.
kourosh_mage.defend: That's statistically unfair, and simply untrue. Leave {name} alone.
kourosh_mage.friend_left: {name}'s away, and the party's odds of a good conversation have dropped sharply.
kourosh_mage.friend_back: Ah, {name}'s back. My estimate of today has improved considerably.
kourosh_mage.common_numbers: Twelve years of pricing how likely things are, very carefully. People who work with numbers find this world restful, because for once they hold still.

liam_suncleric.meet: G'day, I'm Liam, firefighter and paramedic back home, healer here. If it all goes bad, stay behind me and breathe out loud so I can hear you.
liam_suncleric.meet_neighbour: Grom's Rest, mate, I'm in the hut next to the one with the two kids. I'm Liam, and I've seen you about the village.
liam_suncleric.ask_home: Whereabouts are you from, mate? I'm terrible with accents.
liam_suncleric.ask_work: What'd you do back home, mate? You've got the look of somebody who's done shifts.
liam_suncleric.answer_home: Katoomba, up in the Blue Mountains outside Sydney. Gum trees, fog, and a lot of bushfire.
liam_suncleric.answer_work: Firefighter, then paramedic, then both, for seventeen years. The roster never cared which badge you had on at three in the morning.
liam_suncleric.chat_food: A barbecue on a Sunday arvo with a cold beer and the crew. Snags, onions, white bread, the whole works.
liam_suncleric.chat_sleep: I haven't slept properly since about 2019, mate, to be fair. I get a few hours, and that'll do.
liam_suncleric.chat_missing: The quiet in the truck on the way back from one that went well. Nobody says anything, and everybody's grinning.
liam_suncleric.chat_here: My first year here was the easiest of my life, because the job was everywhere. Then it went quiet for a season, and that nearly finished me.
liam_suncleric.tease_quiet: You're like a good crew member, {name}, never says a word and always turns up, and I love it.
liam_suncleric.tease_talker: Mate, {name}, you'd talk a cocky off a branch. Keep going, I'm enjoying it.
liam_suncleric.tease_careful: You size up a job like an old fire chief, {name}. Good on you, mate, but we're losing the light.
liam_suncleric.tease_bold: You'd run into a burning shed for a cat, {name}. I know, because I would too.
liam_suncleric.tease_any: You'd be all right on my crew, {name}, if you could make a decent cuppa. Work on it.
liam_suncleric.tease_back: Fair cop, {name}, that one landed, mate.
liam_suncleric.take_it_kindly: Too right, {name}, I can't argue with that one.
liam_suncleric.bristle: Nah, leave that one, {name}. It's not a joking thing for me.
liam_suncleric.apologise: Sorry, mate, that came out wrong. I'm tired, and I took it out on you.
liam_suncleric.double_down: I'll stand by that one, mate. Somebody had to say it.
liam_suncleric.needle_quiet: You freeze up and say nothing when it matters. I need to know where you are, mate.
liam_suncleric.needle_talker: Mate, calm down and stop talking for a sec. Panic's catching, and you're spreading it.
liam_suncleric.needle_careful: You stand in the doorway thinking while it all burns. Move, or get out of the way.
liam_suncleric.needle_bold: You go in alone every time, and I know exactly where that ends up, mate.
liam_suncleric.needle_any: You panic, every time, and somebody else has to deal with it, usually me.
liam_suncleric.bite_back: I've carried people out of burning houses, mate. Don't tell me I don't pull my weight.
liam_suncleric.hurt: Yeah, that one stung, I'll be honest. I'll go and have a cuppa and think on it.
liam_suncleric.laugh_off: Mate, I've had drunks on the highway at three in the morning say worse. Water off a duck's back.
liam_suncleric.confide: {name}, I lost two of my crew in the 2019 fires, and half my street, and I went straight back to work. I never stopped to look at it.
liam_suncleric.listen: No rush, {name}, mate. I'm here, and it stays with me.
liam_suncleric.look_out: Behind me in there, {name}, and breathe out loud so I can hear you.
liam_suncleric.accept: No worries, {name}, I'll do it your way, mate.
liam_suncleric.deflect: She'll be right, {name}, it's a scratch from the highway days. Help someone worse off.
liam_suncleric.check_in: Breathe out loud for me, {name}, so I can hear it. Where's it hurting?
liam_suncleric.blame: Going in alone, in there, and the rest of us paid for it. I know the look, mate.
liam_suncleric.thank: Mate, you got me back, and I'm usually the one doing that. I owe you a beer, a big one.
liam_suncleric.brush_off: No worries, mate, that's the job. Breathe slow, you're right.
liam_suncleric.worry: Steady, {name}, steady, I've got you. Breathe out loud for me.
liam_suncleric.handed_down: Reckon this was yours, mate. You'll get it back, no dramas.
liam_suncleric.hand_fine: No worries, it's yours, mate. I've got my shears, that's plenty.
liam_suncleric.hand_sulk: Bit rough, nobody asking. I'll get over it.
liam_suncleric.turn_friendly: You're one of my crew now, {name}, mate. That's the best thing I can say about anybody.
liam_suncleric.turn_friends: I'd go in for you, {name}, any fire, any night. And I'd let you go in for me, which is harder.
liam_suncleric.turn_grating: We don't really click, mate. No worries, we'll get the job done.
liam_suncleric.turn_rivals: I'll still pull you out if it comes to it, mate, that's who I am. Don't expect a barbie after.
liam_suncleric.make_up: Righto, {name}, let's knock this on the head, mate. Reckon we can start again?
liam_suncleric.defend: Oi, ease up, mate, that's not on. {name} did everything right.
liam_suncleric.friend_left: It's a quiet station without {name}. I keep listening for the radio.
liam_suncleric.friend_back: Good on you, {name}, you're back! Crew's complete again, mate.
liam_suncleric.common_medic: Seventeen years as a paramedic, mostly at three in the morning on the highway. Anyone who's worked in medicine knows the worst calls come at the worst hours.
liam_suncleric.common_fire_crew: I fought bushfires for seventeen summers in the Blue Mountains. Anybody who's been on a fire line knows you watch the wind before you watch the fire.
liam_suncleric.common_rescue: Going back in for people is the whole job, mate. Somebody who's done rescue work has that same look, like they're always counting heads.
liam_suncleric.common_aussie: You're an Aussie! Mate, where from? I haven't heard a proper accent in years.

lucia_suncleric.meet: I'm Lúcia, {querido|querida}, and you've got half the Barrens in your hair. I'll heal you, I'll pray for you, and I'll fix that hair while we walk.
lucia_suncleric.meet_neighbour: The Crossroads, of course, I've seen you by the inn, {querido|querida}! I'm Lúcia, on the stool by the door, and I'm cutting your hair later.
lucia_suncleric.ask_home: So where are you from, {querido|querida}? Tell me everything, I want the whole story.
lucia_suncleric.ask_work: And what was your work, before? Tell me while I fix this fringe.
lucia_suncleric.answer_home: Goiânia, in the middle of Brazil. Hot, flat, and everybody knows everybody's business.
lucia_suncleric.answer_work: I had my own salon, pink tiles and two chairs, and a radio that only got one station. Saturdays there was a queue down the street.
lucia_suncleric.chat_food: Pamonha, {querido|querida}, sweet corn wrapped in the husk, from the stall outside the church. I'd sell my scissors for one.
lucia_suncleric.chat_sleep: Prayers first, then I sleep like a baby, always have. Without them I'm up all night.
lucia_suncleric.chat_missing: Singing in church with other people, meu Deus, all of us together. That's the thing I'd ask the saints for first.
lucia_suncleric.chat_here: Here the sun answers when I pray, and the priests were very surprised. I wasn't surprised at all.
lucia_suncleric.tease_quiet: You're so shy, {name}! I'll get you talking, everybody talks in my chair eventually.
lucia_suncleric.tease_talker: Finally, somebody who talks as much as me! {name}, {querido|querida}, we're going to be best friends.
lucia_suncleric.tease_careful: You'd ask for a trim and then make me take off one hair, {name}. I know your type, I love your type.
lucia_suncleric.tease_bold: You'd cut your own fringe in the dark, {name}, wouldn't you? I can tell from here.
lucia_suncleric.tease_any: That hair, {name}, meu Deus, who did that to you? Sit down, I'm fixing it.
lucia_suncleric.tease_back: Ai, you got me, {name}! That was a good one.
lucia_suncleric.take_it_kindly: True, true, {name}, and I won't argue, my mother would agree with you.
lucia_suncleric.bristle: Not about that, {name}, please. Don't joke about prayer.
lucia_suncleric.apologise: Ai, desculpa, that was unkind of me. I talk too much and the wrong thing comes out.
lucia_suncleric.double_down: I'm keeping it, {querido|querida}. I said it with love, but I said it.
lucia_suncleric.needle_quiet: It's like cutting hair for a statue with you. Talk to me, please.
lucia_suncleric.needle_talker: Even I can't get a word in, and I always get a word in. Let somebody else speak.
lucia_suncleric.needle_careful: You think and think and never decide, {querido|querida}. Pick a haircut and live with it.
lucia_suncleric.needle_bold: You rush into everything, and somebody has to pray for you every night. That somebody's me.
lucia_suncleric.needle_any: You laugh at people who pray. I've noticed, and I'm still praying for you.
lucia_suncleric.bite_back: I've healed you all and never asked for a thing, so don't tell me I'm not helping.
lucia_suncleric.hurt: Ai, that hurt, I won't pretend. I'll go and say a little prayer and come back.
lucia_suncleric.laugh_off: Ha, I've had customers say worse with my scissors at their neck, {querido|querida}. Let's keep going.
lucia_suncleric.confide: {name}, every Sunday my grandmother lit a candle for everybody on our street, by name. When she died, I took over the list, and I still light them.
lucia_suncleric.listen: Come here, {name}, sit. I'll never repeat a word said in my chair, and you're in my chair now.
lucia_suncleric.look_out: Keep near me in there, {name}, so the Light can reach you from my hands.
lucia_suncleric.accept: Your way, {name}, and I'll pray it works.
lucia_suncleric.deflect: I've got the saints watching me, {querido|querida}, I'm fine. Go and help somebody else.
lucia_suncleric.check_in: {name}, {querido|querida}, let me see you. Where does it hurt?
lucia_suncleric.blame: Somebody rushed in without a prayer, and look at us all now.
lucia_suncleric.thank: That was nearly the end of me, {querido|querida}, and now I'm lighting a candle for you on Sunday.
lucia_suncleric.brush_off: Ai, it's nothing, it's the Light, not me. Sit and rest.
lucia_suncleric.worry: Meu Deus, {name}, you scared me! Sit, sit, let me pray over you.
lucia_suncleric.handed_down: Ai, I'm wearing yours now! It's in good hands, like my best scissors.
lucia_suncleric.hand_fine: Take it, {querido|querida}, it looks so much better on you. I've got my rosary.
lucia_suncleric.hand_sulk: Meu Deus, and nobody asked me. I'll pray about it.
lucia_suncleric.turn_friendly: You're on my candle list now, {name}. Every Sunday, I promise.
lucia_suncleric.turn_friends: You're family now, {name}, like the girls in my salon. I'll do your hair for free, forever.
lucia_suncleric.turn_grating: It makes me sad that we don't get along. I'll keep praying for you anyway.
lucia_suncleric.turn_rivals: The Light doesn't choose, so I'll heal you anyway. I'm not happy about it, though.
lucia_suncleric.make_up: Ai, {name}, enough of this. Come here, let me hug you, and we start again.
lucia_suncleric.defend: Ai, that's not fair at all, so stop it. {name} was perfect in there.
lucia_suncleric.friend_left: {name} went home for a while, and I've lit a candle for them already.
lucia_suncleric.friend_back: {name}, meu Deus, you're back! Come here, let me look at that hair.
lucia_suncleric.common_faith: My grandmother raised me on rosaries and saints' days, and I still pray out loud, with my whole heart. It's good to be near somebody else who prays.
lucia_suncleric.common_portuguese: You speak Portuguese, {querido|querida}! Meu Deus, finally, I can talk properly.
lucia_suncleric.common_brazil: Brazilian, like me! Where from, {querido|querida}? I'm from Goiânia, tell me everything.

luka_stormbringer.meet: Call me Luka. I used to captain a ferry, and now I call storms, carefully, so stand behind me if a squall comes in.
luka_stormbringer.meet_neighbour: You're down at the Tempest Shallows too, near the landing. I'm Luka, and I've watched you come and go in the weather.
luka_stormbringer.ask_home: Which coast is yours? Everybody's got one, even the inland people.
luka_stormbringer.ask_work: What kept you busy before all this? Tell me, we've got a long crossing.
luka_stormbringer.answer_home: Split, in Croatia, the son of a fisherman. My wife's family is from the island of Brač.
luka_stormbringer.answer_work: I captained a car ferry for fifteen years, between Split and the islands. A crew of eight, and the run in every weather.
luka_stormbringer.chat_food: Grilled fish at my wife's konoba on Brač, with blitva and a glass of wine. Bad grilled fish is a crime, and this world is full of criminals.
luka_stormbringer.chat_sleep: Sailors sleep in short pieces, with one ear on the weather. Polako, it works well enough.
luka_stormbringer.chat_missing: The Adriatic at dawn from the bridge, flat and silver, before the first cars came aboard.
luka_stormbringer.chat_here: The first storm I called nearly drowned me. That's how I knew it was mine. I call it carefully now.
luka_stormbringer.tease_quiet: A good crew member, {name}, never says a word on the bridge. I'd sign you on.
luka_stormbringer.tease_talker: You'd chat to the passengers all the way to Brač and back, {name}. They'd love you, and I'd go mad.
luka_stormbringer.tease_careful: Sky, then sea, then sky again, before you step outside, {name}. Good, that's a sailor's habit.
luka_stormbringer.tease_bold: You'd sail into a bura for the fun of it, {name}. Ajme, I've buried braver men.
luka_stormbringer.tease_any: You're like a good crossing, {name}, rough at the start and fine in the end.
luka_stormbringer.tease_back: Ha, fair wind, {name}, you caught me there.
luka_stormbringer.take_it_kindly: That's true, {name}, and my wife would tell you so, loudly.
luka_stormbringer.bristle: Leave that alone, {name}. Some things you don't joke about at sea.
luka_stormbringer.apologise: That was out of line, and I'm sorry. The weather's in my head, not my manners.
luka_stormbringer.double_down: I'll not take it back. A captain says the hard thing so the passengers don't have to.
luka_stormbringer.needle_quiet: If you see weather coming, say so. A crew that keeps quiet loses the boat.
luka_stormbringer.needle_talker: Polako, polako, slow down with the talking. I can't hear the wind.
luka_stormbringer.needle_careful: Wait much longer and you'll miss the tide. Some crossings you have to make while you can.
luka_stormbringer.needle_bold: You've no respect for the weather, and the weather doesn't forgive. I've seen it, many times.
luka_stormbringer.needle_any: You panic on deck, and panic spreads faster than water. Keep it inside.
luka_stormbringer.bite_back: I've brought a ferry home through a bura with two hundred people aboard. Lecture me about the sea when you've done that.
luka_stormbringer.hurt: Ajme, that one went in. I'll go and watch the sky for a while.
luka_stormbringer.laugh_off: Seasick passengers were ruder than that every summer for fifteen years. Polako, let's keep going.
luka_stormbringer.confide: {name}, I had two hundred passengers aboard that morning, and I don't know what happened to one of them. I think about them every evening.
luka_stormbringer.listen: I'm here, {name}, on the bridge with you. Take your time, the sea's calm.
luka_stormbringer.look_out: Stand behind me in there, {name}, like a squall's coming. It usually is.
luka_stormbringer.accept: Aye aye, {name}, your heading this time.
luka_stormbringer.deflect: It's a splash, {name}, nothing more, so help the others first.
luka_stormbringer.check_in: Steady, {name}, talk to me. Where did the wave hit you?
luka_stormbringer.blame: Somebody steered into the weather in there, and we all went under. You know who.
luka_stormbringer.thank: That was deep water, and I know deep water. Hvala, thank you for pulling me out.
luka_stormbringer.brush_off: Polako, it's nothing at all. Sit and get your breath back.
luka_stormbringer.worry: Ajme, {name}, you went down like a ship in a bura. Sit, and breathe.
luka_stormbringer.handed_down: That was yours, and now it's on me. I'll keep it dry and stowed properly.
luka_stormbringer.hand_fine: Take it, it's yours now. A captain only needs his whistle.
luka_stormbringer.hand_sulk: A good crew asks the captain first, and nobody did.
luka_stormbringer.turn_friendly: I'd have you on my crew, {name}, any weather. That's high praise from a captain.
luka_stormbringer.turn_friends: When I get my own boat, {name}, you're first aboard. I'll keep a place on the bridge for you.
luka_stormbringer.turn_grating: We don't sail well together, you and me. I'll keep to my end of the boat.
luka_stormbringer.turn_rivals: I'll get you through the storm, because a captain does. Don't expect a glass of wine after.
luka_stormbringer.make_up: Enough rough water between us, {name}. Let's start the crossing again.
luka_stormbringer.defend: That's not fair, and I watched it all. Leave {name} alone.
luka_stormbringer.friend_left: The crew's a hand short with {name} away, and I feel it.
luka_stormbringer.friend_back: Welcome aboard again, {name}. The weather's better with you here.
luka_stormbringer.common_boats: Fifteen years on the bridge of a ferry, in every weather. Anybody who's worked on the water learns to be properly afraid of it.

marco_paladin.meet: My name's Marco. I'm a locksmith, and here I stand in front of people, so you go where you need to go and I'll be in front of you.
marco_paladin.meet_neighbour: We're both in the Undercity, I think, off the Trade Quarter. I'm Marco, with the tools on the windowsill.
marco_paladin.ask_home: Where do your people come from, {ragazzo|ragazza}? Tell me about them.
marco_paladin.ask_work: Your trade, before? A man should know what the people beside him can do.
marco_paladin.answer_home: Naples, the Quartieri Spagnoli, the narrow streets above Via Toledo. My father mended shoes there.
marco_paladin.answer_work: I was a locksmith for thirty-one years, with my own shop and a door that was always open.
marco_paladin.chat_food: A good coffee in the morning, standing at the bar, in one go. That's the whole of Naples in a cup.
marco_paladin.chat_sleep: Old men sleep badly, and I'm an old man. I wake at five and lie there listening to the street.
marco_paladin.chat_missing: A street where everybody knows each other. Here I'm learning the Forsaken one by one.
marco_paladin.chat_here: I looked for people to be useful to in my first fortnight here. That's what I do, I find out what's broken.
marco_paladin.tease_quiet: You're as quiet as me, {name}. Between us, we'll say about ten words a day.
marco_paladin.tease_talker: You talk like my wife, {name}, and I love my wife, so I'll allow it.
marco_paladin.tease_careful: You test a lock before you touch it, {name}. You'd have been a good apprentice.
marco_paladin.tease_bold: You kick the door before you've tried the handle, {name}. Every time, I've watched you.
marco_paladin.tease_any: You remind me of my apprentice, {name}, stubborn and good. Don't tell him I said so.
marco_paladin.tease_back: Ha, you got me, {name}. Very good, {ragazzo|ragazza}.
marco_paladin.take_it_kindly: You're right, {name}, and Carmela would have told me first.
marco_paladin.bristle: Not that, {name}. I'll stand for a lot, but not that.
marco_paladin.apologise: Scusa, I spoke badly. That's not how I should talk to anyone.
marco_paladin.double_down: Once said, it stays said. I'm too old to take things back.
marco_paladin.needle_quiet: Something's broken and you won't say what. I can't fix what I'm not shown.
marco_paladin.needle_talker: You talk too much and listen too little, {ragazzo|ragazza}. Try it the other way.
marco_paladin.needle_careful: You've stood at that door long enough. Some locks you just open.
marco_paladin.needle_bold: You show off in front of everyone, and somebody else pays for it. I've seen it all my life.
marco_paladin.needle_any: You make promises and you don't keep them. I can't abide that.
marco_paladin.bite_back: I've stood in front of people my whole life and never asked for thanks. Don't tell me I'm not doing enough.
marco_paladin.hurt: Hm, that was heavy. I'll carry it a while and see.
marco_paladin.laugh_off: My wife said worse every morning for forty years, {ragazzo|ragazza}. Andiamo, let's go on.
marco_paladin.confide: {name}, I held my grandson four times before all this. Four, I counted. I think about that more than I'd say.
marco_paladin.listen: I'll keep it, {name}, like a key that only opens one door.
marco_paladin.look_out: Behind me in there, {name}. That's where you stay.
marco_paladin.accept: Va bene, {name}, we'll do it your way.
marco_paladin.deflect: A stuck door's hurt me worse, {name}. Look after the young ones.
marco_paladin.check_in: Let me see, {name}. Where is it, and how bad?
marco_paladin.blame: Somebody didn't wait, and we all paid. I'll say no more, but I saw.
marco_paladin.thank: I owe you my life now, {ragazzo|ragazza}, and I pay my debts.
marco_paladin.brush_off: It's nothing, it needed doing. Sit a moment.
marco_paladin.worry: Sit down, {name}, slowly. My heart's not as young as it was.
marco_paladin.handed_down: Yours, I think, before it was mine. I'll keep it oiled, like a good lock.
marco_paladin.hand_fine: Take it, {ragazzo|ragazza}, it's yours now. An old man needs very little.
marco_paladin.hand_sulk: A man likes to be asked. Nobody asked me.
marco_paladin.turn_friendly: I'd let you mind the shop, {name}. That's trust, in Naples.
marco_paladin.turn_friends: You'd have a key to my door, {name}, if I still had a door. That's what family means to me.
marco_paladin.turn_grating: We don't fit together, you and I, like the wrong key. That's all right.
marco_paladin.turn_rivals: Everyone gets me in front of them, you included. Don't mistake it for more.
marco_paladin.make_up: Basta, {name}, enough. We start again, like men of sense.
marco_paladin.defend: No, that's wrong, and I saw it. You'll leave {name} alone.
marco_paladin.friend_left: The door's quieter without {name} coming through it, and I notice it.
marco_paladin.friend_back: Ah, {name}, you've come home. Good, come in.
marco_paladin.common_locks: Thirty-one years of opening doors for people who'd locked themselves out of their lives. Another locksmith knows the real job is listening.
marco_paladin.common_italian: You speak Italian! Finalmente, {ragazzo|ragazza}, where from? Tell me, and I'll tell you what's wrong with it.
marco_paladin.common_parent: Two girls, Giulia and Sara, and a grandson, Matteo, born the February before all this. That's my whole wealth.

marcus_stormbringer.meet: I'm Marcus, a meteorologist, which here means I'm the man who tells you it's going to rain about ten minutes before it does.
marcus_stormbringer.meet_neighbour: Durotar, the ridge above the coast road, that's me, Marcus! I've seen you on the road, and I'm the hut full of notes.
marcus_stormbringer.ask_home: Where'd you grow up? I'm curious what the weather was like, sorry, I'm always curious about that.
marcus_stormbringer.ask_work: Your old job, what was it? I'll try not to turn it into a conversation about clouds.
marcus_stormbringer.answer_home: Toronto, Scarborough in the east end. My parents came from Lagos before I was born.
marcus_stormbringer.answer_work: I was a meteorologist for fifteen years, writing severe-weather warnings for people whose job was deciding they were inconvenient.
marcus_stormbringer.chat_food: Jollof rice at my mum's on a Sunday, the proper Nigerian kind, and an argument with my sister about whose is better. Hers isn't as good, whatever she says.
marcus_stormbringer.chat_sleep: I wake up when the pressure drops, which is a terrible habit and a very useful one. My skin's a barometer now.
marcus_stormbringer.chat_missing: My two nephews asking why the sky's blue, every single visit, and me explaining Rayleigh scattering for twenty minutes. They loved it, I think.
marcus_stormbringer.chat_here: On Earth I could see a storm coming days out and never touch it. Here it answers when I call, and I'm mostly fine with that.
marcus_stormbringer.tease_quiet: You're like a high-pressure system, {name}, calm and stable and saying nothing. I find it very reassuring.
marcus_stormbringer.tease_talker: Finally, somebody who talks as much as me! Sorry, {name}, I'll let you finish, eventually.
marcus_stormbringer.tease_careful: You check the sky before you leave the tent, {name}. Brilliant, you're my favourite person here.
marcus_stormbringer.tease_bold: You'd walk into a lightning storm holding a sword up, {name}. I've done the maths, please don't.
marcus_stormbringer.tease_any: You never listen to my forecasts, {name}, and you always bring a coat anyway. I've noticed, and I'm touched.
marcus_stormbringer.tease_back: Ha, okay, {name}, I didn't see that one coming, and that's my job.
marcus_stormbringer.take_it_kindly: Completely fair, {name}, and my sister says the same.
marcus_stormbringer.bristle: Please don't make a joke of that, {name}. I've seen what happens when people don't take it seriously.
marcus_stormbringer.apologise: Sorry, that came out badly, I was thinking about something else. I'm sorry, I mean it.
marcus_stormbringer.double_down: I'll stand by it. I've been right before and been ignored, and I won't stay quiet this time.
marcus_stormbringer.needle_quiet: You saw it coming and didn't say anything. I've spent my whole career trying to make people say something.
marcus_stormbringer.needle_talker: You're talking over the warning, and the warning's the important bit. Please, just listen.
marcus_stormbringer.needle_careful: Still deciding when it hits, that'll be you. Sometimes the forecast says go now.
marcus_stormbringer.needle_bold: You ignore every warning I give you, and then you're surprised. It's exhausting to watch.
marcus_stormbringer.needle_any: You always say it'll probably be fine. It usually isn't, and I've got the data.
marcus_stormbringer.bite_back: I've been proved right a lot of times and watched it change nothing. Don't you brush me off as well.
marcus_stormbringer.hurt: Oh, okay, that's, yeah, that hurt. I'll go and look at the sky for a bit.
marcus_stormbringer.laugh_off: Ha, managers said worse about my warnings for fifteen years. The storms came anyway.
marcus_stormbringer.confide: {name}, once a flood took a trailer park my warning had named, and people died who didn't need to. I've never told anybody here that.
marcus_stormbringer.listen: I'm listening, {name}, properly, no weather talk, I promise. Take your time.
marcus_stormbringer.look_out: Keep near me in there, {name}. I can feel it before it comes, and I'll pull you clear.
marcus_stormbringer.accept: Your call, {name}, and I'll trust your forecast this time.
marcus_stormbringer.deflect: Ha, it's nothing, {name}, minor turbulence. Check on the others.
marcus_stormbringer.check_in: Talk to me, {name}, where's it got you? I'm here, I'm not going anywhere.
marcus_stormbringer.blame: I said it was coming, and somebody ignored it. That's happened to me before, and I hate it.
marcus_stormbringer.thank: I could feel it going, and then it didn't. Thank you, really, thank you.
marcus_stormbringer.brush_off: Ah, it's nothing, it's what we do. Sit down, breathe.
marcus_stormbringer.worry: Oh no, no, {name}, sit down, please, let me look. That frightened me.
marcus_stormbringer.handed_down: Oh, I've got your gear now? It's safe, I promise, I'm very careful.
marcus_stormbringer.hand_fine: No, take it, it's absolutely fine. I've got my notes, that's all I need.
marcus_stormbringer.hand_sulk: It's fine, I'm used to not being asked about things.
marcus_stormbringer.turn_friendly: You actually listen to my forecasts, {name}. You've no idea how much that means.
marcus_stormbringer.turn_friends: I'd tell you about the trailer park, {name}, and I've never told anyone. You're one of the few.
marcus_stormbringer.turn_grating: We don't really get on, do we? That's okay, I'm used to people brushing me off.
marcus_stormbringer.turn_rivals: I'll still warn you when it's coming. Whether you listen is up to you.
marcus_stormbringer.make_up: This is silly, {name}, isn't it? Let's start again, properly.
marcus_stormbringer.defend: Hey, that's not fair, and it's not true. Leave {name} alone.
marcus_stormbringer.friend_left: {name}'s away for a bit, and nobody listens to my forecasts now.
marcus_stormbringer.friend_back: Brilliant, {name}'s back! Clear skies today, I checked.
marcus_stormbringer.common_sky: I spent my whole career watching the sky, reading what it was about to do. Anybody who's watched the sky for a living knows it never does the same thing twice.

mariana_priest.meet: I'm Mariana, a priest, and a radiation therapist before that. I'll tell you what I'm going to do before I do it, so nothing's a surprise.
mariana_priest.meet_neighbour: Ariden's Watch, of course, I'm in the infirmary there. I'm Mariana, and I've probably checked your readings already.
mariana_priest.ask_home: Which city's yours? I keep a note of everybody's, it helps me remember birthdays.
mariana_priest.ask_work: And before this, what was your field? I'm always interested in how people were trained.
mariana_priest.answer_home: Monterrey, in the north of Mexico. My father worked in the steelworks and my mother taught school.
mariana_priest.answer_work: Radiation therapist, ten years at a cancer centre. I lined up beams to the millimetre so they hit the tumour and nothing else.
