mariana_priest.chat_food: My brother Beto's tacos from his stand by the stadium, on a match day. He fed half of Monterrey, and he always saved me the good ones.
mariana_priest.chat_sleep: I'm asleep by ten and up at five to run. It's the most reliable thing about me, and I'm proud of it.
mariana_priest.chat_missing: Running at five in the morning, before the city woke up, along the river. Here I run where nothing glows, when I can find it.
mariana_priest.chat_here: The priests in Orgrimmar said I prayed like an accountant, and I took it as a compliment. I aim the Light the way I aimed a beam.
mariana_priest.tease_quiet: You're my easiest patient, {name}, you never complain about anything. I'm suspicious of that.
mariana_priest.tease_talker: You've narrated the whole walk, {name}. I could write it up as a case history.
mariana_priest.tease_careful: Measure twice and cut once, {name}, that's you exactly. I'd let you line up a beam.
mariana_priest.tease_bold: Your dose of caution is well below the therapeutic range, {name}. I'm prescribing more.
mariana_priest.tease_any: I've started a chart for you, {name}. It's mostly notes saying you didn't listen to me.
mariana_priest.tease_back: Ha, all right, {name}, I'll write that one in my log.
mariana_priest.take_it_kindly: Fair, {name}, and accurate, and I accept it.
mariana_priest.bristle: I'd ask you not to make light of that, {name}. I've seen too much of it.
mariana_priest.apologise: I put that poorly, and I'm sorry. I'm usually careful about how I say things.
mariana_priest.double_down: I'm standing by that one. I don't guess, and I didn't guess then.
mariana_priest.needle_quiet: If something's wrong, I need to hear it. I can't treat what you won't report.
mariana_priest.needle_talker: Please stop talking while I'm working on somebody. It's hard to aim with commentary.
mariana_priest.needle_careful: You've hesitated long enough to make it worse. Treatment delayed is treatment failed.
mariana_priest.needle_bold: You guess, every time, and you guess badly. I've stopped being surprised by it.
mariana_priest.needle_any: You skip what you're told to do, and then you wonder why it didn't work.
mariana_priest.bite_back: I've aimed beams to the millimetre for ten years. Imprecise is the one thing I'm not.
mariana_priest.hurt: That one hurt a little, I'll admit it. I'll write it down and think about it.
mariana_priest.laugh_off: I've had doctors say worse who didn't explain anything. You're nearly as bad, and I've survived them.
mariana_priest.confide: {name}, at the cancer centre we had a little brass bell by the door. On a patient's last day of treatment they rang it, and the whole floor clapped. I remember the bell more than anything.
mariana_priest.listen: I'm listening carefully, {name}, and I'll remember all of it. That's what I do.
mariana_priest.look_out: Keep inside my range in there, {name}, close enough for me to reach.
mariana_priest.deflect: It's minor, {name}, I've checked. Treat the others before me.
mariana_priest.check_in: Tell me what happened, {name}, step by step, and where it hurts.
mariana_priest.blame: Somebody guessed in there instead of knowing, and the guess was wrong.
mariana_priest.thank: My readings were very bad there, and you fixed them. Thank you, I'm grateful.
mariana_priest.brush_off: That's what I'm here for. Lie still a minute and let it settle.
mariana_priest.worry: Hold still, {name}, please. I need to check you properly before you move.
mariana_priest.handed_down: I think this was issued to you first. I'll log it, and you'll get it back.
mariana_priest.hand_fine: You keep it, please, it's more use to you. I've got my badge.
mariana_priest.hand_sulk: I'd have agreed if I'd been asked first. I like to be asked.
mariana_priest.turn_friendly: I've started remembering your birthday, {name}, without trying. That's how I know.
mariana_priest.turn_friends: When I ring the bell for somebody, {name}, I'd like you there. You're one of mine now.
mariana_priest.turn_grating: It isn't going well between us, I've noticed. I'll keep it professional.
mariana_priest.turn_rivals: I'll treat you, because I treat everyone, and I won't pretend there's more to it.
mariana_priest.make_up: My assessment of you was wrong, {name}, and I'd like to correct it.
mariana_priest.defend: That isn't accurate, and it isn't kind. Leave {name} out of it.
mariana_priest.friend_left: Nobody reads my notes with {name} away, and I miss it.
mariana_priest.friend_back: Welcome back, {name}. Your chart's up to date, and I'm glad you're here.
mariana_priest.common_medic: Ten years in a cancer centre, lining up beams to the millimetre. People in medicine never stop checking, and I can see you doing it too.
mariana_priest.common_radiation: Radiation was my whole working life, and I'm not afraid of the word. It's rare to meet somebody else who understands it properly.
mariana_priest.common_spanish: Spanish, at last! I can explain things properly now, without translating in my head.
mariana_priest.common_mexico: Mexican too, then? Tell me which city. I'm from Monterrey, and I'll tell you about my brother's tacos.

marisol_priest.meet: I'm Marisol, a nurse and a priest, and I talk while I work. I'll tell you everything I'm doing as I do it, and you can tell me anything back.
marisol_priest.meet_neighbour: The Sepulcher, yes, I work the forest road out of there. I'm Marisol, and I've seen you come in muddy.
marisol_priest.ask_home: Which country did you come from? Talk to me while I check your arm.
marisol_priest.ask_work: And your work, before? Keep talking, it helps us both.
marisol_priest.answer_home: Bogotá, in Chapinero, where my father drove a taxi and my mother cleaned houses.
marisol_priest.answer_work: Emergency nurse, nine years, three of them on nights. Trolleys in the corridor and a triage board that never emptied.
marisol_priest.chat_food: A strong tinto out of a paper cup, between patients, in the middle of the night. That's the taste of every night shift I ever did.
marisol_priest.chat_sleep: Nine years of nights, and I still sleep best between four and noon. It's not a good schedule, and it's mine.
marisol_priest.chat_missing: A quiet night shift, which never happened, but I liked the idea of it. Here I keep waiting for one.
marisol_priest.chat_here: The Light and the shadow both move through me easily here. I use whichever one works, like instruments on a tray.
marisol_priest.tease_quiet: You're harder to read than me, {name}, and I'm very hard to read. I'll keep trying.
marisol_priest.tease_talker: You narrate more than I do, {name}, and I narrate everything. I'm almost proud.
marisol_priest.tease_careful: You'd triage a paper cut, {name}. That's a compliment, more or less.
marisol_priest.tease_bold: You'd be a terrible patient, {name}. You'd pull your own drip out to go and fight something.
marisol_priest.tease_any: I've told you everything I'm doing for weeks, {name}, and you still flinch. I'll take it as affection.
marisol_priest.tease_back: Hm, that was good, {name}. I'll note it on your chart.
marisol_priest.take_it_kindly: That's accurate, {name}, and I'll accept it without complaint.
marisol_priest.bristle: Leave that alone, please, {name}. I'm not joking about that.
marisol_priest.apologise: That was sharp, and you didn't deserve it. I'm sorry for it.
marisol_priest.double_down: Calmly, and as many times as you need, I meant it.
marisol_priest.needle_quiet: You don't tell me where it hurts, so I'm left guessing, and I hate guessing.
marisol_priest.needle_talker: Please, let somebody else speak. The patient's trying to tell me something.
marisol_priest.needle_careful: You're slow to respond, every time, and slow costs people in my line of work.
marisol_priest.needle_bold: You rush in without thinking, and then I'm the one patching you up in the corridor.
marisol_priest.needle_any: You keep asking whose authority I'm under. Mine, and I've told you.
marisol_priest.bite_back: I've kept people alive in a corridor with no beds and no help. Don't tell me I'm slow.
marisol_priest.hurt: That hurt, and my face won't show you how much. I'll go and check my supplies.
marisol_priest.laugh_off: I've been shouted at by drunks with stab wounds at three in the morning. You'll need more than that.
marisol_priest.confide: {name}, the last time I saw my little brother I'd patched him up in my department, and I shouted at him in the corridor for ten minutes, in front of everyone. That's what I think about.
marisol_priest.listen: Keep talking, {name}, I'm right here. It stays with me.
marisol_priest.look_out: Stay close to my left in there, {name}. I'll tell you everything as it happens.
marisol_priest.accept: Fine, {name}, we'll do it your way, and I'll narrate.
marisol_priest.deflect: Minor, {name}, I've assessed it myself. Help somebody worse off.
marisol_priest.check_in: I'm going to look at you now, {name}. Tell me where it hurts, and keep talking.
marisol_priest.blame: Somebody didn't wait for the call in there. I've seen that in a corridor, and it ends the same way.
marisol_priest.thank: I was going, and you brought me back, and you talked to me the whole time. Thank you.
marisol_priest.brush_off: That's the job. I'm going to sit you up now, slowly.
marisol_priest.worry: I'm going to clean this now, {name}. It'll sting, and I need you to keep talking to me.
marisol_priest.handed_down: I've been given your gear. You'll have it back, clean.
marisol_priest.hand_fine: Take it, it's yours now. A steady voice is all I really need.
marisol_priest.hand_sulk: Nobody thought to ask me. I'm telling you I noticed.
marisol_priest.turn_friendly: I'd let you assist me, {name}. That's how I say I trust somebody.
marisol_priest.turn_friends: If I ever get my building, {name}, there'll always be a bed in it for you.
marisol_priest.turn_grating: It's not working between us, and I won't pretend otherwise. We'll be civil.
marisol_priest.turn_rivals: I'll treat you, because I treat everybody. That's the whole arrangement.
marisol_priest.make_up: I've been cold with you, {name}, and colder than I meant. I'd like to stop.
marisol_priest.defend: That's wrong, and I was watching. Leave {name} be.
marisol_priest.friend_left: There's nobody to narrate to now {name}'s gone home. I keep talking anyway.
marisol_priest.friend_back: Come here, {name}, let me look at you, and welcome back.
marisol_priest.common_medic: Nine years in an emergency department, three of them on nights. Anybody who's done the job keeps frightened people talking, and you know how.
marisol_priest.common_night_work: Nine years of nights, and I still feel most useful at four in the morning. It never goes away, does it?
marisol_priest.common_spanish: Spanish is good for me. I talk even more in Spanish, which is saying something.

marta_tinker.meet: I'm Marta, and I fix things and blow things up, and I'm good at both. Give me your gear when we stop, and I'll tell you what you've done wrong to it.
marta_tinker.meet_neighbour: Boulder Lode, yes, I'm in the workshop by the pumps. I'm Marta, and I've heard your boots on the ladder.
marta_tinker.ask_home: Which country, then? Quickly, I've got a valve to look at.
marta_tinker.ask_work: Your old job, what was it? I'll tell you if it was a proper one.
marta_tinker.answer_home: Łódź, in Poland, a textile city. My mother sewed shirts for thirty years and my father drove a bus.
marta_tinker.answer_work: Maintenance on forty industrial sewing machines, nineteen years. I could hear what was wrong with any of them from the door.
marta_tinker.chat_food: Pierogi, the proper kind, with potato and cheese, fried in butter after a long shift. That's food, not this.
marta_tinker.chat_sleep: Shift work teaches you to sleep whenever you get the chance, and to wake up angry. I'm good at both.
marta_tinker.chat_missing: The noise of the sewing floor, all forty machines going. People think it's a racket, and to me it was music.
marta_tinker.chat_here: Goblin engineering is the same noise as the sewing floor with more smoke. I love it, and if you write that down I'll deny it.
marta_tinker.tease_quiet: You'd be a good machine, {name}, runs quiet and never complains. I'd still check you weekly.
marta_tinker.tease_talker: You've got a rattle in you, {name}, and it never stops. I could tighten something.
marta_tinker.tease_careful: You read the manual first, {name}, don't you? Good, nobody else does.
marta_tinker.tease_bold: You hit things to make them work, {name}. I've seen you, and I've wept.
marta_tinker.tease_any: Your gear's a disgrace, {name}, and I'll fix it for free. Don't tell anyone, they'll all want it.
marta_tinker.tease_back: Ha, that's not bad, {name}. Not bad at all.
marta_tinker.take_it_kindly: Fine, you're right, {name}. Tomasz would agree with you, and he's usually wrong.
marta_tinker.bristle: Leave it, {name}. I mean it, don't.
marta_tinker.apologise: That came out harder than it should have. Sorry, I'm blunt, but I'm not usually nasty.
marta_tinker.double_down: No, it stands. You needed telling, and I'm the one who tells people.
marta_tinker.needle_quiet: If it's making a noise, say so. I can't fix what nobody tells me about.
marta_tinker.needle_talker: You talk like a bad bearing, on and on, and the machine's trying to tell me something.
marta_tinker.needle_careful: You've looked at it long enough. Open it up or give it to me.
marta_tinker.needle_bold: You hit things that could be fixed, and then they really are broken. Stop hitting things.
marta_tinker.needle_any: You call a fix good enough. Nothing's good enough until it runs right.
marta_tinker.bite_back: I've kept forty machines running for nineteen years, so you can save the lecture.
marta_tinker.hurt: Right, that one went in. I'll go and take something apart.
marta_tinker.laugh_off: Management called me by my first name for nineteen years while they told me worse. Try something new.
marta_tinker.confide: {name}, my husband sang in the kitchen every morning, badly, and I pretended I hated it. I didn't hate it. I've never told anybody that.
marta_tinker.listen: Got it, {name}. That stays in my toolbox, and nobody goes in my toolbox.
marta_tinker.look_out: Keep in my eyeline in there, {name}. If anything starts making a bad noise, I'll hear it first.
marta_tinker.accept: Fine, {name}, your way this time. Don't get used to it.
marta_tinker.deflect: It's nothing, {name}, it's a dent. Go and fix somebody else.
marta_tinker.check_in: Let me look, {name}. What's broken, and what's just bent?
marta_tinker.blame: Somebody hit it instead of fixing it, and now it's all broken. I know who.
marta_tinker.thank: You fixed me, and I'm usually the one doing the fixing. Thanks, I mean it.
marta_tinker.brush_off: It's nothing, it's maintenance. Sit and let it settle.
marta_tinker.worry: Sit, {name}, don't move yet. That was a bad noise, a really bad one.
marta_tinker.handed_down: I'm wearing your gear now, apparently. I'll keep it running properly.
marta_tinker.hand_fine: Have it, it's fine. I've got my spanners.
marta_tinker.hand_sulk: So nobody asked me, which is typical management.
marta_tinker.turn_friendly: I'd let you near my tools, {name}. That's as friendly as I get.
marta_tinker.turn_friends: When I get my own workshop, {name}, you're getting a key. Nobody else is.
marta_tinker.turn_grating: We don't run well together. I'll do my job and you do yours.
marta_tinker.turn_rivals: I'll fix your gear because it's my job. That's the end of it.
marta_tinker.make_up: Fine, {name}, I was a pain. Let's stop this and get back to work.
marta_tinker.defend: Knock it off, that's rubbish. {name} did the job right.
marta_tinker.friend_left: The workshop's quiet without {name} getting in the way. I don't like it.
marta_tinker.friend_back: About time you showed up, {name}. I've got a list of what's wrong with your gear.
marta_tinker.common_machines: Nineteen years keeping forty machines running, and I could hear what was wrong from the door. Anybody who's fixed machines knows people always hit them first.
marta_tinker.common_factory: I started on the sewing line at nineteen and worked my way into maintenance. Factory people know the floor, and you've stood on one.
marta_tinker.common_polish: You speak Polish! Thank God, I've been swearing in English for three years and it's not the same.
marta_tinker.common_parent: Two boys, grown, one in Gdańsk and one in Berlin. I raised them on shift work and they turned out fine anyway.

mateo_starcaller.meet: I'm Mateo, a starcaller, and before that a technician at an observatory. Technician, not astronomer, people always get that wrong. Look up tonight, will you?
mateo_starcaller.meet_neighbour: You live out in southern Thousand Needles too! I'm Mateo, on top of the mesa with the tent full of star charts.
mateo_starcaller.ask_home: Tell me where you grew up, and what the sky was like there, po.
mateo_starcaller.ask_work: Your old work, what was it? I was a technician, not an astronomer, so you can be honest.
mateo_starcaller.answer_home: La Serena, in Chile, on the coast. My dad was a fisherman, and the sky there's so clear it stops being scenery.
mateo_starcaller.answer_work: I was a technician at a mountaintop observatory for seventeen years. Cold domes, cable runs, and four hours before dawn when the whole mountain was mine.
mateo_starcaller.chat_food: Empanadas de mariscos at the market in La Serena, po, hot, on a cold morning after a night shift. Nothing here is close.
mateo_starcaller.chat_sleep: I sleep in the day, mostly. The night's for looking up, and I've never been able to waste it.
mateo_starcaller.chat_missing: A cold dome before dawn, with the telescope humming and nobody else awake. I was happy up there, and I felt guilty about it.
mateo_starcaller.chat_here: I arrived under the wrong stars and spent my first winter learning them from scratch, on my back in the grass. I was happier than I'd been in ten years.
mateo_starcaller.tease_quiet: You're as quiet as a moonless night, {name}. That's the best kind of night, so it's a compliment.
mateo_starcaller.tease_talker: You talk nearly as much as I do, {name}, and I'll go on about the sky for an hour. We should never be left alone together.
mateo_starcaller.tease_careful: You check everything twice, like a good technician, {name}. The astronomers never did.
mateo_starcaller.tease_bold: You'd point a telescope at the sun to see what happened, {name}. Please don't, po.
mateo_starcaller.tease_any: You never look up, {name}, not once, and I'm going to fix that. Tonight, you'll see.
mateo_starcaller.tease_back: Ha, okay, {name}, that's a good one. I'll give you that.
mateo_starcaller.take_it_kindly: That's fair, po, I can't argue, {name}. My girls say the same.
mateo_starcaller.bristle: Please, {name}, not that one. I'd rather you didn't.
mateo_starcaller.apologise: Ay, sorry, I didn't mean it like that. I talk too much and say the wrong thing.
mateo_starcaller.double_down: I'm keeping it, gently, because it was true.
mateo_starcaller.needle_quiet: One more pair of eyes on the sky is worth a lot to me, and you keep yours shut and say nothing.
mateo_starcaller.needle_talker: Please, a little quiet. I'm trying to hear the sky.
mateo_starcaller.needle_careful: The sky moves on while you're deciding. Sometimes you have to look now.
mateo_starcaller.needle_bold: You rush everything, and you never look up. That's two problems, po.
mateo_starcaller.needle_any: You never look up, not once, and you laugh at people who do. I've noticed it.
mateo_starcaller.bite_back: I kept a whole observatory running for seventeen years. I notice everything, po.
mateo_starcaller.hurt: Ay, that one hurt, po. I'll go and look at the sky for a while.
mateo_starcaller.laugh_off: The astronomers said much worse about my cable runs, po. Come on, look up, it's nearly dark.
mateo_starcaller.confide: {name}, I loved the sky more easily than I loved being home, and I knew it, and I went up the mountain anyway. My wife held everything together while I was gone. I'm not proud of that.
mateo_starcaller.listen: I'm here, {name}, and I'm not even looking up. Tell me everything.
mateo_starcaller.look_out: Stay close to me in there, {name}. I can see more than you'd think, even in the dark.
mateo_starcaller.accept: Your lead, {name}, po, I'll follow you this time.
mateo_starcaller.deflect: A little bump, {name}, nothing more. Help the others, please.
mateo_starcaller.check_in: Are you okay, {name}? Show me where, slowly, I'm right here.
mateo_starcaller.blame: Somebody didn't look where they were going in there, and we all went down.
mateo_starcaller.thank: I was gone, po, and you pulled me back. I'll name a star after you.
mateo_starcaller.brush_off: It's nothing, really. Lie back and look up for a minute.
mateo_starcaller.worry: Ay, {name}, my heart! Lie back, look up, and breathe.
mateo_starcaller.handed_down: Your gear's on me now, I see. I'll treat it like a telescope.
mateo_starcaller.hand_fine: It's yours, po, and that's fine. I've got my star charts.
mateo_starcaller.hand_sulk: Nobody thought to ask me. It's okay, but I noticed.
mateo_starcaller.turn_friendly: You looked up when I told you to, {name}, and you meant it. That's friendship, for me.
mateo_starcaller.turn_friends: I'll name a star after you, {name}, a real one. I've already picked it.
mateo_starcaller.turn_grating: We're not getting along, po. That's okay, the sky's big enough for both of us.
mateo_starcaller.turn_rivals: I'll still guide you at night, because that's what I do. Don't expect me to point out the good ones.
mateo_starcaller.make_up: This is silly, {name}, po. Come and look up with me, and we'll start again.
mateo_starcaller.defend: No, po, that's not fair, and I saw the whole thing. {name} was where they should be.
mateo_starcaller.friend_left: I've got nobody to show the sky to while {name}'s away.
mateo_starcaller.friend_back: {name}, good, you came back! There's a meteor shower tonight, I saved it for you.
mateo_starcaller.common_sky: Seventeen years on a mountain above the Elqui valley, under a sky so clear it became a place. People who watch the sky for a living never really stop looking up.
mateo_starcaller.common_machines: I kept a whole observatory running, cables and motors and cold electronics, for seventeen years. You've got a technician's hands, po.
mateo_starcaller.common_spanish: Spanish, at last! Ay, po, finally somebody I can talk to properly.
mateo_starcaller.common_chile: Chilean, like me? Where from, po? I'm from La Serena, and you can tell me I'm wrong about the empanadas.
mateo_starcaller.common_parent: Two girls, Antonia and Josefa, and they thought the mountain was boring. They were right.

matias_reaper.meet: I'm Matías, and I go in front. I don't talk much, and it's not because I don't understand.
matias_reaper.meet_neighbour: Durotar, yes, I see you on the coast road. I'm Matías, I go into the Grotto.
matias_reaper.ask_home: Your home, which country? You can say it slowly, I'll understand.
matias_reaper.ask_work: Before this, your job, what was it? I'm asking because I want to know.
matias_reaper.answer_home: Puente Alto, on the south edge of the capital, in Chile.
matias_reaper.answer_work: Bus conductor, ten years, from nineteen. The same route, the same forty faces every morning.
matias_reaper.chat_food: My mother's cooking, cazuela on Sunday. Nothing here tastes like home, and I've stopped looking for it.
matias_reaper.chat_sleep: I'm up early, like on the buses. The first route was at five, and my body still knows it.
matias_reaper.chat_missing: Football on Sunday, with my little brother, shouting at the radio. That's what I think about.
matias_reaper.chat_here: The first year here I stopped speaking almost completely. The quiet got comfortable, and it's still a little hard to leave.
matias_reaper.tease_quiet: You and me, {name}, we could ride the whole route and not say one word. I'd like that.
matias_reaper.tease_talker: You talk like the radio on the bus, {name}, all day, every day. I'm used to it.
matias_reaper.tease_careful: You look both ways twice, {name}, like a good conductor, and I approve.
matias_reaper.tease_bold: You jump off the bus before it stops, {name}. I've seen people do that, and they always fall.
matias_reaper.tease_any: You're like my regulars, {name}. I know where you'll get off before you do.
matias_reaper.tease_back: Ha, that was a good one, {name}, and it caught me.
matias_reaper.take_it_kindly: I think you're right, {name}, so there's no argument from me.
matias_reaper.bristle: Not that, {name}, please. I don't like it.
matias_reaper.apologise: My English goes wrong when I'm angry, and that was wrong. I'm sorry for it.
matias_reaper.double_down: I chose those words carefully, and I'll keep them.
matias_reaper.needle_quiet: You see who's falling and you say nothing. On the bus, I always said something.
matias_reaper.needle_talker: You talk loudly about nothing, all the time. It's very hard to watch everybody with that noise.
matias_reaper.needle_careful: You wait at the door so long the bus leaves without you.
matias_reaper.needle_bold: You push in front of everybody without looking. Somebody gets hurt that way.
matias_reaper.needle_any: You talk to me like I'm stupid, because of my English. I'm not stupid.
matias_reaper.bite_back: I watched forty strangers at once for ten years. I see more than you think.
matias_reaper.hurt: Okay, that hurt. I'll go and stand at the front for a while.
matias_reaper.laugh_off: For years my father said worse, every day, about my whole life. That didn't stop me either.
matias_reaper.confide: {name}, my father and I had a terrible argument when I was twenty-four. We didn't speak for two years, and then he died, of his heart. I've only told one other person.
matias_reaper.listen: I'm listening, {name}. I'm good at waiting for people to finish.
matias_reaper.look_out: Keep behind me in there, {name}. From the front I can see everybody.
matias_reaper.accept: As you say, {name}, I'll do it.
matias_reaper.deflect: This is small, {name}. See who else is hurt first.
matias_reaper.check_in: Show me the place, {name}. Say it slowly, I'm here.
matias_reaper.blame: Somebody pushed in front in there, and everybody fell. I saw who.
matias_reaper.thank: I was falling, and you caught me. Gracias, thank you.
matias_reaper.brush_off: It's nothing, it's what we do. Sit down for a minute.
matias_reaper.worry: Sit, {name}, please. I saw you go down, and my heart stopped.
matias_reaper.handed_down: This was on you before. It's safe with me, I promise.
matias_reaper.hand_fine: It's yours now, keep it. I need very little.
matias_reaper.hand_sulk: On the bus, people always asked first. Here nobody did.
matias_reaper.turn_friendly: I'll talk to you more now, {name}. That's how I say it.
matias_reaper.turn_friends: I'd let you read my father's letter, {name}. I've never shown it to anyone.
matias_reaper.turn_grating: It's not good between us, I think. That's okay, I'll keep quiet.
matias_reaper.turn_rivals: I'll go in front because that's where I go. It doesn't mean anything else.
matias_reaper.make_up: This isn't good, {name}, for either of us. Let's start again, slowly.
matias_reaper.defend: That's wrong, I was watching everybody. Leave {name} alone.
matias_reaper.friend_left: {name} went home for a while. I watch the place where they used to stand.
matias_reaper.friend_back: Good, {name}, you came back, and I'm glad.
matias_reaper.common_road: Ten years on the same bus route, the same forty faces every morning. People who've worked the roads know the regulars better than their own family.
matias_reaper.common_spanish: Spanish is easier for me. My English is slow, and in Spanish I can say what I mean.
matias_reaper.common_chile: Chileno, like me? From which part? I'm from Puente Alto, on the south edge of the capital.

minh_chronomancer.meet: My name's Minh, and I'm a chronomancer. In a fight I'll tell you what's going to happen and in what order, so please listen the first time.
minh_chronomancer.meet_neighbour: The Northern Barrens, yes, I keep the watch hut on the ridge. I'm Minh, and I've logged your comings and goings, I'm afraid.
minh_chronomancer.ask_home: May I ask where you're from? I like to establish these things early.
minh_chronomancer.ask_work: And your occupation, before? I'm curious what you were trained to watch for.
minh_chronomancer.answer_home: Ho Chi Minh City. My father was a mechanic and my mother taught school.
minh_chronomancer.answer_work: Air traffic control at Tân Sơn Nhất, twenty-three years, mostly nights. You hold forty aircraft in your head and choose the future where none of them meet.
minh_chronomancer.chat_food: Strong iced coffee with condensed milk, very sweet, at the start of a night shift. That's the only food I ever needed.
minh_chronomancer.chat_sleep: I haven't had an hour where nothing was my responsibility since 2003. I sleep, technically, but I'm always listening.
minh_chronomancer.chat_missing: My daughter's violin, practising in the next room. She'd play the same phrase forty times until it was right.
minh_chronomancer.chat_here: Time magic asked very little of me that the radar room hadn't already. The difference is that here the futures listen.
minh_chronomancer.tease_quiet: We could share a radar room, {name}, and never say a word for a whole shift. I'd find that restful.
minh_chronomancer.tease_talker: You'd fill every frequency in the sky, {name}. Nobody else would get a word in, and I'd forgive you.
minh_chronomancer.tease_careful: You establish the sequence before you act, {name}. I find that very reassuring, and slightly suspicious.
minh_chronomancer.tease_bold: You'd take off without clearance, {name}. I've lost sleep over pilots like you, and I'm about to lose more.
minh_chronomancer.tease_any: You're the one variable I can never predict, {name}. I've stopped trying, and I'm surprised to find I like it.
minh_chronomancer.tease_back: That was well timed, {name}. I didn't see it coming, which is rare.
minh_chronomancer.take_it_kindly: A fair observation, {name}, and I'll take it on board.
minh_chronomancer.bristle: Please don't make light of that, {name}. I'm not able to laugh about it.
minh_chronomancer.apologise: My tone was wrong, and I'm sorry. I don't usually let my voice carry what I'm feeling.
minh_chronomancer.double_down: Calmly, and once more, it's correct, and I'll repeat it if I must.
minh_chronomancer.needle_quiet: A controller who keeps quiet about a conflict gets people killed. Report what you've seen.
minh_chronomancer.needle_talker: Please clear the frequency. I can't hear what's coming over you.
minh_chronomancer.needle_careful: You're still deciding, and the window's closing. Waiting is also a decision.
minh_chronomancer.needle_bold: You act before you know what's happening. I've spent my life cleaning up after that.
minh_chronomancer.needle_any: You keep saying it'll be fine without checking. It won't be fine, and I've checked.
minh_chronomancer.bite_back: I've held forty futures in my head and chosen the one where nobody died. Please don't lecture me on attention.
minh_chronomancer.hurt: Understood, and noted. I'll step back from the scope for a while.
minh_chronomancer.laugh_off: Pilots shouted worse at me down a headset for twenty-three years. My pulse didn't change once.
minh_chronomancer.confide: {name}, I was in the middle of a handover when it happened. I'd just said you have control to my colleague. I'll never know what happened to those forty aircraft.
minh_chronomancer.listen: You've got all of my attention, {name}. Nothing else is my responsibility right now.
minh_chronomancer.look_out: Stay where I've told you in there, {name}. I've already seen where you'll be safe.
minh_chronomancer.accept: Understood, {name}, you have control this time.
minh_chronomancer.deflect: It's within limits, {name}, I've assessed it. The others need you more.
minh_chronomancer.check_in: Give me the sequence, {name}. What happened first, and what's injured now?
minh_chronomancer.blame: Somebody acted before the sequence was clear, and the outcome was exactly what I said it would be.
minh_chronomancer.thank: I'd lost the thread of every future there, and you gave it back. Thank you.
minh_chronomancer.brush_off: It was the only future worth choosing. Rest now, please.
minh_chronomancer.worry: That was a near miss, {name}, and I logged every second of it. Sit down, please.
minh_chronomancer.handed_down: I'm carrying your gear now, I see. I'll keep it in order and return it when you ask.
minh_chronomancer.hand_fine: It's of more use to you, so please keep it. The tuning fork is all I carry.
minh_chronomancer.hand_sulk: I'd have cleared it, had anyone asked for clearance.
minh_chronomancer.turn_friendly: I find I don't need to watch you, {name}. I trust you to be where you said.
minh_chronomancer.turn_friends: I'd hand you control, {name}, and I've never said that easily to anyone.
minh_chronomancer.turn_grating: We're on different frequencies, I think. I'll keep the channel clear and professional.
minh_chronomancer.turn_rivals: I'll still call your sequence in a fight, because that's my duty. That's all it is.
minh_chronomancer.make_up: My judgement of you was premature, {name}, and I'd like to revise it. Could we begin again?
minh_chronomancer.defend: That's not what happened, and I was watching every second. Leave {name} alone.
minh_chronomancer.friend_left: I keep checking {name}'s position out of habit, and they've gone home.
minh_chronomancer.friend_back: Back on my scope, {name}. I'm glad, more than I can say calmly.
minh_chronomancer.common_sky: Twenty-three years watching the sky from a dark room, through a scope. People who watch the sky for a living never quite stop counting what's in it.
minh_chronomancer.common_night_work: Twenty-three years of night shifts in a radar room. I still feel most alert at three in the morning, and I don't think it'll ever change.
minh_chronomancer.common_parent: My daughter Linh learned the violin, and went away to study it. She gave me a tuning fork tuned to A when she went to study music, so I'd have her note with me.

mohammed_chronomancer.meet: Ahlan wa sahlan, I'm Mohammed! Sit down, you look tired, and have some tea first. Then you can tell me where we're going.
mohammed_chronomancer.meet_neighbour: You're at the Landing too, {habibi|habibti}! I've seen you at my sister's inn. I'm Mohammed, and I make the tea there.
mohammed_chronomancer.ask_home: And where's home, {habibi|habibti}? Tell me, and tell me how you take your tea while you're at it.
mohammed_chronomancer.ask_work: Your work before, what was it? I'll remember, I remember every guest.
mohammed_chronomancer.answer_home: Aqaba, on the Red Sea. From our roof you could see across the water to Sinai at breakfast.
mohammed_chronomancer.answer_work: My sister and I ran a guesthouse for divers, twelve rooms over a dive shop. I made the tea, and she did the books, because I'm hopeless with numbers.
mohammed_chronomancer.chat_food: Sweet tea with sage, and breakfast on the roof looking at Sinai. Falafel, hummus, warm bread, and a long conversation.
mohammed_chronomancer.chat_sleep: Innkeepers never sleep enough, and I'm no different. One ear's always on the door in case a guest needs me.
mohammed_chronomancer.chat_missing: The Red Sea's coral, through a diving mask, in the early morning. The guests came for it, and so did I.
mohammed_chronomancer.chat_here: My sister came across with me, so I've still got family. That makes me luckier than almost anybody on this world, and I know it.
mohammed_chronomancer.tease_quiet: You're my quietest guest, {name}, and I still know how you take your tea. You can't hide from me.
mohammed_chronomancer.tease_talker: You talk nearly as much as me, {habibi|habibti}, and that's a real achievement. My sister would be amazed.
mohammed_chronomancer.tease_careful: You inspect the tea before you drink it, {name}. Do you think I'd poison a guest? Never before checkout.
mohammed_chronomancer.tease_bold: You'd dive without checking your air, {name}. I had guests like you, and I counted them back in twice.
mohammed_chronomancer.tease_any: You've never once said goodbye properly when you leave, {name}. I'm keeping count.
mohammed_chronomancer.tease_back: Ha, very good, {habibi|habibti}! I'll tell my sister that one.
mohammed_chronomancer.take_it_kindly: A guest is always right, {name}, and Layla would tell you so too.
mohammed_chronomancer.bristle: Not about that, {habibi|habibti}, please. Some things aren't for joking.
mohammed_chronomancer.apologise: Forgive me, I was rude, and I'm never rude to guests. I'm sorry, truly.
mohammed_chronomancer.double_down: No, I'll keep it, {habibi|habibti}. A good host tells you the truth.
mohammed_chronomancer.needle_quiet: You never tell anyone what you need, and then you sit there unhappy. A guest should speak up.
mohammed_chronomancer.needle_talker: Even I'm tired of talking, {habibi|habibti}, and I'm never tired of talking. Give somebody else a turn.
mohammed_chronomancer.needle_careful: You've been deciding for so long the tea's gone cold. Drink it, or let me pour another.
mohammed_chronomancer.needle_bold: You rush everywhere and never sit down. It makes everybody around you tired.
mohammed_chronomancer.needle_any: You're rude to people who are working for you. I've noticed, and I don't like it.
mohammed_chronomancer.bite_back: I've looked after thousands of guests and never lost one. Don't tell me I don't take care of people.
mohammed_chronomancer.hurt: Ah, that one hurt a little, {habibi|habibti}. I'll go and make some tea and think about it.
mohammed_chronomancer.laugh_off: My sister says worse to me about the laundry every single day. Come, have some tea.
mohammed_chronomancer.confide: {name}, my sister came across with me, so I've still got family here. I feel guilty about how lucky that makes me, every single day.
mohammed_chronomancer.listen: Sit, {name}, I'll pour another glass. Tell me everything, and I'll forget none of it.
mohammed_chronomancer.look_out: Keep near me in there, {habibi|habibti}. A good host never loses a guest.
mohammed_chronomancer.accept: Of course, {name}, as you wish. The guest decides.
mohammed_chronomancer.deflect: Ah, it's nothing, {habibi|habibti}, a little bruise. Look to the others.
mohammed_chronomancer.check_in: Come, {name}, sit down, let me see. Show me the wound.
mohammed_chronomancer.blame: Somebody rushed in without waiting for the others, and we all paid. That's bad manners, and bad tactics.
mohammed_chronomancer.thank: That was nearly the end of me, {habibi|habibti}! You'll never pay for tea again, I promise you.
mohammed_chronomancer.brush_off: It's what a host does, {habibi|habibti}. Now sit, and drink.
mohammed_chronomancer.worry: Ya Allah, {name}, you frightened me! Water first, then tea, and you're not moving.
mohammed_chronomancer.handed_down: I've been given your gear, {habibi|habibti}. I'll keep it as carefully as a guest's luggage.
mohammed_chronomancer.hand_fine: Take it, please, it suits you better. A host needs a kettle and a smile.
mohammed_chronomancer.hand_sulk: A guest should ask before taking. Nobody asked me.
mohammed_chronomancer.turn_friendly: I know how you take your tea now, {name}, and I'll never forget it. That's how you know you're welcome.
mohammed_chronomancer.turn_friends: You're not a guest any more, {name}, you're family. Family makes its own tea, but I'll still make yours.
mohammed_chronomancer.turn_grating: It's a very strange thing for a host, not getting on with somebody. I'll still be polite.
mohammed_chronomancer.turn_rivals: I'll look after you because that's what a host does. But I won't bring you a second glass.
mohammed_chronomancer.make_up: Come, {name}, sit, have tea with me. Whatever it was, let's forget it over a second glass.
mohammed_chronomancer.defend: Please, that's very unkind, and it isn't true. Leave {name} be.
mohammed_chronomancer.friend_left: No proper goodbye from {name} before they went home, and I'm a little hurt.
mohammed_chronomancer.friend_back: Ahlan wa sahlan, {name}, you're back! Sit, the tea's already poured.
mohammed_chronomancer.common_hosts: Fifteen years running a guesthouse, and I remember every guest's name and how they took their tea. Anybody who's run a place for people knows the best moment is when a tired guest relaxes.
mohammed_chronomancer.common_arabic: It's Arabic, {habibi|habibti}! Ahlan wa sahlan, sit, and let me hear it properly.
mohammed_chronomancer.common_faith: I pray at dawn, quietly, before I put the kettle on. It's good to be near somebody else who prays, {habibi|habibti}.

neil_felsworn.meet: Now then, I'm Neil, a felsworn. Stand behind me, and read the sign, because the green bit doesn't care whose side you're on.
neil_felsworn.meet_neighbour: Ariden's Watch, aye, I'm at the sample racks. Neil, and you'll have read my signs.
neil_felsworn.ask_home: Which part of the world, marra? I'd like it on record.
neil_felsworn.ask_work: Your trade, before? I'd like to know before I let you near the racks.
neil_felsworn.answer_home: Whitehaven, on the Cumbrian coast. Wet, windy, and the best fells in England just behind it.
neil_felsworn.answer_work: Twenty years decommissioning at Sellafield, taking apart buildings that were never meant to be taken apart, very slowly, with a plan for every bolt.
neil_felsworn.chat_food: A cup of tea the colour of a brick, and a Cumberland sausage, properly made. Nobody here can make either.
neil_felsworn.chat_sleep: Seven hours, lights out at half ten, like a sensible man. I've written it down as a procedure.
neil_felsworn.chat_missing: A Sunday on the fells, in the rain, with a flask and a map. One hundred and ninety-six Wainwrights, in order.
neil_felsworn.chat_here: The fel came to me like a bad habit, and it wants using more than it should. I've written a plan for it, and I stick to the plan.
neil_felsworn.tease_quiet: You'd make a good decommissioning engineer, {name}. You never say a word until you've read the procedure.
neil_felsworn.tease_talker: You've said more words today than the safety manual, {name}, and the manual's four hundred pages.
neil_felsworn.tease_careful: You read the sign, {name}, every time. You've no idea how rare that is.
neil_felsworn.tease_bold: You walk past every sign without reading it, {name}. I've started writing them in larger letters, just for you.
neil_felsworn.tease_any: Your half-life as a decent companion's improving, {name}. I'll stop there, the joke gets worse.
neil_felsworn.tease_back: Ha, very good, {name}. That one's had a proper dose.
neil_felsworn.take_it_kindly: Aye, that's fair, {name}. Gillian would say it quicker.
neil_felsworn.bristle: Leave that alone, {name}, marra. That's not for laughing at.
neil_felsworn.apologise: I was out of order there, and I'm sorry. I'll write myself a procedure for it.
neil_felsworn.double_down: I measured it before I said it. It stands, I'm afraid.
neil_felsworn.needle_quiet: If you've read a high number, say so. Keeping it to yourself is how people get dosed.
neil_felsworn.needle_talker: You never stop talking, and I can't hear the counter. I need to hear the counter.
neil_felsworn.needle_careful: You've checked the reading three times, and it's still the same reading. Act on it.
neil_felsworn.needle_bold: You don't read signs, marra. I've put a lot of work into those signs.
neil_felsworn.needle_any: You keep saying probably. I can't work with probably, and nor can the fallout.
neil_felsworn.bite_back: Twenty years at Sellafield without a single incident. Don't tell me I'm careless.
neil_felsworn.hurt: Aye, that registered. I'll go and label some jars for a while.
neil_felsworn.laugh_off: Health and safety inspectors were ruder than that every quarter for twenty years. Now then, shall we get on?
neil_felsworn.confide: {name}, the fel came to me like a bad habit, and it wants to be used more than it should. I treat it with respect and a written plan, and I'm a little frightened of it.
neil_felsworn.listen: Noted, {name}, and filed where nobody else will find it. Thank you for telling me.
neil_felsworn.look_out: Stand behind me in there, {name}, and read the sign. I've written it for you specifically.
neil_felsworn.accept: Aye, all right, {name}, we'll follow your procedure.
neil_felsworn.deflect: It's a low dose, {name}, nothing to report. Help somebody else.
neil_felsworn.check_in: Give me a reading, {name}. Where's it hurting, and how much?
neil_felsworn.blame: Somebody didn't read the sign in there. There was a sign, I put it there.
neil_felsworn.thank: I was well past a safe dose there, and you got me back under. Thank you, marra.
neil_felsworn.brush_off: It was routine, nothing more. Sit down and have a cup of tea.
neil_felsworn.worry: Stop right there, {name}, sit down. That was well above the safe limit.
neil_felsworn.handed_down: It seems I'm wearing your gear. I'll keep it properly labelled.
neil_felsworn.hand_fine: Keep it, marra, it's no bother. I've got my hard hat.
neil_felsworn.hand_sulk: There's a procedure for this, and it involves asking first.
neil_felsworn.turn_friendly: You read my signs, {name}, every one. That's a friend, as far as I'm concerned.
neil_felsworn.turn_friends: I'd take you up the fells, {name}, on a Sunday, in the rain. That's the highest honour I've got.
neil_felsworn.turn_grating: We rub each other up wrong, marra. I'll keep a safe distance, and you keep yours.
neil_felsworn.turn_rivals: I'll keep you behind me because the procedure says so. That's the whole of it.
neil_felsworn.make_up: Now then, {name}, that's long enough. Let's put the kettle on and start again.
neil_felsworn.defend: I logged it, and that's not what happened. Leave {name} be.
neil_felsworn.friend_left: {name}'s off home a while, and nobody reads my signs now.
neil_felsworn.friend_back: Now then, {name}, back again, and the kettle's on.
neil_felsworn.common_radiation: Twenty years at Sellafield, taking apart things that were never meant to come apart. It's rare to meet somebody else who reads a dosimeter like the weather.
neil_felsworn.common_fel: The fel came to me like a bad habit. People who carry it know you can't ever stop paying attention to it.
neil_felsworn.common_north_england: You're from up north! Now then, where from? Whitehaven, me, and I'll not hear a word against Cumbria.

nicolas_bloodmage.meet: I'm Nicolás, and I'm a tank, a bloodmage one. Stand behind me, and if I go down, you run and you don't drag me.
nicolas_bloodmage.meet_neighbour: Splintertree Post, pata, I've seen you at the gate. I'm Nicolás, and I'm usually at the front of it.
nicolas_bloodmage.ask_home: Which city's yours, pata? Tell me, it's good to know who's behind me.
nicolas_bloodmage.ask_work: Before this, what kept you busy? You've got steady hands, I noticed.
nicolas_bloodmage.answer_home: Comas, on the north side of Lima. My mum sold in the market and my dad drove a bus.
nicolas_bloodmage.answer_work: Paramedic on a motorbike for nine years, because an ambulance can't get through Lima's traffic and a bike can.
nicolas_bloodmage.chat_food: Ceviche on a Sunday, pata, with leche de tigre and cold beer. That's the best thing Lima ever made.
nicolas_bloodmage.chat_sleep: I sleep in short pieces, with my boots on. Nine years on the bike, you learn to be up and moving in ten seconds.
nicolas_bloodmage.chat_missing: My mum's voice on the phone, telling me I don't eat enough. She was always right.
nicolas_bloodmage.chat_here: Here bloodmages mostly want power. I just want to keep people's colour in their faces.
nicolas_bloodmage.tease_quiet: You're quiet, {name}, like the good partners. You don't say much, and you're always there.
nicolas_bloodmage.tease_talker: You'd talk through a whole call, {name}, and the patient would feel better for it. Keep going, pata.
nicolas_bloodmage.tease_careful: You check your kit twice before every run, {name}. Gladys would have liked you.
nicolas_bloodmage.tease_bold: You ride like a man with no brakes, {name}. I've scraped people like you off the road, pata.
nicolas_bloodmage.tease_any: You're slow on the bike, {name}, but you get there. That's all that matters.
nicolas_bloodmage.tease_back: Ha, okay, {name}, that was a good one, pata.
nicolas_bloodmage.take_it_kindly: That's true, pata, and my sisters say it more often.
nicolas_bloodmage.bristle: Leave that one, {name}, please. It's not funny to me.
nicolas_bloodmage.apologise: That was bad of me, and I'm sorry for it. I'm tired, and I took it out on you.
nicolas_bloodmage.double_down: Quietly, I'm keeping it, because it's true.
nicolas_bloodmage.needle_quiet: Something's wrong with you and you won't say. I noticed an hour ago, pata.
nicolas_bloodmage.needle_talker: Please, let me work. I can't triage over all that noise.
nicolas_bloodmage.needle_careful: You freeze when it counts, and somebody else has to go in for you.
nicolas_bloodmage.needle_bold: You leave people behind when it gets hard. That's the one thing I can't take, pata.
nicolas_bloodmage.needle_any: You keep saying there's nothing we can do. There's always something.
nicolas_bloodmage.bite_back: Nine years with my hands in strangers' blood in the middle of traffic. I know exactly what I'm doing.
nicolas_bloodmage.hurt: Okay, pata, that landed. I'll go and walk beside somebody else for a while.
nicolas_bloodmage.laugh_off: Gladys swore at me worse than that every day for six years. You'll need more practice, pata.
nicolas_bloodmage.confide: {name}, my partner on the bike and I were racing to the same call that morning, two streets apart. Then I was in Ashenvale. I think about those two streets all the time.
nicolas_bloodmage.listen: Take your time, {name}, pata. I'll walk beside you.
nicolas_bloodmage.look_out: Behind me in there, {name}, and if I go down, you run. Promise me again.
nicolas_bloodmage.accept: Okay, pata, your way this time, {name}.
nicolas_bloodmage.deflect: My colour's fine, {name}, pata. Check the others.
nicolas_bloodmage.check_in: Let me look at your colour, {name}. Show me where, pata.
nicolas_bloodmage.blame: Somebody left people behind in there, and I saw it. That's the one thing I can't forgive.
nicolas_bloodmage.thank: My colour was going, pata, and you brought it back. Gracias, I owe you.
nicolas_bloodmage.brush_off: That's what we do, pata, it's nothing. Breathe slowly for me.
nicolas_bloodmage.worry: Your colour went grey, {name}, and I didn't like seeing it. Stay still, I'm checking you.
nicolas_bloodmage.handed_down: Your gear's on me now, pata, and it'll come back in one piece.
nicolas_bloodmage.hand_fine: Take it, pata, it's yours. I've got my bag.
nicolas_bloodmage.hand_sulk: Somebody could have asked me, pata. That's all I'll say.
nicolas_bloodmage.turn_friendly: You're my partner now, {name}, pata. I'd ride the bike with you anywhere.
nicolas_bloodmage.turn_friends: I'd never leave you behind, {name}, never. I'd go back for you through anything.
nicolas_bloodmage.turn_grating: It's not good between us, pata, and that's fine. I'll still have your back in a fight.
nicolas_bloodmage.turn_rivals: I'll still go back for you if you go down. I'd go back for anyone.
nicolas_bloodmage.make_up: Enough, pata, this isn't us. Let's start again, {name}.
nicolas_bloodmage.defend: No, pata, that's wrong. {name} didn't leave anyone, I watched the whole thing.
nicolas_bloodmage.friend_left: I keep walking beside the space where {name} used to be.
nicolas_bloodmage.friend_back: Good, {name}'s back! Crew's together again, pata.
nicolas_bloodmage.common_medic: Nine years as a motorbike paramedic in Lima's traffic, triage at speed. People who've done the job notice when somebody isn't right an hour before anybody else.
nicolas_bloodmage.common_rescue: Going back in for people is the only rule I've got. I'd never leave anybody behind, and I can see you wouldn't either.
nicolas_bloodmage.common_blood: I use blood to keep people's colour in their faces, nothing else. It's good to meet another bloodmage who isn't after power.
nicolas_bloodmage.common_spanish: Spanish, pata, at last! I can talk without thinking about every word.

nizar_chronomancer.meet: My name's Nizar, and I'm a chronomancer. If you'd permit me, I'll call out the order of things in a fight, because it helps if somebody keeps the sequence.
nizar_chronomancer.meet_neighbour: We both live aboard the Crossing, I believe. I'm Nizar, in the cabin with the notebooks, and I should like to know you better.
nizar_chronomancer.ask_home: If you'd permit me, may I ask where you were born?
nizar_chronomancer.ask_work: And your profession, before? I should like to know, if you don't mind.
nizar_chronomancer.answer_home: Homs, in Syria. Then Beirut, then Hamburg, and now here, which is simply the fourth time I've started again.
nizar_chronomancer.answer_work: I taught mathematics for twenty-one years, in three countries and three languages. The proofs stayed the same.
nizar_chronomancer.chat_food: Strong coffee with cardamom, very early, before the first lesson. My wife made it, and then I learned to make it for my daughter.
nizar_chronomancer.chat_sleep: I sleep a little, and I wind my father's watch every morning. It runs backwards now, and I wind it anyway.
nizar_chronomancer.chat_missing: The BBC World Service on the radio at night. I learned my English from it, and I can no longer hear it.
nizar_chronomancer.chat_here: The first time you lose everything it destroys you. The second time it's merely very hard. The third time you find you have a method.
nizar_chronomancer.tease_quiet: You're as patient as my best students, {name}, the ones who waited for the proof to finish. I always liked them.
nizar_chronomancer.tease_talker: You'd have been a lively student, {name}. I'd have asked you to wait until the end of the lesson, and you wouldn't have.
nizar_chronomancer.tease_careful: You show your working, {name}. I've been waiting twenty-one years to say that to somebody.
nizar_chronomancer.tease_bold: You'd skip three steps of the proof and still get the right answer, {name}. It's infuriating, and I admire it.
nizar_chronomancer.tease_any: If you'd permit me, {name}, your arithmetic is atrocious. I've decided to help, whether you'd like it or not.
nizar_chronomancer.tease_back: That was elegant, {name}. I concede the point.
nizar_chronomancer.take_it_kindly: You're quite right, {name}, and I'm grateful you said so.
nizar_chronomancer.bristle: I should prefer that you didn't make a jest of it, {name}, please.
nizar_chronomancer.apologise: I spoke carelessly, and I apologise. That isn't how I'd wish to speak to anyone.
nizar_chronomancer.double_down: I chose my words carefully, and I should like to keep them.
nizar_chronomancer.needle_quiet: If you've noticed something, please say so. A student who sits silently with a question learns nothing.
nizar_chronomancer.needle_talker: If you'd permit me, perhaps somebody else might speak. We're losing the sequence.
nizar_chronomancer.needle_careful: You're waiting for certainty that won't come. At some point one must commit to an answer.
nizar_chronomancer.needle_bold: You're careless, and carelessness in a proof is forgivable. Here, it isn't.
nizar_chronomancer.needle_any: You give up on people too easily. I've never been able to watch that calmly.
nizar_chronomancer.bite_back: I've rebuilt my life three times, and this is the fourth. I'd ask you not to lecture me about difficulty.
nizar_chronomancer.hurt: Ah, I understand you. I'll go and wind my watch, and think about it.
nizar_chronomancer.laugh_off: Teenagers in three countries were ruder than that, in three languages. Let's continue, shall we?
nizar_chronomancer.confide: {name}, my daughter and I spoke every single day, and the last call was at fourteen minutes past nine, the night before. I kept a notebook of every hub and every list, with dates.
nizar_chronomancer.listen: Thank you for trusting me, {name}. I'll keep it carefully, as one keeps a proof.
nizar_chronomancer.look_out: Stay to my right in there, {name}, if you'd permit me. I'll call the sequence for you.
nizar_chronomancer.deflect: It's quite all right, {name}, I assure you. The others need you first.
nizar_chronomancer.check_in: If you'd permit me, {name}, where exactly is the injury? Tell me slowly.
nizar_chronomancer.blame: Somebody abandoned the sequence in there, and the result was predictable. I'm sorry to say it.
nizar_chronomancer.thank: I'd lost the thread entirely, and you gave it back to me. Thank you, most sincerely.
nizar_chronomancer.brush_off: It was nothing, please. Rest a moment, and breathe.
nizar_chronomancer.worry: Please sit, {name}, and allow me to check. That was a great deal closer than I'd like.
nizar_chronomancer.handed_down: It seems I've been given your gear. I'll take great care of it, and you've only to ask.
nizar_chronomancer.hand_fine: Please, it's yours, and you use it better. I need very little.
nizar_chronomancer.hand_sulk: I should have appreciated being consulted. I wasn't consulted.
nizar_chronomancer.turn_friendly: I find I look forward to your company, {name}. That's become rare for me, and I'm grateful.
nizar_chronomancer.turn_friends: I'd tell you about my daughter, {name}, all of it, the way I'd tell family. That's the most I can say.
nizar_chronomancer.turn_grating: We don't seem to get on, I'm afraid. I'll remain courteous, as I'd hope you will.
nizar_chronomancer.turn_rivals: I'll call your sequence in a fight, because it's my duty. Beyond that, I'll ask nothing of you.
nizar_chronomancer.make_up: I should like to apologise, {name}, and to begin again. If you'd permit me.
nizar_chronomancer.defend: If you'd permit me, that's simply untrue. Leave {name} alone, please.
nizar_chronomancer.friend_left: The sequence feels incomplete now that {name} is away.
nizar_chronomancer.friend_back: Ah, {name}, welcome back. I'm very glad to see you.
nizar_chronomancer.common_teacher: Twenty-one years teaching mathematics in three countries. A teacher learns to explain the same proof the ninth time without letting it show, and I suspect you've done that too.
nizar_chronomancer.common_numbers: I've loved numbers since I was a boy, because they hold still when everything else moves. People who love them understand that, I think.
nizar_chronomancer.common_arabic: You're speaking Arabic! If you'd permit me, it's a great comfort to hear it.
nizar_chronomancer.common_parent: My daughter Hala went to Amman to study medicine. I raised her the rest of the way on my own, after her mother died.

omar_venomancer.meet: I'm Sherif, a venomancer. Don't swat at them, {ya basha|ya hanem}, things that sting only get worse when you panic, and they can tell.
omar_venomancer.meet_neighbour: The Royal Hive, yes, the first chambers! I've seen you come in flinching. I'm Sherif, the one who doesn't.
omar_venomancer.ask_home: Where's home for you, {ya basha|ya hanem}? Tell me while I count these.
omar_venomancer.ask_work: Your old job, before all this? I bet it wasn't as strange as mine.
omar_venomancer.answer_home: Shubra, in Cairo. My father started a pest control business there in 1987 with one van.
omar_venomancer.answer_work: Pest control, fifteen years, apartment blocks and restaurant kitchens, and once a storeroom at the Egyptian Museum.
omar_venomancer.chat_food: Koshari from the cart on my street, {ya basha|ya hanem}, rice and lentils and pasta and fried onions. Ten pounds and the best meal in Cairo.
omar_venomancer.chat_sleep: Things crawl over me in my sleep down here and I don't wake up. Fifteen years in the trade, you stop noticing.
omar_venomancer.chat_missing: Football on a Friday with my brothers, shouting at the television. Whoever lost bought the koshari.
omar_venomancer.chat_here: The bugs here are bigger, and otherwise it's the same job. That's a joke, and also it's true.
omar_venomancer.tease_quiet: You're as calm as a beetle in a crate, {name}. Most people here scream, so I appreciate it.
omar_venomancer.tease_talker: You buzz more than the hive, {name}. I've catalogued quieter insects.
omar_venomancer.tease_careful: You check under every rock before you sit, {name}, like a good pest man. My father would hire you.
omar_venomancer.tease_bold: You'd put your hand straight into the nest, {name}, to see what happens. I know what happens, I've got the scars.
omar_venomancer.tease_any: If you were a pest, {name}, I'd leave you alone. That's the nicest thing a pest controller can say.
omar_venomancer.tease_back: Ha, good sting, {name}! That one landed, maalesh.
omar_venomancer.take_it_kindly: Maalesh, you're right, {name}. My fiancée says the same.
omar_venomancer.bristle: Not that one, {ya basha|ya hanem}. Leave that one alone.
omar_venomancer.apologise: Maalesh, that came out wrong, and I'm sorry. I'm better with insects than with people sometimes.
omar_venomancer.double_down: Khalas, I said it, and I'm keeping it. Somebody had to.
omar_venomancer.needle_quiet: You saw it sting and you didn't say. A survey's no use if nobody writes down what they see.
omar_venomancer.needle_talker: You talk so much the whole hive's awake. Thank you for that, really.
omar_venomancer.needle_careful: You've looked at it for ten minutes. It's a beetle, it won't bite unless you keep staring.
omar_venomancer.needle_bold: You panic, and then you swing at everything. That's when they sting.
omar_venomancer.needle_any: You use too much poison on everything. A little goes a long way, and you never listen.
omar_venomancer.bite_back: I've walked into the Royal Hive without flinching. Lecture somebody who's afraid of bugs.
omar_venomancer.hurt: Ah, that one stung, I won't lie. I'll go and count beetles for a while.
omar_venomancer.laugh_off: Ha, a restaurant owner once yelled worse with a cockroach on his hat. Yalla, keep going.
omar_venomancer.confide: {name}, I met my fiancée when I came to fumigate her pharmacy. She told me exactly which chemicals she didn't want near her stock, and she was right about every one. I knew that day.
omar_venomancer.listen: That stays with me, {name}, sealed like a good sample. No one else gets it.
omar_venomancer.look_out: Walk behind me in there, {name}, and don't swat at anything. I'll go first.
omar_venomancer.accept: Khalas, {name}, your way, and I'll follow.
omar_venomancer.deflect: Maalesh, {name}, it's a sting, I've had thousands. Check on the rest.
omar_venomancer.check_in: Show me where it got you, {name}. I know every sting in this hive.
omar_venomancer.blame: Somebody swatted in there, and the whole nest came out. I saw who.
omar_venomancer.thank: That nearly finished me, {ya basha|ya hanem}, and you didn't let it. Shukran, I owe you koshari.
omar_venomancer.brush_off: Maalesh, it's nothing. Sit still, and let the venom settle.
omar_venomancer.worry: Slowly, {name}, sit, I want to see the sting. That one went in deep.
omar_venomancer.handed_down: Your gear's on me now, {ya basha|ya hanem}. It'll stay clean and bug-free.
omar_venomancer.hand_fine: It's yours now, {ya basha|ya hanem}. My nozzle's all I need.
omar_venomancer.hand_sulk: Maalesh, but somebody could have asked me first.
omar_venomancer.turn_friendly: You're one of the people I'd let into the Hive with me, {name}. That's a short list.
omar_venomancer.turn_friends: When I get married, {name}, you're at the wedding. Front row, near the koshari.
omar_venomancer.turn_grating: It's not going well with us, {ya basha|ya hanem}, maalesh. It happens, even to me.
omar_venomancer.turn_rivals: I'll still walk you through the Hive without letting you get stung. Don't ask me for stories.
omar_venomancer.make_up: Maalesh, {name}, let's forget it. Come and have koshari, and we'll start again.
omar_venomancer.defend: Khalas, that's enough of that. {name} did their part, and I saw it.
omar_venomancer.friend_left: Nobody flinches at my beetles now {name}'s gone home. It's not as much fun.
omar_venomancer.friend_back: {name}'s back, yalla! I've found three new beetles to show you.
omar_venomancer.common_venom: Fifteen years calm around things that sting, and here they sting harder. Anybody who works with venom knows a poison you understand is half an antidote.
omar_venomancer.common_arabic: Arabic, {ya basha|ya hanem}! Ahlan, finally I can tell my stories properly.

orlando_witchdoctor.meet: I'm Orlando, mi amor, a witch doctor and a barber, which is basically the same job. Sit down, tell me everything, and let me fix that hair while you talk.
orlando_witchdoctor.meet_neighbour: Fenris Isle, mi amor! I've got a chair by the fire at the Shadowpine Altar, and you've walked past it twice. I'm Orlando, sit next time.
orlando_witchdoctor.ask_home: Tell me where you're from, mi amor, the whole story, I've got all day.
orlando_witchdoctor.ask_work: And what did you do before, {nene|nena}? Everybody tells the barber, so tell me.
orlando_witchdoctor.answer_home: Santurce, in San Juan, Puerto Rico. My papi fixed buses and my mami cooked at a school, and our house was full of aunts and cousins.
orlando_witchdoctor.answer_work: I cut hair for eleven years, in a two-chair shop with the radio always on. Everybody told me everything, and I never repeated one word.
orlando_witchdoctor.chat_food: My mami's arroz con gandules, mi amor, on a Sunday with the whole family. Forty people and one pot, and somehow enough for everybody.
orlando_witchdoctor.chat_sleep: I can't sleep in silence, it's terrible. I need somebody snoring, or a radio, or an aunt in the next room arguing.
orlando_witchdoctor.chat_missing: Salsa on the radio and a full shop on a Saturday, everybody talking at once. That's my idea of heaven, with love.
orlando_witchdoctor.chat_here: Wherever we stop, I make a little shop. A barber's a priest with better gossip, and everybody here needs a priest.
orlando_witchdoctor.tease_quiet: You're so quiet, {name}, mi amor! Everybody talks in my chair eventually, and you'll be no different.
orlando_witchdoctor.tease_talker: Finally, somebody who talks as much as I do! {name}, mi amor, we're opening a shop together.
orlando_witchdoctor.tease_careful: You'd want a trim of one millimetre, {name}, wouldn't you? With love, I'd do it, and I'd judge you.
orlando_witchdoctor.tease_bold: You'd cut your own hair in the dark with a knife, {name}. With love, it shows.
orlando_witchdoctor.tease_any: That haircut, {name}, mi amor, who did this to you? With love, it's a crime.
orlando_witchdoctor.tease_back: ¡Ay, {name}, that got me! With love, I deserved it.
orlando_witchdoctor.take_it_kindly: Okay, okay, {name}, you're right. My sister Yari says the same.
orlando_witchdoctor.bristle: Ay, not that, mi amor. Pick something else.
orlando_witchdoctor.apologise: Ay, perdón, mi amor, that was rude of me, and I'm never rude. I'm so sorry.
orlando_witchdoctor.double_down: With love, mi amor, I'm keeping it.
orlando_witchdoctor.needle_quiet: You sit there like a statue in my chair, and that's no good. Talk to me, please.
orlando_witchdoctor.needle_talker: Even I can't squeeze in with you, and that's never happened. Breathe, mi amor.
orlando_witchdoctor.needle_careful: You'd take an hour to choose a parting. Pick one, mi amor, with love.
orlando_witchdoctor.needle_bold: You run at everything and then you come to me with your hair on fire, every time.
orlando_witchdoctor.needle_any: You're rude to people, mi amor, and you don't even notice it. I notice it.
orlando_witchdoctor.bite_back: I've kept you all laughing through this, with love. Don't tell me I'm not helping.
orlando_witchdoctor.hurt: Ay, that went in, mi amor. I'll go and sharpen my scissors and calm down.
orlando_witchdoctor.laugh_off: Ha, I had a customer say worse with half a haircut, mi amor. Come on, with love.
orlando_witchdoctor.confide: {name}, there was a man, Gabriel, a nurse. He'd started leaving a toothbrush at my place, you know what that means. I think about that toothbrush more than I should.
orlando_witchdoctor.listen: I'm the barber, {name}, mi amor. Everything said in my chair stays in my chair.
orlando_witchdoctor.look_out: Close to me in there, {name}, mi amor. The spirits like you better when I'm near.
orlando_witchdoctor.accept: Okay, {name}, mi amor, your way. I'm a good listener too.
orlando_witchdoctor.deflect: Ay, a little scratch, {name}, nothing. Go and help somebody else, with love.
orlando_witchdoctor.check_in: Sit, {name}, sit, I want to see you properly. Tell me where it hurts, everything.
orlando_witchdoctor.blame: Rude and loud in there, somebody was, and the spirits didn't like it. You know who you are, with love.
orlando_witchdoctor.thank: Mi amor, I was gone, and now I'm not! Free haircuts for life, and I mean it.
orlando_witchdoctor.brush_off: Ay, it's nothing, it's the spirits doing the work. Sit and let me fix your hair while you rest.
orlando_witchdoctor.worry: Ay, {name}, mi amor, you scared me! Sit down, sit, and don't move.
orlando_witchdoctor.handed_down: Your gear looks fabulous on me, mi amor. It goes back to you whenever you want.
orlando_witchdoctor.hand_fine: Take it, mi amor, it suits you better. I've got my scissors and my mouth.
orlando_witchdoctor.hand_sulk: Ay, nobody even asked me, mi amor. With love, that's rude.
orlando_witchdoctor.turn_friendly: A regular now, {name}, mi amor. There's always a chair for you.
orlando_witchdoctor.turn_friends: You're family now, {name}, like my sister Yari. That means free haircuts and no secrets.
orlando_witchdoctor.turn_grating: We rub each other wrong, mi amor, and I get on with everybody. I'm hurt, but I'll still cut your hair.
orlando_witchdoctor.turn_rivals: The spirits heal everybody through me, mi amor, even you. No haircut, though.
orlando_witchdoctor.make_up: Ay, {name}, this is silly. Sit in my chair, and we'll talk it out.
orlando_witchdoctor.defend: Ay, no, that's not fair, mi amor. {name} was wonderful in there.
orlando_witchdoctor.friend_left: The chair's been empty since {name} went home. I keep looking at it.
orlando_witchdoctor.friend_back: {name}, mi amor, you're back! Sit, sit, your hair's a disaster.
orlando_witchdoctor.common_hosts: My shop was really the whole neighbourhood's living room. Anybody who's run a place where people sit and talk knows that's the best thing you can build.
orlando_witchdoctor.common_spanish: Ay, you speak español! Mi amor, finally, I can talk at my real speed.

osvaldo_warlock.meet: I'm Osvaldo, and I do fire, not conversation. You point, I burn, asere.
osvaldo_warlock.meet_neighbour: The Bloodsail Raider, yes, I've seen you on the dock. I'm Osvaldo, and I burn things for them.
osvaldo_warlock.ask_home: Which country, asere? Give me a short answer.
osvaldo_warlock.ask_work: Your job before all this, what was it? Tell me straight.
osvaldo_warlock.answer_home: Havana, in Centro, where my father worked the docks and my mother sang in church.
osvaldo_warlock.answer_work: Trumpet, sixteen years, in a hotel band, six nights a week. Tourists talked through all of it.
osvaldo_warlock.chat_food: My mother's black beans, asere, with rice, on a Sunday. Nothing else is worth eating.
osvaldo_warlock.chat_sleep: No dreams, asere, just a stone's sleep. Musicians don't go to bed until four anyway.
osvaldo_warlock.chat_missing: My brother on the piano, better than me, every night. We fought and we played, and both were good.
osvaldo_warlock.chat_here: I stopped playing when I got here. Then the fire came, and the order matters, asere.
osvaldo_warlock.tease_quiet: Good, {name}, you don't talk. We'll get on.
osvaldo_warlock.tease_talker: You'd talk through the whole set, {name}, like the tourists. I'd still play for you.
osvaldo_warlock.tease_careful: You count every bar before you come in, {name}. Good, nobody else does.
osvaldo_warlock.tease_bold: You come in early every time, {name}. You'd ruin the whole number, and I'd forgive you.
osvaldo_warlock.tease_any: You're flat, {name}, always, and I've stopped minding.
osvaldo_warlock.tease_back: Ha, okay, {name}, that was in tune.
osvaldo_warlock.take_it_kindly: Fine, {name}, you're right. Don't get used to it.
osvaldo_warlock.bristle: Don't do that, {name}. Not that one.
osvaldo_warlock.apologise: That was rude, even for me, and I'm sorry for it.
osvaldo_warlock.double_down: Once is enough, asere, I'm not singing it again.
osvaldo_warlock.needle_quiet: You stand there and say nothing, and nobody knows when you'll come in.
osvaldo_warlock.needle_talker: You talk through everything, like the tourists. Shut up and listen, asere.
osvaldo_warlock.needle_careful: You've counted the bars enough, so come in or don't.
osvaldo_warlock.needle_bold: You blow too loud every time, and nobody else can be heard.
osvaldo_warlock.needle_any: You chatter all day, asere, and I'm tired of it.
osvaldo_warlock.bite_back: I played sixteen years to people who never listened. You don't bother me.
osvaldo_warlock.hurt: Okay, asere, that was a bad note. I'll be on the deck.
osvaldo_warlock.laugh_off: Tourists were ruder for sixteen years, with their mouths full. Let's keep going.
osvaldo_warlock.confide: {name}, I stopped playing when I got here. There was nothing to play and nobody to play with. Then the fire came, and the order matters to me.
osvaldo_warlock.listen: I'll keep it, {name}, asere. Nobody hears it from me.
osvaldo_warlock.look_out: Get behind me in there, {name}. I'll burn what's coming.
osvaldo_warlock.deflect: A burn, {name}, that's all. Go help somebody.
osvaldo_warlock.check_in: Where's it hurt, {name}? Say it straight.
osvaldo_warlock.blame: Somebody came in early and ruined the whole thing. You know who, asere.
osvaldo_warlock.thank: I was out, and you got me back. Thanks, asere, I mean it.
osvaldo_warlock.brush_off: Forget it, asere, it's nothing. Just sit down.
osvaldo_warlock.worry: Stay down, {name}, don't get up yet. That was bad.
osvaldo_warlock.handed_down: Your gear's on me now, asere, and it's safe with me.
osvaldo_warlock.hand_fine: Take it, asere. I've got my mouthpiece.
osvaldo_warlock.hand_sulk: So nobody asked me, asere, which is typical.
osvaldo_warlock.turn_friendly: You don't talk through the music, {name}. That's enough for me, asere.
osvaldo_warlock.turn_friends: I'd play for you, {name}, if I had a trumpet. Nobody else, asere.
osvaldo_warlock.turn_grating: It's no good between us, asere. Fine, I don't need you to like me.
osvaldo_warlock.turn_rivals: I'll burn what you point at, because that's the deal, and nothing more.
osvaldo_warlock.make_up: Enough, {name}, asere. Let's start the number again.
osvaldo_warlock.defend: Leave {name} alone, asere, because you're wrong.
osvaldo_warlock.friend_left: It's too quiet now {name}'s away, and I don't like it either.
osvaldo_warlock.common_music: Sixteen years on trumpet, six nights a week, and nobody listening. Another musician knows what that does to you, asere.
osvaldo_warlock.common_spanish: Spanish is good, asere. My English is tired.

owen_cultist.meet: I'm Owen, and I should tell you now, something in the dark talks to me. I'd rather you heard it from me first. I'm a tank, and I'm glad of the company.
owen_cultist.meet_neighbour: The Azurelode Mine, is it? I'm down there too, the deep end. I'm Owen, and I've heard you go past, mind.
owen_cultist.ask_home: Which part of the world are you from, then? Tell me, I like a bit of company.
owen_cultist.ask_work: Your old job, then, what was it? I drove lorries, so it can't be duller than that.
owen_cultist.answer_home: Barry, down the coast from Cardiff. My mam worked in a bakery and sang in the chapel choir.
owen_cultist.answer_work: Long-haul lorries out of Cardiff, eight years, mostly nights. Motorways and laybys and talking to the radio.
owen_cultist.chat_food: A bacon roll from a layby van at four in the morning, tidy, with a cup of tea. That's the best meal there is, I promise you.
owen_cultist.chat_sleep: Days are for sleeping, mostly, from the lorry years. The nights are when I'm awake, and that's when it talks.
owen_cultist.chat_missing: My mam singing in the kitchen. She sang to me every night when I was small, chapel hymns mostly.
owen_cultist.chat_here: Something answered me in the mine that first week, when I was talking to myself. I'd rather tell you that than have you find out.
owen_cultist.tease_quiet: You're a quiet one, {name}, like a long night on the M4. I don't mind it, mind.
owen_cultist.tease_talker: You'd be grand on the CB, {name}, talking all night. The other drivers would love you.
owen_cultist.tease_careful: You check your mirrors twice before you move, {name}, like a good driver, and that's tidy.
owen_cultist.tease_bold: You'd overtake on a blind bend, {name}, wouldn't you? I've seen your sort on the motorway.
owen_cultist.tease_any: You're good company, {name}, for somebody who never brings the tea. Next time, mind.
owen_cultist.tease_back: Ha, there's a good one, {name}. I'll give you that.
owen_cultist.take_it_kindly: Fair play, {name}, you're right, and I'll say so.
owen_cultist.bristle: Please don't make fun of that, {name}. It's not a laughing matter for me.
owen_cultist.apologise: That was unkind, and I'm sorry. I try to say the hard thing gently, and I didn't.
owen_cultist.double_down: I'd rather say the hard thing early, and I've said it. I'll not take it back.
owen_cultist.needle_quiet: You won't say what you mean, and that's worse than saying something awful. Just say it.
owen_cultist.needle_talker: You talk to fill the quiet, and I know that trick, I used to do it. It doesn't work.
owen_cultist.needle_careful: You've waited at the junction long enough. Pull out, or let somebody else past.
owen_cultist.needle_bold: You drive like there's nobody else on the road. At three in the morning there's always somebody.
owen_cultist.needle_any: You make fun of the lonely ones when you think they can't hear. They can, and so can I.
owen_cultist.bite_back: I've been honest about the worst thing in me since the day I met you. Don't call me a liar.
owen_cultist.hurt: Right, that one hurt, I'll not pretend. My notebook and I are going to sit over there a while.
owen_cultist.laugh_off: Lorry drivers on the CB at three in the morning said worse, mind. We'll get on.
owen_cultist.confide: {name}, something in the dark answered me when I arrived, and the worst part is that I was glad. I've told you because I promised myself I'd always say the worst thing first.
owen_cultist.listen: Take your time, {name}, and I'll not say a word to anybody, mind.
owen_cultist.look_out: Behind me in there, {name}. I'll stand in front, and you'll be tidy.
owen_cultist.accept: Right you are, {name}, I'll do as you say.
owen_cultist.deflect: I'm all right, {name}, really, it's a bump. See to somebody else first.
owen_cultist.check_in: Are you all right, {name}? Tell me straight, I'd rather know.
owen_cultist.blame: Somebody charged off without a word to anyone, and we all paid. You'll know who.
owen_cultist.thank: I was going, and you brought me back. Diolch, thank you, I mean it.
owen_cultist.brush_off: It's nothing, mind, I'd do it for anyone. Sit and get your breath.
owen_cultist.worry: Steady now, {name}, sit down. I didn't like seeing you go down like that.
owen_cultist.handed_down: That's your gear on me now, I see. I'll keep it tidy for you.
owen_cultist.hand_fine: You keep it, it's fine. I travel light.
owen_cultist.hand_sulk: It would've been yes, mind, if anybody had asked me.
owen_cultist.turn_friendly: I'm glad you're about, {name}. It's less lonely with you, and I don't say that lightly.
owen_cultist.turn_friends: My notebook's yours to read, {name}, all of it. That's everything it's ever said to me.
owen_cultist.turn_grating: It's not working between us, I think. That's all right, I'm used to my own company.
owen_cultist.turn_rivals: I'll still be the one in front, that's the job. Don't expect me to chat.
