owen_cultist.make_up: Let's stop this, {name}, it's no good for either of us. Can we begin again?
owen_cultist.defend: No, that's not fair, and it's not true. Leave {name} be, now.
owen_cultist.friend_left: It's lonely again with {name} away. I knew it would be.
owen_cultist.friend_back: Back again, {name}, tidy. I've missed the company, mind.
owen_cultist.common_the_dark: Something in the dark answered me when I arrived, and I was glad. You've heard something too, I think, and you know how that feels.
owen_cultist.common_road: Eight years of long-haul nights on the M4, talking to the radio. People who've driven for a living know the road's never really empty.
owen_cultist.common_night_work: Eight years of nights, in a cab, through the small hours. I'm still most awake when everybody else is asleep, and that's when it talks.
owen_cultist.common_welsh: Shwmae, you're Welsh! Duw, it's good to hear a proper voice. Where from, then?

pasang_primalist.meet: I'm Pasang, a mountain guide, and a primalist here. I set the pace, and the pace is slow.
pasang_primalist.meet_neighbour: The Aspen country, yes, I'm in the stone hut up the slope. I'm Pasang, and I've watched you climb too fast.
pasang_primalist.ask_home: Which mountains are yours? Everybody's got some, even if they're small.
pasang_primalist.ask_work: Before this, what did you carry? Everyone carries something.
pasang_primalist.answer_home: Khumjung, in the Solukhumbu, in Nepal. Almost every family there works on the big mountains.
pasang_primalist.answer_work: Mountain guide, nineteen seasons above eight thousand metres, carrying for people who went home famous.
pasang_primalist.chat_food: Butter tea, very salty, in the morning, and dal bhat at night. The mountain gives you an appetite, and that's all you need.
pasang_primalist.chat_sleep: High up, I sleep fine. It's the low ground that keeps me awake, the air's too thick.
pasang_primalist.chat_missing: A clear dawn on the mountain, before anyone's awake, with the whole range pink. Nothing here is that quiet.
pasang_primalist.chat_here: The spirits of stone and cold talk to me here. I treat it like a work arrangement, not a mystery.
pasang_primalist.tease_quiet: You're quiet like a good porter, {name}. You carry it and you don't complain, and I approve.
pasang_primalist.tease_talker: You'd talk all the way to the summit, {name}, and run out of breath at base camp.
pasang_primalist.tease_careful: You test every step on the ice, {name}. Good, that's why you're still alive.
pasang_primalist.tease_bold: You'd climb without a rope to save time, {name}. I've carried people like you down, and they were heavy.
pasang_primalist.tease_any: It's your day four, {name}, and you still have manners. That's rare, and I've noticed.
pasang_primalist.tease_back: Ha, that's good, {name}. Day four and you've still got jokes.
pasang_primalist.bristle: Please don't, {name}. That's not one for laughing.
pasang_primalist.apologise: I spoke badly, and I'm sorry for it. Even guides lose their manners on day four.
pasang_primalist.double_down: On the mountain or at the bottom, it's the same answer. I meant it.
pasang_primalist.needle_quiet: You feel sick and you don't say. That's how people die on day four.
pasang_primalist.needle_talker: You're wasting breath, and you'll need it higher up. Please, a little quiet.
pasang_primalist.needle_careful: At every step you stop, and the weather's turning. Some days you have to go.
pasang_primalist.needle_bold: You rush the mountain like it owes you something. It doesn't, and it'll collect.
pasang_primalist.needle_any: You think the mountain's something to conquer. It isn't, and you'll find out.
pasang_primalist.bite_back: I've carried loads above eight thousand metres nineteen times. I know the mountain.
pasang_primalist.hurt: Okay, I heard that. I'll go ahead and set the pace for a while.
pasang_primalist.laugh_off: Famous people were ruder to me on day four, every season. I'm still here, and some of them aren't.
pasang_primalist.confide: {name}, two of my cousins died doing this work, Nima on the icefall and Lhakpa on Makalu. I keep their names to myself, mostly. Now you've got them too.
pasang_primalist.listen: Slowly, {name}, there's no hurry up here.
pasang_primalist.look_out: Rope up behind me in there, {name}. I'll set the pace, and you'll be fine.
pasang_primalist.accept: Your pace today, {name}, and I'll follow it.
pasang_primalist.deflect: I'm a porter, {name}, it's nothing. Look to the others.
pasang_primalist.check_in: Sit, {name}, and tell me the truth. Where's the injury?
pasang_primalist.blame: Somebody rushed the climb in there, and the mountain collected. You know who.
pasang_primalist.thank: I was slipping, and you held the rope. I'll remember that on every mountain.
pasang_primalist.brush_off: It's nothing, that's what the rope's for. Sit, breathe slowly.
pasang_primalist.worry: Sit, {name}, sit, and drink this. You've gone a bad colour.
pasang_primalist.handed_down: You carried this before me. I'll carry it carefully now.
pasang_primalist.hand_fine: You keep it, I carry light. That's the first rule.
pasang_primalist.hand_sulk: A porter's asked before he's loaded. Nobody asked me.
pasang_primalist.turn_friendly: You've still got your manners on day four, {name}. That's how I choose friends.
pasang_primalist.turn_friends: I'd rope up with you, {name}, on any mountain. I don't say that about anyone.
pasang_primalist.turn_grating: We don't climb well together. I'll go ahead, and you can follow at your pace.
pasang_primalist.turn_rivals: I'll guide you because I'm the guide. A guide doesn't have to like the client.
pasang_primalist.make_up: Enough of this, {name}. Let's rope up again and start from the bottom.
pasang_primalist.defend: That's not fair, and it isn't true. Leave {name} alone.
pasang_primalist.friend_left: {name}'s gone down for a while. The slope's quieter, and I notice.
pasang_primalist.friend_back: Good, {name}, you came back up. The pace is still slow.
pasang_primalist.common_mountains: Nineteen seasons above eight thousand metres, and I still think the mountains are the best place in the world. Mountain people know high ground changes a person.

pavlo_knight.meet: I'm Pavlo, and I hold lines. Tell me where and for how long, and I'll stay there exactly that long.
pavlo_knight.meet_neighbour: The Sepulcher, yes, I hold the road out of it. I'm Pavlo, and I think you've walked past my wall a few times.
pavlo_knight.ask_home: Which town raised you? I like to place people, it's an old habit.
pavlo_knight.ask_work: Your profession before all this, may I ask? I'm curious what people were for.
pavlo_knight.answer_home: Lviv, in Ukraine. My father drove a tram and my mother was a librarian.
pavlo_knight.answer_work: History teacher, sixteen years, to fourteen-year-olds who'd rather be anywhere else. Before that, a museum.
pavlo_knight.chat_food: Varenyky with sour cream, and strong tea from my wife's old flask. Simple food, eaten slowly.
pavlo_knight.chat_sleep: Teachers sleep badly in September and well in July. Here it's always September.
pavlo_knight.chat_missing: A good question from a child, the kind that makes the whole room go quiet. I'd teach a hundred bad lessons for one of those.
pavlo_knight.chat_here: Nobody here needs a history teacher. It took me most of three years to stop being wounded by that.
pavlo_knight.tease_quiet: You'd sit at the back of my class, {name}, and say nothing, and get the best mark. I always noticed the quiet ones.
pavlo_knight.tease_talker: You'd have been sent to the corridor twice a week, {name}. I'd have missed you every time.
pavlo_knight.tease_careful: You read the whole question before you answer, {name}. You've no idea how rare that is.
pavlo_knight.tease_bold: You'd answer before I'd finished the question, {name}, and be wrong, and be charming about it.
pavlo_knight.tease_any: If you were a war, {name}, I'd teach you every spring. You're very repetitive.
pavlo_knight.tease_back: Full marks for that one, {name}, well done.
pavlo_knight.take_it_kindly: You're right, {name}, and a good teacher admits it.
pavlo_knight.bristle: That one's not for joking, {name}, if you don't mind.
pavlo_knight.apologise: That was unworthy of me, and I'm sorry. I'd have sent a pupil out for less.
pavlo_knight.double_down: That stands, I'm afraid. I'd say it to the whole class.
pavlo_knight.needle_quiet: If you know the answer, put your hand up. Sitting there with it helps nobody.
pavlo_knight.needle_talker: Quiet at the back, please. Some of us are trying to hold a line.
pavlo_knight.needle_careful: Three checks and it hasn't changed. History doesn't wait for anybody.
pavlo_knight.needle_bold: You charge in like every war I ever taught, and it ends like every war I ever taught.
pavlo_knight.needle_any: You're certain without knowing anything, and that's what frightens me most in people.
pavlo_knight.bite_back: I held a room of fourteen-year-olds together for sixteen years. You're not harder than that.
pavlo_knight.hurt: That's fair, I think, and it stings. I'll go and stand on the wall for a while.
pavlo_knight.laugh_off: Fourteen-year-olds were crueller to me every morning for sixteen years. I've heard it all, and I'm still here.
pavlo_knight.confide: {name}, my son and I argued about history at the dinner table every night. Of everything, that's what I'd ask to have back.
pavlo_knight.listen: Teachers learn to wait for the end of the sentence, {name}, so go on, I'm here.
pavlo_knight.look_out: Behind the shield, {name}, and hold your ground. I'll tell you when to move.
pavlo_knight.accept: Where you want me, {name}, I'll hold.
pavlo_knight.deflect: It's a bruise, {name}, nothing more. Others need you more than I do.
pavlo_knight.check_in: Sit, {name}, and tell me in order. What hit you, and where?
pavlo_knight.blame: Somebody broke the line in there, and everything after it was predictable. I've taught it a hundred times.
pavlo_knight.thank: My line broke there, and you held it for me. I'm in your debt.
pavlo_knight.brush_off: It's what a line is for, holding. Sit and catch your breath.
pavlo_knight.worry: That was much too close, {name}. Sit behind the wall a while, please.
pavlo_knight.handed_down: Yours, if I remember right, and now on me. You'll have it back.
pavlo_knight.hand_fine: Of more use to you than me, so it's yours. A teacher needs very little.
pavlo_knight.hand_sulk: I'd have liked to be asked. Manners are the first lesson, and the last.
pavlo_knight.turn_friendly: I'm glad of your company, {name}. You'd have been one of my good ones.
pavlo_knight.turn_friends: I'd teach you anything I know, {name}, and I know a great deal of useless history.
pavlo_knight.turn_grating: We don't sit well together, you and I. I'll keep the peace, as I always did in class.
pavlo_knight.turn_rivals: The line needs holding, so I'll hold it in front of you, and that's all.
pavlo_knight.make_up: I owe you an apology, {name}, and a teacher should be quick to give one. I'm sorry for it.
pavlo_knight.defend: That's simply untrue, and unkind. Leave {name} alone.
pavlo_knight.friend_left: There's nobody to argue history with while {name}'s away.
pavlo_knight.friend_back: Take your place, {name}, welcome back, and let's begin.
pavlo_knight.common_teacher: Sixteen years standing in front of a room that would rather be anywhere else. Anybody who's taught knows you keep it together by presence alone.
pavlo_knight.common_ukrainian: Ukrainian, like me! Tell me which city. I'm from Lviv, and I'll tell you everything that's wrong with Kyiv.
pavlo_knight.common_parent: My son Andriy was studying engineering in Kraków. We argued about history at dinner every night, and he usually won.

pieter_guardian.meet: I'm Pieter, and I'll take the hits, because I'm the one wearing the armour. Now check your straps before we go anywhere.
pieter_guardian.meet_neighbour: Northern Tanaris, ja, the dig sites. I'm Pieter, with the clipboard, and I've checked your straps from a distance.
pieter_guardian.ask_home: Where were you raised, then? It's good to know who I'm standing in front of.
pieter_guardian.ask_work: What line of work were you in? Tell me before I see how you handle a harness.
pieter_guardian.answer_home: Pretoria, born and raised, then twenty-eight years in Rotterdam. My wife's Dutch.
pieter_guardian.answer_work: Port safety officer, twenty-eight years. Clipboard, hard hat, and the most tedious man on the dock, ja.
pieter_guardian.chat_food: A braai on a Sunday, boerewors and pap, with a cold beer. And my wife's stamppot, which I'll defend to the death.
pieter_guardian.chat_sleep: Seven hours, ja, after a safety check of the tent. You'd be amazed what crawls in.
pieter_guardian.chat_missing: Rugby on a Saturday, with my girls shouting at the ref louder than me. They learned it from me.
pieter_guardian.chat_here: A world with monsters in it needs a safety man more than a port does. I took to this place straight away, and I'm a bit ashamed of that.
pieter_guardian.tease_quiet: You'd make a good safety officer, {name}. Nobody'd notice you until it mattered.
pieter_guardian.tease_talker: Lekker, {name}, you never stop talking. At least I always know where you are.
pieter_guardian.tease_careful: Harness, then harness again, {name}. Ja, you're my favourite person on this dig.
pieter_guardian.tease_bold: Jislaaik, {name}, you'd walk under a crane without looking up. I've filled in forms about people like you.
pieter_guardian.tease_any: Your straps are a disgrace, {name}, every morning. I check them anyway, and I always will.
pieter_guardian.tease_back: Ha, lekker, {name}, that one got through my guard.
pieter_guardian.take_it_kindly: Ja, fair enough, {name}. Anneke would tell you the same.
pieter_guardian.apologise: I was rude there, ja, and I'm sorry for it. I'm gruff, but I'm not usually rude.
pieter_guardian.double_down: Nee, it stands. A safety man doesn't take back a warning.
pieter_guardian.needle_quiet: A loose strap nobody reports is how small things become funerals. Say what you see.
pieter_guardian.needle_talker: Less talking, more checking, please. The pit doesn't care how interesting you are.
pieter_guardian.needle_careful: Enough checking, ja. Now trust the harness and go.
pieter_guardian.needle_bold: You're a man in a hurry, and I've buried men in a hurry. You need to slow down.
pieter_guardian.needle_any: You keep saying accidents happen. They don't happen, they're caused, and you cause them.
pieter_guardian.bite_back: Twenty-eight years of nobody dying on my dock. Lecture me when you've done the same.
pieter_guardian.hurt: Ja, okay, that one hit. I'll go and check some straps for a while.
pieter_guardian.laugh_off: Ha, I've been shouted at by thousands of men in a hurry. You'll have to queue.
pieter_guardian.confide: {name}, I've pulled nine men out of those pits in three years. I keep the number because somebody should. I don't talk about the ones I didn't.
pieter_guardian.listen: Ja, {name}, I'm listening. That stays off the clipboard.
pieter_guardian.look_out: Get behind the armour, {name}, ja? That's arithmetic, not courage.
pieter_guardian.accept: Ja, {name}, your plan. Check your straps first, mind.
pieter_guardian.deflect: A dent, {name}, that's what the armour's for. Check the others.
pieter_guardian.check_in: Ja, {name}, where's the damage? Tell me straight, I've filled in a lot of forms.
pieter_guardian.blame: Somebody didn't check before they went in, ja. That's how it always starts.
pieter_guardian.thank: The armour wasn't enough there, and you were. Dankie, thank you.
pieter_guardian.brush_off: Ag, it's nothing, ja. Sit, and let me check your straps while you're down.
pieter_guardian.worry: Jislaaik, {name}, that was close. Sit down and don't move till I've looked.
pieter_guardian.handed_down: That's your gear on me now, ja. I'll keep it inspected.
pieter_guardian.hand_fine: Ja, you keep it, it's better on you. I've got my father's knife.
pieter_guardian.hand_sulk: There's a procedure, ja, and it starts with asking, and nobody asked.
pieter_guardian.turn_friendly: You check your straps without being told now, {name}. That's a friend, as far as I'm concerned.
pieter_guardian.turn_friends: I'd trust you to rig my harness, {name}. I've never said that to anybody but my father.
pieter_guardian.turn_grating: We don't see eye to eye, ja. I'll keep you safe anyway, that's the job.
pieter_guardian.turn_rivals: The armour's on me, so I take the hits in front of you. Arithmetic, not friendship.
pieter_guardian.make_up: Ag, {name}, this nonsense has gone on long enough. Let's start again, ja?
pieter_guardian.defend: Nee, that's wrong, and I was watching. Back off from {name}.
pieter_guardian.friend_left: Nobody's here to tease about their straps since {name} went home.
pieter_guardian.friend_back: Straps first, {name}, then we talk. Welcome back, ja.
pieter_guardian.common_parent: Two girls, Lotte and Sanne, grown now, in Rotterdam. They shout at the rugby louder than me.
pieter_guardian.common_docks: Twenty-eight years on the docks at Rotterdam. Anybody who's worked a port knows the danger's always the thing nobody's watching.

ramiro_primalist.meet: I'm Ramiro, a primalist, and I listen to the rock. If I tell you to stop and listen, stop, because the mountain always talks before it moves.
ramiro_primalist.meet_neighbour: Onyxhollow, yes, the mining quarter. I'm Ramiro, and I've heard you on the ladders, {compadre|comadre}.
ramiro_primalist.ask_home: Your town, {compadre|comadre}, which one is it? Tell me about the ground there.
ramiro_primalist.ask_work: And your work, before? A man knows a lot about you from your hands.
ramiro_primalist.answer_home: Potosí, in Bolivia, under the Cerro Rico, the silver mountain.
ramiro_primalist.answer_work: I mined silver for twenty years, like my father and grandfather. Twelve-hour shifts, and an offering to El Tío every Friday.
ramiro_primalist.chat_food: Salteñas in the morning before a shift, {compadre|comadre}, and coca tea. That's how a miner starts the day.
ramiro_primalist.chat_sleep: Underground I sleep like the dead, pues. Up here, with all this sky, I lie awake.
ramiro_primalist.chat_missing: A football match on the radio after a shift, with the whole shift listening. Nobody here knows the teams.
ramiro_primalist.chat_here: The first stone that lifted itself into my hand frightened me badly. I'm used to it now, mostly.
ramiro_primalist.tease_quiet: You listen like a good miner, {name}. You hear the rock before the rest of us.
ramiro_primalist.tease_talker: So much talk, {name}, {compadre|comadre}, and the rock can't get a word in.
ramiro_primalist.tease_careful: You tap the roof before you walk under it, {name}. My father would have liked you.
ramiro_primalist.tease_bold: You'd walk into a drift without timber, {name}. I've dug people like you out, pues.
ramiro_primalist.tease_any: You're good stone, {name}, mostly. A few cracks, but you hold.
ramiro_primalist.tease_back: Ya, that's good, {name}. The rock laughed too.
ramiro_primalist.take_it_kindly: That's so, {name}, and there's no arguing with true things.
ramiro_primalist.bristle: No, {compadre|comadre}, not that. Some things you don't joke about underground.
ramiro_primalist.apologise: My mouth ran ahead of me, and I'm sorry for it. A miner should guard his mouth like his lamp.
ramiro_primalist.double_down: Once, and the rock heard it, so I won't take it back.
ramiro_primalist.needle_quiet: You heard the rock and said nothing. Down there, that kills a whole shift.
ramiro_primalist.needle_talker: Stop talking, please, and listen. The mountain's trying to warn us.
ramiro_primalist.needle_careful: You've tapped that wall ten times. Either it holds or it doesn't, so decide.
ramiro_primalist.needle_bold: You don't listen, and you go in anyway. That's how careless miners die.
ramiro_primalist.needle_any: You think the earth is dead. It isn't, and it's listening to you.
ramiro_primalist.bite_back: I've kept a shift alive under a mountain for twenty years. You can keep your lessons.
ramiro_primalist.hurt: Ya, that one went deep, {compadre|comadre}. I'll go and sit with the stone a while.
ramiro_primalist.laugh_off: The cooperative was ruder than that every payday, pues, and never paid on time.
ramiro_primalist.confide: {name}, my daughter Maribel wanted to be a geologist. I was saving so she'd study the mountain instead of dying in it. That's what I carry.
ramiro_primalist.listen: Ya, {name}, slowly, like the rock settling. I'm listening to you.
ramiro_primalist.look_out: Walk where I walk in there, {name}, and when I say listen, listen.
ramiro_primalist.accept: Ya, {name}, your way, and I'll follow.
ramiro_primalist.deflect: A rock fall, {name}, a small one. Check the others first.
ramiro_primalist.check_in: Stop, {name}, and let me see. Where did the stone hit you?
ramiro_primalist.blame: Somebody didn't listen in there, and the mountain came down on all of us.
ramiro_primalist.thank: The rock nearly had me, and you pulled me out. Gracias, {compadre|comadre}, from my heart.
ramiro_primalist.brush_off: It's nothing, pues, that's what a shift is for. Breathe slowly now.
ramiro_primalist.worry: Ya, {name}, that was bad. Sit down, and let the dust settle.
ramiro_primalist.handed_down: I've been given your gear, {compadre|comadre}. I'll keep it like my lamp.
ramiro_primalist.hand_fine: You keep it, pues. I mined twenty years with less.
ramiro_primalist.hand_sulk: A miner asks before he takes another man's tools, and nobody asked.
ramiro_primalist.turn_friendly: You're part of my shift now, {name}. That means something, underground.
ramiro_primalist.turn_friends: I'd go down any shaft with you, {name}. That's the most a miner can say.
ramiro_primalist.turn_grating: We don't dig well together, {compadre|comadre}. I'll keep to my own drift.
ramiro_primalist.turn_rivals: I'll still listen to the rock for you, because I listen for everybody, and nothing more.
ramiro_primalist.make_up: Enough of this, {name}, {compadre|comadre}. Let's leave an offering and start again.
ramiro_primalist.defend: No, that's wrong, and I was there. Leave {name} be.
ramiro_primalist.friend_left: {name} went up for a while, and the tunnels feel emptier.
ramiro_primalist.friend_back: Back down with us, {name}, good. The rock's quiet today.
ramiro_primalist.common_stone: Twenty years in the silver mountain, listening to the rock. Anybody who's worked stone knows it talks before it moves.
ramiro_primalist.common_mountains: I grew up under the Cerro Rico, high up, where the air's thin. Mountain people know the mountain decides, not us.
ramiro_primalist.common_spanish: Spanish, {compadre|comadre}, good! Now I can say it properly.
ramiro_primalist.common_parent: Two girls, Maribel and Sonia. Maribel wanted to be a geologist, and I was saving for it.

ratih_ranger.meet: I'm Ratih, a ranger. Walk quieter, please, and don't thank me for things.
ratih_ranger.meet_neighbour: The Shimmering Flats, yes, I'm on the rise. I'm Ratih, and I've watched you cross the salt.
ratih_ranger.ask_home: Your country, which one? You can keep it short.
ratih_ranger.ask_work: Your work before all this, what was it? I'd like to know.
ratih_ranger.answer_home: Riau, in Sumatra, in Indonesia. My father tapped rubber at the edge of the forest.
ratih_ranger.answer_work: Forest ranger, fifteen years, mostly alone. Poachers and illegal loggers, and a government that paid for the uniform.
ratih_ranger.chat_food: Rendang, cooked slowly all day, and rice. My mother made it for every holiday, and I've never had better.
ratih_ranger.chat_sleep: I sleep light, always. In the forest you wake for the one sound that's wrong.
ratih_ranger.chat_missing: Birdsong at dawn in the forest, all of it at once. Out here on the salt there's nothing.
ratih_ranger.chat_here: People here thank me, and I find it strange. It makes me want things I've never wanted.
ratih_ranger.tease_quiet: You walk quietly, {name}, like a ranger. I approve, and I don't approve of many.
ratih_ranger.tease_talker: Everything in the forest would hear you coming, {name}. It would hear you leaving too.
ratih_ranger.tease_careful: You look before you step, {name}. That's how rangers stay alive.
ratih_ranger.tease_bold: You'd walk into a snare to see if it worked, {name}. I promise you it works.
ratih_ranger.tease_any: You're less noisy than you were, {name}, and that's progress.
ratih_ranger.tease_back: That was good, {name}, I'll allow it.
ratih_ranger.take_it_kindly: Right, {name}, and I won't pretend otherwise.
ratih_ranger.bristle: Leave that, {name}, please. I don't like it.
ratih_ranger.apologise: That was sharp of me, and I'm sorry. I'm not used to people.
ratih_ranger.double_down: Then and now, I mean it.
ratih_ranger.needle_quiet: You saw the wrong thing and kept it to yourself. That's how poachers get away.
ratih_ranger.needle_talker: You're very loud, all the time. Nothing out here will come near us.
ratih_ranger.needle_careful: You've watched it long enough to lose it. Move, or it's gone.
ratih_ranger.needle_bold: You walk without looking, every single time. One day the ground will look for you.
ratih_ranger.needle_any: You make so much noise, and you never stop. I'm tired of it.
ratih_ranger.bite_back: I patrolled a forest alone for fifteen years. I can look after myself and you.
ratih_ranger.hurt: Okay, that one hurt. I'll walk ahead for a while.
ratih_ranger.laugh_off: Poachers have shouted worse at me from across a river. Let's keep going.
ratih_ranger.confide: {name}, I promised my sister I'd visit her and her boy that summer, and I kept putting it off for one more patrol. Then there was no summer.
ratih_ranger.listen: I hear you, {name}. Take your time, I'm good at silence.
ratih_ranger.look_out: Walk in my steps in there, {name}. I'll find the wrong thing first.
ratih_ranger.accept: Fine, {name}, I'll do it your way.
ratih_ranger.deflect: It's nothing, don't thank me, {name}. Check on the others.
ratih_ranger.check_in: Show me the wound, {name}, quietly. I'll look properly.
ratih_ranger.blame: Somebody walked in without looking, and everything heard us.
ratih_ranger.thank: I was going, and you brought me back. I won't say thank you twice, so listen.
ratih_ranger.brush_off: Don't thank me, please. Sit still for a minute.
ratih_ranger.worry: Quiet, {name}, and still. Let me check you before you move.
ratih_ranger.handed_down: Your gear's with me now. I'll keep it safe for you.
ratih_ranger.hand_fine: It's yours, I travel light. I've got the bow.
ratih_ranger.hand_sulk: If somebody had asked me first, it would have been yes.
ratih_ranger.turn_friendly: I don't mind walking with you, {name}. That's a lot, from me.
ratih_ranger.turn_friends: I'd stand in a line with you, {name}, rostered and briefed. I've never wanted that before.
ratih_ranger.turn_grating: We don't walk well together. I'll take point, and you can follow.
ratih_ranger.turn_rivals: I'll still tell you when I see something wrong. That's the job, nothing else.
ratih_ranger.make_up: This is a waste of energy, {name}. Let's stop it.
ratih_ranger.defend: No, I saw everything, and that's wrong. Leave {name} be.
ratih_ranger.friend_left: The salt's quieter without {name}, and I didn't think it could be.
ratih_ranger.friend_back: I kept watch for you, {name}, and you came back.
ratih_ranger.common_wild: Fifteen years in a Sumatran forest, reading the land for the one wrong thing. People who've worked in the wild listen for what isn't there.

reka_necromancer.meet: I'm Réka, a necromancer, and that's my crow. Don't stare at it, it's shy, and it was shy before it died too.
reka_necromancer.meet_neighbour: The Black Strand, na, of course! I've seen you on the beach. I'm Réka, with the crow, and the crow's seen you too.
reka_necromancer.ask_home: And where are you from? I'm curious what cartoons you watched as a child.
reka_necromancer.ask_work: Your job, before all this? I'll guess first, and I'm usually wrong in funny ways.
reka_necromancer.answer_home: Pécs, in Hungary, but I lived in Budapest, in a studio above a bakery.
reka_necromancer.answer_work: Stop-motion films, twelve years, moving puppets a millimetre at a time and taking a picture. One of them won a prize at Annecy.
reka_necromancer.chat_food: Fresh bread from the bakery downstairs at six in the morning, na, still warm. I woke up hungry for twelve years.
reka_necromancer.chat_sleep: My crow sleeps worse than me, and I sleep badly. We keep each other up, mostly out of spite.
reka_necromancer.chat_missing: My cat Kocka, who hated every puppet I ever made. She'd knock them off the table one by one.
reka_necromancer.chat_here: Necromancy's exactly like stop-motion, if you ask me. Weight, timing and follow-through, every time.
reka_necromancer.tease_quiet: You're so still, {name}, I could animate you. Don't worry, I won't, yet.
reka_necromancer.tease_talker: You'd be a terrible puppet, {name}, you'd never hold a pose.
reka_necromancer.tease_careful: A millimetre at a time, {name}, that's how you move. You'd make a lovely stop-motion character.
reka_necromancer.tease_bold: You move like a puppet with the strings cut, {name}. Very dramatic, very short-lived.
reka_necromancer.tease_any: My crow likes you, {name}, and it doesn't like anybody, so I'm suspicious.
reka_necromancer.tease_back: Ha, jó, {name}, that was a good one. My crow laughed too.
reka_necromancer.bristle: Please don't, {name}. Leave that one in its grave.
reka_necromancer.apologise: That was nastier than I meant, and I'm sorry. My jokes go wrong sometimes.
reka_necromancer.double_down: That one stays, it was a good line.
reka_necromancer.needle_quiet: You never move until it's too late. Even my puppets had more timing.
reka_necromancer.needle_talker: My crow's started hiding from your talking. That takes effort.
reka_necromancer.needle_careful: You take forever, na, and the scene's over before you move.
reka_necromancer.needle_bold: You flail about like bad animation. Weight, timing, follow-through, please.
reka_necromancer.needle_any: You call what I do evil, and you've never once watched it properly.
reka_necromancer.bite_back: I've made dead things move beautifully for years. Don't lecture me about control.
reka_necromancer.hurt: Ah, that one landed, I'll admit it. I'll go and sulk with my crow.
reka_necromancer.laugh_off: Ha, festival critics were far nastier, na, and my film still won. Come on, then.
reka_necromancer.confide: {name}, my father ran a little puppet theatre, and I grew up backstage watching him bring wooden things to life. I started making films because it was the closest thing to what he did.
reka_necromancer.listen: My crow and I are both listening, {name}. Neither of us will tell anyone.
reka_necromancer.look_out: Stay where my crow can see you in there, {name}. It'll tell me if you're in trouble.
reka_necromancer.accept: Jó, {name}, your way. I'll follow the script.
reka_necromancer.deflect: Na, it's a scratch, {name}. My crow's had worse, and it's dead.
reka_necromancer.check_in: Hold still, {name}, and show me where. Small adjustments are my speciality.
reka_necromancer.blame: Somebody moved without timing in there, and the whole scene fell apart.
reka_necromancer.thank: I was nearly one of my own puppets there. Köszönöm, thank you.
reka_necromancer.brush_off: Na, it's nothing, just a small adjustment. Sit still for me.
reka_necromancer.worry: Na, {name}, that was far too dramatic. Sit down, I'm checking you over.
reka_necromancer.handed_down: Na, so now I'm in your gear. It'll stay in better shape than my puppets.
reka_necromancer.hand_fine: Take it, jó, it suits you. I've got my mannequin.
reka_necromancer.hand_sulk: So nobody asked me. My crow's offended on my behalf.
reka_necromancer.turn_friendly: My crow's decided you're all right, {name}, and so have I.
reka_necromancer.turn_friends: You can help with my moving picture, {name}. Nobody else gets to touch the frames.
reka_necromancer.turn_grating: It's not good between us, na. Fine, my crow doesn't like you either.
reka_necromancer.turn_rivals: I'll still raise what we need, it's my craft. Don't expect a cartoon.
reka_necromancer.make_up: This is silly, {name}, na. Let's start the scene again.
reka_necromancer.defend: That's nonsense, and I saw it all. Back off from {name}.
reka_necromancer.friend_left: My crow keeps looking for {name}, who's gone home for a while.
reka_necromancer.friend_back: Look who's back, {name}! My crow's learned a new hop, come and see.
reka_necromancer.common_craft: Twelve years moving puppets a millimetre at a time. Anybody who makes things by hand knows the patience is the whole art.
reka_necromancer.common_animals: My crow, and before it my cat Kocka, who hated every puppet I ever made. Animals are the best critics.

rhys_ranger.meet: I'm Rhys, and this is Tegan. Keep your voice down near the trees, would you, she hunts better when nobody's chattering.
rhys_ranger.meet_neighbour: Stonetalon West, is it? Tegan spotted you on the ridges before I did, and my name's Rhys, by the way.
rhys_ranger.ask_home: Which valley or town raised you, then? You walk like somebody who's climbed a few hills.
rhys_ranger.ask_work: And before all this, what were you at? Tegan's curious, and so am I.
rhys_ranger.answer_home: Brecon, in the Beacons, in Wales. One valley, and I never wanted to leave it.
rhys_ranger.answer_work: Falconer, at a centre outside town. Weddings in summer, school visits in winter, and a lot of people in hats.
rhys_ranger.chat_food: My mam's Welsh cakes, warm off the bakestone, with sugar on top. Tegan liked them too, which I wasn't meant to allow.
rhys_ranger.chat_sleep: Tegan wakes me at first light, every morning, without fail. She's never let me have a lie-in in seven years.
rhys_ranger.chat_missing: Rugby on a Saturday at the club, everybody singing in the bar after. Even when we lost, and we usually lost.
rhys_ranger.chat_here: Tegan found her first hare here inside a week. I thought, well, if she can, so can I.
rhys_ranger.tease_quiet: Tegan likes you, {name}, because you're quiet. She's very particular, mind.
rhys_ranger.tease_talker: You'd frighten every bird in the Beacons, {name}, talking like that. Tegan's forgiven you, just about.
rhys_ranger.tease_careful: You move like a falconer, {name}, slow and patient. Tegan approves, and so do I.
rhys_ranger.tease_bold: You'd fly a hawk in a thunderstorm, {name}, just to see what happened. Duw, please don't ever try it.
rhys_ranger.tease_any: Tegan's decided you're all right, {name}. I'm still making my mind up, mind.
rhys_ranger.tease_back: Ha, there's a good one, {name}. Tegan laughed, I swear she did.
rhys_ranger.take_it_kindly: Fair play, {name}, you're not wrong there.
rhys_ranger.bristle: Please, {name}, leave that alone. It's not for joking.
rhys_ranger.apologise: Sorry, that was unkind of me. I'm better with birds than people, as you've noticed.
rhys_ranger.double_down: I meant every word, gently put as it was. Tegan agrees with me, for what it's worth.
rhys_ranger.needle_quiet: There's something in the trees, and you've clocked it, and still you say nothing. Tegan can't read your mind, and nor can I.
rhys_ranger.needle_talker: Please, quieter, you're frightening her. Tegan's had enough noise for one day.
rhys_ranger.needle_careful: She's been waiting for you to move for ten minutes, and she's bored. So am I.
rhys_ranger.needle_bold: You charge through the woods like a bull, and every animal for a mile runs off.
rhys_ranger.needle_any: You treat Tegan like a pet, and she isn't one. She's a hunter, and she's cleverer than you.
rhys_ranger.bite_back: I've kept a hawk calm in front of two hundred people. I can manage you, mind.
rhys_ranger.hurt: Right, that stung a bit. Tegan and I'll be up on the ridge for a while.
rhys_ranger.laugh_off: Wedding guests were ruder after three glasses of wine, every Saturday. Tegan didn't mind, and nor do I.
rhys_ranger.confide: {name}, my dad died when I was eleven, and my mam took a job at the falconry centre so we'd manage. Everything good I've got came out of that.
rhys_ranger.listen: Tegan and I are both listening, {name}. Take your time, she's patient.
rhys_ranger.look_out: Stay where Tegan can see you in there, {name}. She'll warn me before anything gets close.
rhys_ranger.deflect: I'm grand, {name}, just a scratch from the brambles. Tegan's fussing enough for both of us.
rhys_ranger.check_in: Easy now, {name}, easy. Show me where, gently.
rhys_ranger.blame: Somebody went charging through in there, and every creature heard us coming.
rhys_ranger.thank: Diolch, that was close, and you're the reason I'm still here. Tegan thanks you as well.
rhys_ranger.brush_off: No bother at all. Sit still, and let Tegan keep watch.
rhys_ranger.worry: Duw, {name}, you went down hard. Sit still, Tegan's watching you too.
rhys_ranger.handed_down: That's your gear on me now, is it? It'll get the same care as my glove, and that's a lot of care.
rhys_ranger.hand_fine: You have it, it suits you. I've got my glove, and that's enough.
rhys_ranger.hand_sulk: Somebody might have asked first, mind. Tegan's sulking about it.
rhys_ranger.turn_friendly: Tegan's decided she trusts you, {name}, and I trust her. That settles it.
rhys_ranger.turn_friends: Tegan's never flown for anybody but me, {name}, and I'd trust her on your glove.
rhys_ranger.turn_grating: You and I rub each other wrong, I think, and Tegan doesn't like you. She's usually right.
rhys_ranger.turn_rivals: I'll still cover you from the ridge, since we're on the same side out here. Tegan won't, mind.
rhys_ranger.make_up: This is daft, {name}. Tegan's sick of us both, so let's stop.
rhys_ranger.defend: No, that's not true, and Tegan saw it too. Leave {name} be.
rhys_ranger.friend_left: Tegan keeps looking for {name}, and so do I. It's quiet on the ridge.
rhys_ranger.friend_back: Tegan spotted {name} coming before I did. Welcome back, tidy.
rhys_ranger.common_birds: Seven years with Tegan on my glove, and every day she chooses to come back. Anybody who's flown a bird knows that's the best moment there is.
rhys_ranger.common_wild: I grew up in the Beacons, outdoors every day after school. Anybody who's lived in the wild learns to listen before they look.
rhys_ranger.common_welsh: A Welsh voice out here, duw, that's done me good. Which part are you from, north or south?
rhys_ranger.common_animals: Tegan's been mine seven years, and she trusts some people more than others. Anyone who's kept an animal knows to take its word for it.

rosa_hunter.meet: I'm Rosa, and I hunt. I'll tell you what the animals out here are about to do before they do it, and you'll listen.
rosa_hunter.meet_neighbour: Your camp's off the Crossroads road, near mine in the Barrens. I'm Rosa, and I've watched you set up.
rosa_hunter.ask_home: Home, for you, is where exactly? Quickly, the light's going.
rosa_hunter.ask_work: Before this, what was your job? I'll know if you're lying.
rosa_hunter.answer_home: Madrid, Lavapiés, then eight years in Tanzania. My dad drove a bus and my mum did hair.
rosa_hunter.answer_work: Safari and research guide out of Arusha, eight years. Mostly I explained to tourists why the lion was looking at them like lunch.
rosa_hunter.chat_food: Tortilla de patatas, the proper way, with onion, and a cold beer at a bar in Lavapiés. That's the whole of Madrid.
rosa_hunter.chat_sleep: I sleep on the ground, lightly, with one ear open. Eight years in the bush does that.
rosa_hunter.chat_missing: Sitting absolutely still in the dark at a waterhole, waiting for something to come down to drink.
rosa_hunter.chat_here: The animals here think. A quilboar runs a plan and changes it when it sees you. I was bad at it for a whole year, and I hated it.
rosa_hunter.tease_quiet: Finally, {name}, somebody who knows how to sit still. You'd have been good in a hide.
rosa_hunter.tease_talker: Every animal for a mile knows exactly where you are, {name}. I'm almost impressed.
rosa_hunter.tease_careful: You'd wait three hours for the shot, {name}. Good, that's the only way.
rosa_hunter.tease_bold: You'd walk straight up to a lion to see if it was friendly, {name}. It isn't, it's hungry.
rosa_hunter.tease_any: You're a terrible tracker, {name}, and good company anyway. Don't tell anyone I said the second part.
rosa_hunter.tease_back: Ha, fine, {name}, that was good. You got me.
rosa_hunter.take_it_kindly: Fair enough, {name}, I'll take that. I'm bad at some things, and that's one.
rosa_hunter.bristle: Drop it, {name}, I'm not laughing at that one.
rosa_hunter.apologise: I went too far, and I'm sorry. I'm blunt, I'm not usually cruel.
rosa_hunter.double_down: No, I meant it, and I'd say it again. You needed telling.
rosa_hunter.needle_quiet: You saw the tracks and said nothing. That's how people get eaten.
rosa_hunter.needle_talker: You never stop, and everything out here can hear you coming.
rosa_hunter.needle_careful: You've waited so long the animal's walked off. Take the shot or don't.
rosa_hunter.needle_bold: You kill things for nothing, and you don't even notice you're doing it.
rosa_hunter.needle_any: You keep making the animals into symbols. They're animals, they're hungry.
rosa_hunter.bite_back: I've guided in the bush for eight years. Don't tell me how to read an animal.
rosa_hunter.hurt: Fine, that landed. Give me some time on my own at the edge of camp.
rosa_hunter.laugh_off: Tourists in Arusha were ruder than you before breakfast, most weeks, so keep walking.
rosa_hunter.confide: {name}, I've never stayed with anyone long, not once. I'd rather sit still in the dark at a waterhole than talk about why.
rosa_hunter.listen: Go on, {name}. Sitting still and listening is the one thing I'm good at.
rosa_hunter.look_out: Stay at my shoulder in there, {name}, and when I stop, you stop.
rosa_hunter.accept: All right, {name}, I'll let you fuss this once.
rosa_hunter.deflect: Don't fuss, {name}, it's a graze. Go and check the others.
rosa_hunter.check_in: Show me, {name}. Where did it get you, and how deep?
rosa_hunter.blame: Somebody spooked the whole pack in there, and we paid for it. I saw who.
rosa_hunter.thank: Thanks, I mean it, I was finished back there.
rosa_hunter.brush_off: Forget it, it's nothing. Sit still a minute.
rosa_hunter.worry: Stay down, {name}, don't move yet. That was bad.
rosa_hunter.handed_down: So it's your gear I'm carrying now. Ask and it's yours again, any time.
rosa_hunter.hand_fine: Have it, it's better on you. My binoculars are all I really need.
rosa_hunter.hand_sulk: Somebody might have asked me first, that's all I'm saying.
rosa_hunter.turn_friendly: You're all right, {name}. You can sit in my hide.
rosa_hunter.turn_friends: Some night I'll take you to sit by a waterhole in the dark, {name}. Nothing I own is worth more than that.
rosa_hunter.turn_grating: We clash, you and me, and that's fine. I'll keep to my side of camp.
rosa_hunter.turn_rivals: I'll still tell you what's coming, because I'm not stupid, and that's where it ends.
rosa_hunter.make_up: Fine, {name}, I was being stubborn. Let's stop it.
rosa_hunter.defend: That's rubbish, and you know it. Back off and let {name} be.
rosa_hunter.friend_left: Camp's quieter with {name} away. I thought I'd enjoy that more than I do.
rosa_hunter.friend_back: {name}, about time, the hide's been empty without you.
rosa_hunter.common_wild: Eight years in the bush in Tanzania, sitting still in the dark. People who've worked in wild places know they don't care about you, and that's the best part.
rosa_hunter.common_spanish: Somebody else who speaks Spanish, good, now I can be rude properly.

rui_cultist.meet: I'm Rui, and I'm sorry, I heal people, but please don't ask me how. I'll tell you what it does, and the rest I can't say.
rui_cultist.meet_neighbour: You're near the Lashings too, aren't you? I've watched you on the shore. I'm Rui, sorry, I should have said hello before.
rui_cultist.ask_home: Sorry, may I ask where you're from? You don't have to say.
rui_cultist.ask_work: Sorry, what kept you busy back home? I'm curious, you don't have to say.
rui_cultist.answer_home: Peniche, a fishing town on the Portuguese coast. My father fished, and he drowned when I was fourteen.
rui_cultist.answer_work: Sardine boats, twenty years, from sixteen. Nights out and mornings in, and mending nets in the evening.
rui_cultist.chat_food: Grilled sardines in summer, on bread, by the harbour. Sorry, I know that's simple, but it's the best food there is.
rui_cultist.chat_sleep: I sleep by the fire, always. In the dark it's louder, and I'd rather not hear it.
rui_cultist.chat_missing: The sea at dawn, coming back in with the nets full. Desculpa, I think about it every morning.
rui_cultist.chat_here: I took something in my first year when the alternative was dying. I'm sorry, I can't say more than that, and I've never pretended it was a good decision.
rui_cultist.tease_quiet: You're as quiet as me, {name}, which I didn't think was possible. Sorry, that's a compliment.
rui_cultist.tease_talker: You talk enough for both of us, {name}, which is kind of you, really. I never know what to say.
rui_cultist.tease_careful: You check the knots twice, {name}, the way a good fisherman does. Sorry, I notice these things.
rui_cultist.tease_bold: You'd go out in any weather, {name}, wouldn't you? The sea doesn't forgive that, sorry.
rui_cultist.tease_any: You're kind to me, {name}, and I keep apologising for it. Sorry, I'm doing it again.
rui_cultist.tease_back: Ha, sorry, that was good, {name}, and I didn't see it coming.
rui_cultist.take_it_kindly: Sorry, {name}, you've got me there. I won't argue.
rui_cultist.bristle: I'm sorry, {name}, I can't laugh about that one. Please leave it.
rui_cultist.apologise: I'm so sorry, that was unkind. It wasn't what I wanted to say at all.
rui_cultist.double_down: I'm sorry, but I meant it. I don't take it back.
rui_cultist.needle_quiet: Sorry, but you never say what's wrong, and then it's too late. Please, say something.
rui_cultist.needle_talker: Sorry, could you be quieter? It's louder when there's noise, and I can't think.
rui_cultist.needle_careful: I'm sorry, but people get hurt while you're still deciding. Please decide faster.
rui_cultist.needle_bold: You throw yourself at everything, and then it's me putting you back together. Sorry, but it wears me out.
rui_cultist.needle_any: You show off what you can do, and it frightens people. Sorry, but somebody should say it.
rui_cultist.bite_back: I've kept you all alive with something I'd give back if I could. Please don't say I don't care.
rui_cultist.hurt: Okay, sorry, I'm going to sit by the fire for a while.
rui_cultist.laugh_off: Sorry, the fish market men in Peniche said worse every morning, so it's okay.
rui_cultist.confide: {name}, I sent money home to my mother and sisters every week for twenty years. I think about the money more than I think about them, and I'm ashamed of that.
rui_cultist.listen: Sorry it's been hard, {name}. Take your time, please, I'm listening.
rui_cultist.look_out: Stay near me in there, {name}, please, so I can reach you. Sorry, I worry.
rui_cultist.accept: Okay, {name}, sorry, I'll do as you say.
rui_cultist.deflect: Sorry, I'm fine, {name}, please don't worry. The others need you more than I do.
rui_cultist.check_in: Sorry, {name}, are you hurt? Please let me see.
rui_cultist.blame: I'm sorry, but somebody rushed in, and that's why we fell.
rui_cultist.thank: Obrigado, and I'm so sorry I needed bringing back. Thank you, really.
rui_cultist.brush_off: Please, it's nothing, don't thank me. Sorry, just rest.
rui_cultist.worry: Sorry, {name}, please sit down. I was frightened for you.
rui_cultist.handed_down: Sorry, this was yours, wasn't it? I'll mend it if anything tears, I'm good with mending.
rui_cultist.hand_fine: Please keep it, I'm sorry it was ever mine. I've got the fire and my father's needle, and that's plenty.
rui_cultist.hand_sulk: Sorry, it's fine, only nobody asked first. Really, it's fine.
rui_cultist.turn_friendly: I'm glad you're here, {name}. Sorry, I don't say that often, but I mean it.
rui_cultist.turn_friends: You're the first person I've wanted to tell everything to, {name}. Sorry, I still can't, but I want to.
rui_cultist.turn_grating: I'm sorry, I don't think we get on. I'll sit on the other side of the fire.
rui_cultist.turn_rivals: Sorry, but I'll keep healing you, whatever happens between us. It doesn't let me choose.
rui_cultist.make_up: I'm sorry, {name}, for all of it. Can we start again, please?
rui_cultist.defend: Please, stop, that's not fair. Leave {name} alone, I'm sorry, but leave them.
rui_cultist.friend_left: It's very quiet without {name}, sorry, I keep looking up to say something.
rui_cultist.friend_back: I'm so glad, {name}, you came back. Sorry, I'm just glad.
rui_cultist.common_the_dark: Something offered to help me in the dark, and I said yes. You've done the same, I think, and you know what it costs. I'm sorry for both of us.
rui_cultist.common_boats: Twenty years on the sardine boats, nights out and mornings in. People who've worked on the water know the sea can take everything, and I'm sorry, but it does.
rui_cultist.common_portuguese: You speak Portuguese! Desculpa, I'm so glad, I've missed it.

ryan_warlock.meet: I'm Ryan Murphy, a warlock, which means I keep demons on contracts, and I keep the contracts to the letter. My price up front, so nobody's surprised later.
ryan_warlock.meet_neighbour: The Echo Isles, isn't it? I'm in the hut with the contracts on the wall. Ryan, and you've probably heard the rumours.
ryan_warlock.ask_home: And where are you from? I'll tell you mine, it's worse.
ryan_warlock.ask_work: How did you earn a living? Be honest, I was a broker, so nothing you say will shock me.
ryan_warlock.answer_home: Cork, raised by my grandmother on the rosary and very strong opinions, and then twenty years in Boston.
ryan_warlock.answer_work: Broker, twelve years, buyouts mostly. The kind that close factories on a Friday afternoon. I was very good at it.
ryan_warlock.chat_food: A pint of stout in a proper Cork pub, and a toasted sandwich at closing time. Boston never once got it right.
ryan_warlock.chat_sleep: Most nights I'm out cold in minutes, which is one of the more damning things about me. A better man would lie awake.
ryan_warlock.chat_missing: My grandmother's kitchen in Cork, with the radio on and her telling me exactly what was wrong with me.
ryan_warlock.chat_here: Demons are the same as clients, near enough. You find out what they want, you write it down, and you never break the deal.
ryan_warlock.tease_quiet: Silence is the best negotiating tactic there is, {name}, and you'd win every deal without trying.
ryan_warlock.tease_talker: You'd talk a buyer into anything, {name}, and then keep talking until they changed their mind.
ryan_warlock.tease_careful: You read the small print, {name}, every time. You're the client I always dreaded.
ryan_warlock.tease_bold: You'd sign anything without reading it, {name}. I've made a lot of money from people like you.
ryan_warlock.tease_any: You're the only honest person I know, {name}, apart from me, and I'm only honest because I've run out of alternatives.
ryan_warlock.tease_back: Ha, fair play, {name}, that one's going in my file of deserved insults.
ryan_warlock.take_it_kindly: Accurate, {name}, and I'll not argue with accurate.
ryan_warlock.bristle: Leave that, {name}. I'll take most things, not that.
ryan_warlock.apologise: That was a cheap shot, and I'm sorry. I'm trying to stop taking those.
ryan_warlock.double_down: Every word of it holds, I'm afraid. I'm honest now, it's the only trick I've got left.
ryan_warlock.needle_quiet: You've got an opinion and you're keeping it to yourself, which is a negotiating tactic, and I don't like it.
ryan_warlock.needle_talker: You talk like a salesman who hasn't closed. Please, close the deal or stop.
ryan_warlock.needle_careful: You've read the terms three times. Sign it or walk away.
ryan_warlock.needle_bold: You sign everything without reading it, and somebody else always pays. I know, I used to be that somebody's broker.
ryan_warlock.needle_any: You think you're better than you are. I know the look, I wore it for twenty years.
ryan_warlock.bite_back: I've been honest with you since the day we met, which is more than I managed for forty years. Don't call me a liar.
ryan_warlock.hurt: Ah, that went in. I'll go and read my contracts for a while.
ryan_warlock.laugh_off: Men who'd just lost their factories said worse to my face. You'll need to aim higher.
ryan_warlock.confide: {name}, my grandmother raised me in Cork on the rosary and very strong opinions. I'm glad she didn't see what I turned into.
ryan_warlock.listen: I won't sell that, {name}, not for any price. It stays with me.
ryan_warlock.look_out: Keep to my back in there, {name}. The demons have a contract with me, not with you.
ryan_warlock.deflect: I'm grand, {name}, it's a scratch. Look after the ones who deserve it.
ryan_warlock.check_in: Where's the damage, {name}? Itemise it for me.
ryan_warlock.blame: Somebody signed us up for that without reading the terms. I know who.
ryan_warlock.thank: I was out, and you brought me back. That's a debt, and I pay my debts on time.
ryan_warlock.brush_off: It's nothing, call it a down payment. Now sit still a minute.
ryan_warlock.worry: Jesus, {name}, sit down. I didn't care for that at all, and I don't care for much.
ryan_warlock.handed_down: Your gear's mine for now, it seems. It goes back in the same condition, and that's in writing.
ryan_warlock.hand_fine: Fair trade, have it. I've got my contracts.
ryan_warlock.hand_sulk: Nobody asked my permission. In my old job, that'd be a lawsuit.
ryan_warlock.turn_friendly: I trust you, {name}, and I don't trust myself, so that's saying something.
ryan_warlock.turn_friends: I'd sign anything you put in front of me, {name}, without reading it. That's the most dangerous thing I've ever said.
ryan_warlock.turn_grating: I'd rather say it than pretend, so here it is, we're a bad fit. I've done enough pretending.
ryan_warlock.turn_rivals: I'll honour the deal and fight beside you. That's all the deal says.
ryan_warlock.make_up: I got it wrong, {name}, and I'm saying so, which I've only recently learned to do. Let's start again.
ryan_warlock.defend: That's not true, and I'd know a lie. Leave {name} alone.
ryan_warlock.friend_left: With {name} away I've nobody to be honest with, and I find that unnerving.
ryan_warlock.friend_back: Ah, {name}, you're back. Good, I was starting to lie to myself again.
ryan_warlock.common_irish: Another Irish voice, thank God, and I'll want to know which county. Cork, me, and I'll not hear a word against it.
ryan_warlock.common_parent: I've a son, Conor, twenty-two now. His mother divorced me when he was eleven, and she was right to.

santiago_runemaster.meet: Qué más, parce, I'm Santiago, a runemaster. Every rune's a line you can't take back, same as a tattoo, just louder.
santiago_runemaster.meet_neighbour: The Ashen Reach, parce! I've seen you near the works. I'm Santiago, the one cutting runes into everything.
santiago_runemaster.ask_home: Which city made you, parce? Tell me, I like a good origin story.
santiago_runemaster.ask_work: Before all this, parce, what paid the bills? You've got the hands of somebody who made things.
santiago_runemaster.answer_home: Medellín, parce, born and raised. My mother sold arepas from a cart, and I drew on everything, and then on people.
santiago_runemaster.answer_work: Tattoo artist, nine years, in a shop in Laureles with my cousin. The waiting list ran for months.
santiago_runemaster.chat_food: Bandeja paisa, parce, the whole plate, beans and rice and chicharrón and an egg on top. You need a nap after.
santiago_runemaster.chat_sleep: After a good day's line work I'm out like a light. A bad line keeps me up all night.
santiago_runemaster.chat_missing: Reggaeton in the shop, loud, and a first-timer in the chair, nervous, leaving brave. That's the best feeling.
santiago_runemaster.chat_here: The first rune I cut glowed, parce, and I spent a week working out what I'd done right. Then I couldn't stop.
santiago_runemaster.tease_quiet: You'd be a perfect client, {name}, you'd sit still for six hours and never complain.
santiago_runemaster.tease_talker: You'd talk through the whole session, {name}, and I'd let you. It keeps the nerves away.
santiago_runemaster.tease_careful: You'd choose a design for a year before you let me near you, {name}. Bacano, that's how you get a good one.
santiago_runemaster.tease_bold: You'd let me tattoo your face on the first meeting, {name}. I'd say no, and I'd be tempted.
santiago_runemaster.tease_any: You're a work in progress, {name}, the way a good sleeve is. I like where it's going.
santiago_runemaster.tease_back: Ha, bacano, {name}! Clean line, that one.
santiago_runemaster.take_it_kindly: That's fair, parce, I'll take it. My mother says the same.
santiago_runemaster.bristle: Careful, parce, that's a line you can't take back.
santiago_runemaster.apologise: Ay, perdón, parce, that was ugly of me. I'm sorry, really.
santiago_runemaster.double_down: No, parce, I'm keeping it. Some lines you commit to.
santiago_runemaster.needle_quiet: How does it feel, parce? I can't fix the line if you won't tell me.
santiago_runemaster.needle_talker: Please, parce, quiet for a second. I need a steady hand.
santiago_runemaster.needle_careful: You've stared at it so long, parce. Commit to the line.
santiago_runemaster.needle_bold: Rushed lines are ugly, parce, and you rush every single one. I can't stand ugly lines.
santiago_runemaster.needle_any: Your work is sloppy, parce, and sloppy lines get people hurt here.
santiago_runemaster.bite_back: I've done three hundred clients' worth of designs without a bad line. Don't talk to me about care.
santiago_runemaster.hurt: Ay, that went in deep, parce. I'll go and draw for a while.
santiago_runemaster.laugh_off: Ha, my mother said worse about my tattoos every Sunday, parce, so come on.
santiago_runemaster.confide: {name}, I was putting my little brother through a good school in Bogotá. I never once told him how proud I was of him.
santiago_runemaster.listen: I'm here, parce. Talk me through it, like a first-timer.
santiago_runemaster.look_out: Stay out of the sparks in there, {name}. When I cut, things get loud.
santiago_runemaster.deflect: It's nothing, parce, a little scratch. My own needle's done worse to me.
santiago_runemaster.check_in: Talk me through it, {name}, slowly. Which part's hurting?
santiago_runemaster.blame: Somebody rushed the line in there, parce, and now it's ruined.
santiago_runemaster.thank: Parce, I was out and now I'm not! Free tattoo, any design, whenever you want.
santiago_runemaster.brush_off: Pues, it's nothing, parce. Breathe, you're brave.
santiago_runemaster.worry: Ay, parce, {name}, that scared me. Breathe slowly, like a first-timer.
santiago_runemaster.handed_down: So this gear of yours is mine for now, parce. I'll treat it like my best machine.
santiago_runemaster.hand_fine: Take it, parce, it looks bacano on you. I've got my grip.
santiago_runemaster.hand_sulk: Nobody even checked with me, parce. That's not cool.
santiago_runemaster.turn_friendly: You're my client for life now, {name}, parce. Front of the waiting list.
santiago_runemaster.turn_friends: You can design a rune with me any time, {name}, and I'll lend you the good notebook.
santiago_runemaster.turn_grating: This isn't working between us, parce. That's okay, not every design works.
santiago_runemaster.turn_rivals: I'll still cut your runes, because I'm a professional. Don't ask for a tattoo.
santiago_runemaster.make_up: Enough, {name}, parce. Let's start the design again.
santiago_runemaster.defend: Oye, cut it out, parce, that's not fair. Leave {name} alone.
santiago_runemaster.friend_left: The shop feels empty with {name} away, parce, nobody to show my sketches.
santiago_runemaster.friend_back: Qué más, {name}, you're back! I've got a new design to show you.
santiago_runemaster.common_craft: Nine years of line work, and every line's one you can't take back. Anybody who makes things by hand knows the patience is the craft.
santiago_runemaster.common_spanish: Somebody here speaks Spanish, parce! Qué más, finally I can talk properly.

saoirse_starcaller.meet: I'm Saoirse, and I stand in front of things for a living now. Get behind me, keep your head up, and if you get notions this ball's coming at you.
saoirse_starcaller.meet_neighbour: The Sepulcher, is it? We're near enough neighbours, so, and I've clocked you about the place. Saoirse, and I'm the loud one.
saoirse_starcaller.ask_home: Go on, which county are you from? Or country, I suppose, out here.
saoirse_starcaller.ask_work: Were you any good at your job, back home? Tell me what it was first.
saoirse_starcaller.answer_home: Kilkenny, home of hurling, whatever Cork says. My da farmed and my mam was a nurse, and I had a hurl in my hand at five.
saoirse_starcaller.answer_work: Camogie for the county till my knee went at twenty-six, then coaching under-sixteen girls. I loved the coaching more, if you can believe that.
saoirse_starcaller.chat_food: A spice bag from the chipper after training, eaten in the car with the heater on. Don't knock it till you've tried it.
saoirse_starcaller.chat_sleep: Out the minute my head's down, every night, snoring like a tractor, they tell me. Training does that.
saoirse_starcaller.chat_missing: The Nowlan Park crowd on a county final day, with the whole town out. You've never heard noise like it.
saoirse_starcaller.chat_here: I landed somewhere that wanted a body stood in front, and that's the one thing I was ever any good at. It's been easy for me here, and I'm a bit ashamed of how easy.
saoirse_starcaller.tease_quiet: Would it kill you to shout once in a while, {name}? I'd have you roaring on the sideline inside a week.
saoirse_starcaller.tease_talker: You'd talk a referee out of a red card, {name}, and then talk yourself back into one.
saoirse_starcaller.tease_careful: You'd stop to tie your laces in the middle of a match, {name}. Run, for God's sake, run!
saoirse_starcaller.tease_bold: You'd go for a ball with three of them on you, {name}, and I'd pick you first for it.
saoirse_starcaller.tease_any: If you were on my team, {name}, I'd have you running laps till you were sick, and you'd thank me.
saoirse_starcaller.tease_back: Ha, that's a cracker, {name}! I'll have to watch you.
saoirse_starcaller.take_it_kindly: Grand, {name}, guilty as charged. I'll not argue.
saoirse_starcaller.bristle: Mind yourself now, {name}, that one's a step too far.
saoirse_starcaller.apologise: Ah, I went in too hard there, and I'm sorry. I do that, I'm working on it.
saoirse_starcaller.double_down: Every bit of that was meant, so. Better from me than from somebody who doesn't care.
saoirse_starcaller.needle_quiet: Open your mouth and shout when you see something! A silent team's a beaten team.
saoirse_starcaller.needle_talker: Less chat, more running, please. You'd talk the legs off a chair.
saoirse_starcaller.needle_careful: You're thinking about it while it's hitting you. Move first and think on the way!
saoirse_starcaller.needle_bold: You're playing for yourself out there, not the team. I've dropped girls for less.
saoirse_starcaller.needle_any: You're getting above yourself, and you know what happens to people who do that. This ball doesn't miss.
saoirse_starcaller.bite_back: I've taken every hit that came at this party for months, so watch what you say about my effort.
saoirse_starcaller.hurt: Right, that one hit. I'll go and run it off.
saoirse_starcaller.laugh_off: My under-sixteens gave me worse every Tuesday, and they were funnier. Try harder, so.
saoirse_starcaller.confide: {name}, my parents went within a year of each other when I was twenty-nine, and I didn't fall apart, and I've felt guilty about that for years.
saoirse_starcaller.listen: Sit down there, {name}, and tell me all of it. I'm not going anywhere.
saoirse_starcaller.look_out: Keep in my shadow, {name}, and stay there, that's what I'm for.
saoirse_starcaller.deflect: Ah, I'm grand, {name}, it's only a knock. I've had worse in a club match.
saoirse_starcaller.check_in: Up you come, {name}, slowly. Where'd it get you?
saoirse_starcaller.blame: Somebody broke the line in there, and I couldn't cover the gap.
saoirse_starcaller.thank: Fair play, you got me up off the ground. Thanks a million.
saoirse_starcaller.brush_off: Not a bother, that's what a team's for. Get your breath back.
saoirse_starcaller.worry: God almighty, {name}, stay down a minute. You frightened the life out of me.
saoirse_starcaller.handed_down: Right, so I'm in your gear now. I'll mind it like my own hurl.
saoirse_starcaller.hand_fine: Sure take it, it fits you better. I've my ball and my stick and that'll do me.
saoirse_starcaller.hand_sulk: A bit of warning would've been nice, that's all.
saoirse_starcaller.turn_friendly: You'd make my team, {name}, and I'd put you in the starting fifteen.
saoirse_starcaller.turn_friends: Captain's armband's yours if I ever get hurt, {name}. That's me trusting you completely.
saoirse_starcaller.turn_grating: Look, we're not gelling, and there's no use pretending we are.
saoirse_starcaller.turn_rivals: I'll still take the hits for you, because I take them for everybody. Don't read anything into it.
saoirse_starcaller.make_up: Ah, would you stop, {name}, this is daft. Shake my hand and we'll start again.
saoirse_starcaller.defend: Back off now, that's out of order. {name} did nothing to deserve that.
saoirse_starcaller.friend_left: With {name} off home, there's nobody to throw the ball at. I've been aiming at trees.
saoirse_starcaller.friend_back: Look who's back, it's {name}! I've been aiming at trees for weeks.
saoirse_starcaller.common_sport: Anybody who's played proper sport knows the knee goes, or the back goes, and then you coach. And then you find out you love the coaching more.
saoirse_starcaller.common_irish: An Irish accent out here, that's put a grin on me. Which county, and please don't say Tipperary.
saoirse_starcaller.common_teacher: There's a look you get from yard duty in the rain, and you have it. You've taught, haven't you?

sebastian_bloodmage.meet: I'm Sebastián, and you look hungry, my friend. Sit, eat something, and then we can talk about who we're fighting today.
sebastian_bloodmage.meet_neighbour: Tirisfal neighbours, che, and you've never once come to my fire! I'm Sebastián, and that changes tonight.
sebastian_bloodmage.ask_home: Tell me, what did your family eat on a Sunday? That tells me where you're from better than a map.
sebastian_bloodmage.ask_work: Che, before you were swinging that thing, how did you earn your bread?
sebastian_bloodmage.answer_home: Palermo, in Buenos Aires. Twenty of us round the table every Sunday, and my grandmother at the head of it.
sebastian_bloodmage.answer_work: The grill at our steakhouse, twelve years, forty tables and a wood fire. My grandmother Nélida gave me the tongs at twenty-two.
sebastian_bloodmage.chat_food: Asado, my friend, slow over wood, with chimichurri and bread for the juices. It takes all afternoon, and it should.
sebastian_bloodmage.chat_sleep: I sleep wherever the fire is warm, and I'm up first to light it again. Somebody has to.
sebastian_bloodmage.chat_missing: River at the Monumental on a Sunday, with my father and my brothers, losing our voices.
sebastian_bloodmage.chat_here: The Forsaken don't eat much, che, and that was the hardest thing about this place. I keep cooking for them anyway.
sebastian_bloodmage.tease_quiet: You eat as little as you say, {name}. Have another plate, and say something.
sebastian_bloodmage.tease_talker: You talk more than my uncles at a christening, {name}, and they never stopped.
sebastian_bloodmage.tease_careful: You cut your meat into perfect little squares, {name}, like a surgeon. My grandmother would have loved you.
sebastian_bloodmage.tease_bold: You'd put your hand straight on the grill to see if it was hot, {name}. It's hot, che.
sebastian_bloodmage.tease_any: Eat something, {name}, you're getting thin, and I take that personally.
sebastian_bloodmage.tease_back: Ha, che, {name}, very funny! Seconds for you, for that one.
sebastian_bloodmage.take_it_kindly: Fair, fair, {name}, I can't argue with the truth. Have some bread.
sebastian_bloodmage.bristle: Ah, no, {name}, not that. That one isn't funny to me.
sebastian_bloodmage.apologise: Perdón, my friend, that was a stupid thing to say. Eat something, and forgive me.
sebastian_bloodmage.double_down: No, che, I'm sticking with it. I say what I think, and then I feed you.
sebastian_bloodmage.needle_quiet: You sit at my fire and never say if you like the food. Say something, che, anything.
sebastian_bloodmage.needle_talker: Che, your food's gone cold while you talked. Eat first, then the speech.
sebastian_bloodmage.needle_careful: You've been looking at that meat for ten minutes, che. It's cooked, I promise you, eat it.
sebastian_bloodmage.needle_bold: You rush in, and somebody comes back bleeding, and then they can't eat. That makes me angry, che.
sebastian_bloodmage.needle_any: You leave food on the plate, every time. Where I'm from, that's an insult to the cook.
sebastian_bloodmage.bite_back: I've fed this whole party every night out of my own pack, che. Think about that before you say another word.
sebastian_bloodmage.hurt: Okay, che, that one hurt. I'll be at the fire for a while.
sebastian_bloodmage.laugh_off: Ha, my grandmother said worse about my chimichurri every Sunday, che. Pass me the bread.
sebastian_bloodmage.confide: {name}, I've cooked for whoever turns up for three years, and I still lay the table for twenty in my head.
sebastian_bloodmage.listen: Here, {name}, take the good chair by the fire. Tell me everything, slowly.
sebastian_bloodmage.look_out: Stay at my elbow out there, {name}, so I can feed you afterwards.
sebastian_bloodmage.accept: Okay, okay, {name}, you win. But you eat after.
sebastian_bloodmage.deflect: Pfft, I'm fine, che, a little blood never hurt anybody, and I like blood.
sebastian_bloodmage.check_in: Che, {name}, let me see. Sit, sit, where did they hit you?
sebastian_bloodmage.blame: Somebody ran off ahead in there and left us open. Next time, wait, che.
sebastian_bloodmage.thank: Gracias, my friend, I owe you a whole asado for that one.
sebastian_bloodmage.brush_off: Bah, it was nothing, che. Sit and eat something.
sebastian_bloodmage.worry: Che, {name}, sit, sit, you went down like a sack of potatoes. I'm bringing you food.
sebastian_bloodmage.handed_down: So your gear comes to my fire now. I'll keep it clean of grease, I promise.
sebastian_bloodmage.hand_fine: Take it, take it, my friend, it's better on you. I've got my tongs.
sebastian_bloodmage.hand_sulk: Che, a little word first would have been nice. That's all I'm saying.
sebastian_bloodmage.turn_friendly: You've got a seat at my table now, {name}, every night, no arguments.
sebastian_bloodmage.turn_friends: Every Sunday from now on, {name}, you're sitting next to me.
sebastian_bloodmage.turn_grating: We're not sitting easy together, che. You can still eat my food, but sit on the other side.
sebastian_bloodmage.turn_rivals: You'll still get fed, because nobody leaves my fire hungry, not even you.
sebastian_bloodmage.make_up: Enough, {name}, come and eat with me. Nobody stays angry with a full plate.
sebastian_bloodmage.defend: Che, stop that, it isn't true, and {name} doesn't deserve it.
sebastian_bloodmage.friend_left: I keep setting a plate out for {name}, and then I remember.
sebastian_bloodmage.friend_back: Sit, sit, {name}, I cooked too much again, and now I know why.
sebastian_bloodmage.common_kitchen: Anybody who's worked a kitchen knows the heat and the shouting and the family meal after. That's the best hour of the whole day.
sebastian_bloodmage.common_hosts: You count the plates before you count yourself, che, the same as me. People who host don't sit down until everybody's eaten.
sebastian_bloodmage.common_spanish: Castellano, che, at last somebody I can argue about football with.
sebastian_bloodmage.common_blood: You use blood too, che, and you don't flinch. Everybody else looks at me like I've grown horns.

silas_rogue.meet: Name's Silas, and I notice things for a living. What did I do before? Port work, and ask me again tomorrow, it'll be different port work.
silas_rogue.meet_neighbour: Ratchet's yours too, then. I'm over the net-maker's on the middle pier, Silas, and I've already noticed which room's yours.
silas_rogue.ask_home: Go on then, where'd you wash up from? I'll tell you mine, and one of us might even be honest.
silas_rogue.ask_work: Your hands say one job and your walk says another, so which was it?
silas_rogue.answer_home: Antwerp, near the docks. English dad who was mostly at sea, Flemish mum on a cleaner's wage.
silas_rogue.answer_work: Port work, and today's version is crane driver. The true one's duller, security guard, five years watching cameras.
silas_rogue.chat_food: Frites from a stand by the Groenplaats, with mayonnaise, and a Bolleke after. Antwerp's whole cuisine, more or less.
silas_rogue.chat_sleep: Five years of night shifts, and I'd still sleep till noon if you let me. I'm better at night anyway.
silas_rogue.chat_missing: The port at three in the morning, all lit up, cranes going, nobody about. I liked it more than I let on.
silas_rogue.chat_here: I came here thinking there'd be no rules, and it turned out the rules are sharper. Took me four months to get it, and it rearranged me a bit.
silas_rogue.tease_quiet: I can read most people in a minute, {name}, and you've kept me guessing for weeks. It's very annoying.
silas_rogue.tease_talker: You give away everything you're thinking, {name}, and you'd never last a day on the docks.
silas_rogue.tease_careful: You check the exits before you sit down, {name}. Takes one to know one.
silas_rogue.tease_bold: You walk into a room like nobody's ever robbed you, {name}. Give it time.
silas_rogue.tease_any: I've got you figured out, {name}, mostly, about sixty percent. The other forty bothers me.
silas_rogue.tease_back: Ha, nice, {name}, you read me better than I thought.
silas_rogue.take_it_kindly: Caught fair and square, {name}, and I'm not even going to wriggle.
silas_rogue.bristle: Easy, {name}, that's one subject I don't joke about.
silas_rogue.apologise: That was cheap of me, sorry. I hide behind jokes, and sometimes they've got teeth.
silas_rogue.double_down: I'd say it again, and that's me committing to something, so enjoy it.
silas_rogue.needle_quiet: You notice as much as I do, and you never pass it on. That's how docks get robbed.
silas_rogue.needle_talker: You'd tell a stranger your bank details if they smiled. Keep something back, would you?
silas_rogue.needle_careful: You're checking it a fourth time. It's fine, it was fine the first time.
silas_rogue.needle_bold: You walk in like you own the place, and anybody watching knows exactly where to stick the knife.
silas_rogue.needle_any: You believe every story anybody tells you. Out here that gets you robbed or worse.
silas_rogue.bite_back: I've spotted every ambush before it landed, and you've walked away from all of them, which you'd do well to remember.
silas_rogue.hurt: Right, that one found a gap. I'll be on the pier for a bit.
silas_rogue.laugh_off: Captains have called me worse while I was searching their holds. You'll have to dig deeper.
silas_rogue.confide: {name}, the docks had an arrangement where everybody took a little. I never joined in and I never said a word, and the second part's the one that bothers me.
silas_rogue.listen: No jokes, {name}, I promise. Go on, I'm listening properly for once.
silas_rogue.look_out: Watch the shadows in there, {name}, and watch me watching them.
silas_rogue.accept: Fine, you win, {name}. I'll let somebody look after me for once.
silas_rogue.deflect: Barely touched me, {name}, it looks worse than it is.
silas_rogue.check_in: Let's have a look, {name}. Where'd they get you, and don't play it down.
silas_rogue.blame: Somebody didn't watch their corner in there, and I'm not naming names, but I'm looking at them.
silas_rogue.thank: That's one I owe you, and I don't forget who I owe. Thanks.
silas_rogue.brush_off: Don't mention it, really. I'd rather nobody saw me being decent.
silas_rogue.worry: That was ugly, {name}, sit down. I counted the seconds you were down, and there were too many.
silas_rogue.handed_down: So I'm walking around in your gear. Don't worry, I won't sell it.
silas_rogue.hand_fine: Have it, I travel light, and it's easier leaving in a hurry.
silas_rogue.hand_sulk: Funny how nobody checked with me first. I did notice, for the record.
silas_rogue.turn_friendly: I've stopped trying to read you, {name}, and started just enjoying the company.
silas_rogue.turn_friends: I'd tell you the true version of anything, {name}, first time of asking.
silas_rogue.turn_grating: I can't make us fit, and I'm usually better at hiding it.
silas_rogue.turn_rivals: I'll still watch your back, because a dead teammate's bad for business, and it's nothing personal.
silas_rogue.make_up: Call it even, {name}? I was no better than you in all this.
silas_rogue.defend: I was watching, and that's not how it went. Lay off {name}.
silas_rogue.friend_left: With {name} off home, I've nobody to talk straight to. I'm out of practice already.
silas_rogue.friend_back: There you are, {name}, and I'd noticed you were gone, which surprised me.
silas_rogue.common_docks: You watch a crate the way only dock people do. The port teaches you who's lying faster than anywhere.

skye_pyromancer.meet: G'day, I'm Skye, pyromancer. Stand upwind, don't touch anything glowing, and if I say move, move.
skye_pyromancer.meet_neighbour: Southern Needles, yeah? I'm down on the Drowning Floor, so we're neighbours, near enough. Skye, and if you smell smoke, that's me.
skye_pyromancer.ask_home: So what's your home town, mate? I want the town, not the country.
skye_pyromancer.ask_work: What'd you do for work, before this? You stand like somebody who's done night shifts.
skye_pyromancer.answer_home: Ballarat, in Victoria. Dad was a postie and Mum taught primary, and I was outside all day.
skye_pyromancer.answer_work: Vet nurse to pay the bills, and eleven seasons with a CFA brigade. Tanker, pager, and a shed with a kettle.
skye_pyromancer.chat_food: A snag in bread from the sausage sizzle after a burn, with onions, and a cold beer. Best meal there is.
skye_pyromancer.chat_sleep: I sleep with one ear open for the pager, still. It's been two and a half years, and nothing's ever going to beep.
skye_pyromancer.chat_missing: The shed on a quiet night, kettle on, the crew taking the mick out of each other. Best people I ever knew.
skye_pyromancer.chat_here: I found a fire in my first week here and put it out, and that sorted my head out for a year.
skye_pyromancer.tease_quiet: You'd be the one in the truck who never says anything and then saves everybody, {name}. Every crew's got one.
skye_pyromancer.tease_talker: You'd talk the paint off a tanker, {name}, and then complain it needed doing.
skye_pyromancer.tease_careful: You'd do a full risk assessment before lighting a barbie, {name}. I respect it, but it's hilarious.
skye_pyromancer.tease_bold: You'd run into a burning shed for a laugh, {name}, and I'd have to drag you out by the collar.
skye_pyromancer.tease_any: You'd last about a week in my brigade, {name}, before somebody hid your boots.
skye_pyromancer.tease_back: Ha, fair cop, {name}, you've got me there.
skye_pyromancer.take_it_kindly: Yeah, nah, you're right, {name}. Can't argue with that.
